[Operational Exercise at Tuas Second Link]SCDF participated in an emergency response exercise at Tuas Second Link earlier today (23 Jul), together with , Malaysia's Department of Environment and other supporting agencies. This multi-agency exercise simulated an emergency response to hazardous chemical releases resulting from a multi-vehicle accident. Conducted as part of the bilateral co-operation under the Malaysia-Singapore Joint Committee on the Environment, this marks the 14th exercise since 2000. These biennial exercises strengthen both countries' emergency response capabilities and coordination in mitigating hazardous chemical incidents on the Tuas Second Link.Swipe to view the photos from todays exercise.

[Community heroes responding to a vehicle fire]On 21 June 2025 at about 8:55pm, Mr Muhammad Tashir Bin Mansor was resting at home after his duty shift as a firefighter with Changi Airport Groups Airport Emergency Services when he heard a fire alarm from a multi-storey carpark (MSCP) at 635A, Pasir Ris Drive 1. Looking out the window, Mr Tashir saw black smoke from the MSCP and immediately dashed out of his home to help.At the same time, Ms Nur Fatin Binte Raihan, Ms Nur Sakinah Binte Abdul Rahman and Ms Julia Sarah Binte Muhammad Hasan who were at a nearby void deck also saw the black smoke. Ms Julia promptly called 995 and the three ladies also made their way to the MSCP. Upon reaching the MSCP, Mr Tashir spotted a car on fire on the second floor. With the assistance of Ms Julia and Ms Sakinah, Mr Tashir used a nearby hosereel to contain the car fire, while Ms Fatin helped to alert other members of public to stay away.The speedy and courageous actions of the four individuals prevented the fire from spreading.On 8 July 2025, the four Community First Responders were presented with the SCDF Community First Responder Award. The award was presented by COL Ser Boon Hui, Commander, 2nd SCDF Division.You too can make a difference during an emergency by downloading the SCDF myResponder app and registering as a Community First Responder via the app. You can also learn essential lifesaving skills through SCDFs Responder Plus Programme at go.gov.sg/scdfrpp. Lets build ANationOfLifesavers together!CommunityFirstResponderCommunityLifesaversOurCFRsOurHeroesWhatsYourRoleFrom L to R Ms Nur Fatin Binte Raihan; Ms Nur Sakinah Binte Abdul Rahman; Ms Julia Sarah Binte Muhammad Hasan; COL Ser Boon Hui, Commander, 2nd SCDF Division; Mr Muhammad Tashir Bin Mansor

[Height Rescue Operation @ 250 North Bridge Road]Earlier today at about 11:20am, SCDF responded to a height rescue incident involving two workers who were stranded on a gondola between the 28th and 29th floor of a building at the abovementioned location.Upon arrival, firefighters immediately checked on the gondola's stability, as well as the condition of the workers on the gondola.Rescuers from the Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) also responded to the scene and set up the rescue equipment at level 30 and level 29. The gondola was then secured with safety lines, before a DART rescuer descended onto the gondola to rescue the two workers. The DART rescuer secured the two workers who were wearing body harnesses, and brought them into the building through the windows on level 29 and level 30.Both workers were assessed by an SCDF paramedic and conveyed to Raffles Hospital in a stable condition.

[32nd Rota Commander Course Commissioning Parade]Yesterday morning, 75 officer cadets from the 32nd Rota Commander Course (RCC) were commissioned as Senior Officers at a ceremonial parade held at the Civil Defence Academy. The cohort included 23 trainees from the Abu Dhabi Civil Defence Authority.The commissioning marks a key milestone after seven months of intensive training to prepare the officers for a wide range of fire, medical, rescue, and HazMat incidents.Guest of honour Mr Goh Pei Ming, Minister of State for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of Social and Family Development, highlighted SCDFs vital role as Singapores national emergency responder. He urged the new officers to uphold public trust through strong leadership, conviction, and compassion.Congratulations to the 32nd RCC! Wishing them the very best as they embark on their lifesaving journey. ANationofLifesavers

[Fire @ Block 194 Kim Keat Avenue]Earlier this morning at about 11:50am, SCDF responded to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon arrival, one of the bedrooms in a 12th-floor unit was on fire. Firefighters entered the smoke-filled unit and extinguished the fire with a water jet. As a result of the fire, the rest of the unit as well as the corridor area outside the unit sustained heat and smoke damage.Three persons had evacuated from the affected unit before SCDF's arrival. As a precautionary measure, about 60 persons from the block were evacuated by the Police.Two persons from the affected unit were assessed by SCDF for smoke inhalation. One of them was conveyed to KK Womens and Childrens Hospital while the other person declined to be sent to the hospital.Preliminary findings indicate that the cause of the fire is likely from an electrical origin in the affected bedroom.To prevent such fires, SCDF would like to remind the public:a) Do not overload electrical outlets with electrical appliances;b) Always switch off appliances when they are not in use;c) Check the condition of wires regularly. Frayed wires or cracked cords should be replaced or repaired immediately;d) Do not run wires under carpets or mats and keep wires away from hot surfaces;e) Use only appliances and electrical plugs bearing the Safety Mark. The categories of appliances can be found at Do not leave batteries or devices charging unattended for an extended period of time, or leave it charging overnight.

[Community Centre Staff Commended For Saving A Life]On 29 April, three staff members of Boon Lay Community Centre (CC) Ms Gayathiri d/o Selvam, Mr Mohammad Imraan s/o Noor Abdul Kadir Jailaini and Ms Lee May Kay Peggy were on duty when they were approached by a member of the public informing them that someone had collapsed at the CCs multi-purpose hall.Ms Gayathiri and Mr Imraan rushed to the scene and saw the patient lying unresponsive on the floor. Mr Imraan immediately called 995 while Ms Gayathiri ran back to her office to retrieve an Automated External Defibrillator (AED). She returned with Ms Lee, who prepared the AED for use while Ms Gayathiri began CPR.Soon, Ms Jeane Fong Jin Yi, Boon Lay Constituency Director, arrived and contacted the patients family member. Upon using the AED, the patient began showing signs of breathing. The team then continued several more cycles of CPR, as advised by the AED.As a result of the teams timely response and teamwork, they were able to successfully resuscitate the patient prior to SCDFs arrival. The patient survived and is alive today.On 22 May 2025, the four individuals were presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. The awards were presented by SAC Goh Boon Han, Commander, 4th SCDF Division.You too can make a difference during an emergency by downloading the SCDF myResponder app and registering as a Community First Responder via the app. You can also learn essential lifesaving skills through SCDFs Responders Plus Programme at go.gov.sg/scdfrpp. Lets build ANationOfLifesavers together!CommunityFirstResponderCommunityLifesaversOurCFRsOurHeroesWhatsYourRole

[SCDFs 2nd Generation Marine Rescue Vessel Commissioning Ceremony] SCDFs 2nd Generation Marine Rescue Vessel (MRV2G), the Blue Dolphin, was officially commissioned at a ceremony held at the Republic of Singapore Yacht Club earlier today (25 Jun). Mr Edwin Tong, Minister for Law and Second Minister for Home Affairs, graced the ceremony as the Guest of Honour. His wife, Mrs Tong, served as the Lady Patron for the symbolic christening and official induction of the Blue Dolphin into service. Operating from West Coast Marine Fire Station, the Blue Dolphin enhances SCDF's coverage and readiness in Singapore's waters. The MRV2G comes with some key enhancements: - Integrated Command Post to enhance command and control during major incidents- Advanced Navigational System for precise vessel handling - Launch and Recovery System for improved deployment of the Rigid Hull Inflatable Boat during marine firefighting and search and rescue operations- Solar charging system and biofuel-compatible engines for better sustainabilityJointly developed by the SCDF, HTX (Home Team Science and Technology Agency), Defence Science and Technology Agency (DSTA), and Penguin Shipyard International, the MRV2G exemplifies SCDFs commitment to meeting current and future maritime emergency challenges.

[Marine Firefighting Operation @ East of Singapore]This morning (20 June) at about 8:10am, SCDF was alerted to a fire onboard an oil tanker anchored in the waters of Singapores eastern area.Three SCDF marine rescue vessels and about 40 marine firefighting specialists from Brani Marine Fire Station and West Coast Marine Fire Station were deployed to the incident. Upon SCDFs arrival, black smoke was seen emitting from a storeroom in the oil tanker. Marine firefighters used a water monitor from a marine rescue vessel to cool the exterior of the affected oil tanker. Known as boundary cooling, this helps to cool the metal structure of vessels. Concurrently, another team of firefghters boarded the oil tanker to locate the seat of fire and extinguished it using a water jet. There were no reported injuries and all crew members of the affected oil tanker were accounted for. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

[Fire @ Block 5, Holland Close] Earlier this evening at about 7:25pm, firefighters from Alexandra Fire Station responded to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon arrival, one of the bedrooms in a 23rd-floor unit was on fire. Firefighters entered the smoke-filled unit and extinguished the fire with two water jets. As a result of the fire, the rest of the unit also sustained heat and smoke damage. Two persons who had evacuated from the affected unit before SCDF's arrival were assessed for smoke inhalation and conveyed to Singapore General Hospital. About 100 persons were evacuated by the Police and SCDF from the affected block. During the firefighting operation, two firefighters experienced heat exhaustion. One was conveyed to Singapore General Hospital and the other to National University Hospital. Both of them were conscious when conveyed to the hospitals.The cause of the fire is under investigation.*Update: One of the firefighters was discharged from the hospital earlier this morning (20 June) and given five days of medical leave. The other firefighter has been warded for further observation. SCDF will continue to check on their well-being.**Update: The second firefighter was discharged earlier today and was given 4 days of medical leave. Both firefighters are currently resting at home.

[Keeping Singapore Safe | Fire Safety Managers]Since 1994, with the passing of the Fire Safety (Fire Safety Manager) Regulations Act, public and industrial buildings in Singapore (such as those with high occupancy or specific risk profiles) are required to appoint a Fire Safety Manager (FSM). Today, there are around 15,000 certified FSMs in Singapore. Working closely with building owners, the key role of FSMs is to ensure compliance with the Fire Safety Act and its regulations in the building premises the FSM is appointed to. FSMs also help to enhance the safety of building occupants by raising their fire safety awareness and emergency preparedness through fire drills and implementing fire prevention measures in the building premises.As SCDFs key point-of-contact on fire safety matters, FSMs provide essential building information and help facilitate SCDFs emergency response, as well as the evacuation of the building occupants during an emergency. Their fire safety training and expertise make them a vital partner in keeping building premises and communities fire-safe.Swipe through to meet two experienced FSMs: Ms Veronica Mah from National University Hospital and Mr Ibrahim Bin Daud from Singapore Sports Hub!

[Fire @ 20, Jalan Tenteram]At about 11:40am today, firefighters from Central Fire Station responded to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon SCDF's arrival, the fire involved items placed along the corridor outside a unit on the 2nd floor and 3rd floor. The fire had also affected the inside of both these units. The fire was extinguished by SCDF using two water jets. As a result of the fire, a few neighboring units also sustained heat and soot damage.About 40 persons from the affected block were evacuated by the Police and SCDF as a precautionary measure. SCDF conveyed two persons to Singapore General Hospital, two persons to Tan Tock Seng Hospital, and one person to KK Womens and Childrens Hospital for smoke inhalation.The cause of the fire is under investigation.Members of the public are advised to help maintain a safe living environment by keeping common corridors, lift lobbies, and staircases free of clutter. A cluttered corridor can increase the risk of fire spread, hinder evacuation efforts, and delay SCDFs response during an emergency. Find out more on the guidelines on the use of common areas. SCDF conveyed five persons to the hospital for smoke inhalation. One of them, a 51-year-old man, was subsequently arrested by the police for the offence of mischief by fire.Preliminary findings by SCDF indicate that the fire was intentionally started.

[Fire @ Block 226, Lorong 8 Toa Payoh] Yesterday (14 May) at about 10:50pm, firefighters from Bishan Fire Station responded to a fire at Block 226, Lorong 8 Toa Payoh.Upon arrival, the living room of a 10th floor unit was on fire. Firefighters conducted forcible entry into the smoke-filled unit and extinguished the fire with a water jet.During the firefighting operation, firefighters found a person inside a bedroom. The person was brought out to safety and assessed by a paramedic for smoke inhalation and burn injuries. The person was conveyed to Singapore General Hospital. About 30 persons from the neighbouring units were evacuated by the Police and SCDF.A person from a unit on the 14th floor who had experienced breathlessness was conveyed to Tan Tock Seng Hospital.Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire had likely originated from a personal mobility device (PMD) battery in the living room. To prevent such fires, SCDF would like to remind the public not to purchase or use non-original batteries for their active mobility devices, including PMDs and powered assisted bicycles (PABs). Also, do not charge PMD/PAB batteries for an extended period of time or overnight. See the accompanying infographic for more fire safety tips.

[International Firefighters Day]As we commemorate International Firefighters Day (IFFD) today, lets take a moment to honour the contributions and sacrifices made by the global fraternity of firefighters and emergency medical services personnel. This morning, our SCDF frontline personnel donned a red and blue ribbon, stood in solidarity, and observed a minute of silence. The ribbon colours are widely recognised to represent emergency services globally, as well as the main elements firefighters work with - red for fire and blue for water. Every day, our emergency responders answer the call of duty, selflessly protecting and saving lives and property. Here at SCDF, we remember our colleagues who lost their lives in the line of duty. To all our lifesavers, both past and present, thank you for your unwavering dedication and sacrifice in keeping our community safe. InternationalFirefightersDay TheLifeSavingForce

[31st Rota Commander Course Commissioning Parade] Earlier today (21 Apr), 66 officer cadets from the 31st Rota Commander Course (RCC) were commissioned as Senior Officers at the Civil Defence Academy. The 31st RCC comprised 14 local and 52 international cadets from the Abu Dhabi Civil Defence Authority (ADCDA). These cadets from the ADCDA will now join the ranks of many other international officers who have previously graduated from SCDFs training courses. The RCC Commissioning Parade marks a significant milestone for these graduating cadets, who have undergone a comprehensive seven-month training programme to develop their knowledge and skills in firefighting, rescue, and emergency medical response. As Senior Officers, they will lead their fellow officers to advance the lifesaving mission of protecting and saving lives and property. During the event, five officer cadets were presented with awards to recognise their achievements in the following categories:- Overall Best Cadet: Officer Cadet Ethan Poh Xuan Rui - Best in Physical Training: Officer Cadet Arthur Wong Jun Xiang- Best in Knowledge: Officer Cadet Foo Jun Sheng- Best in Practical: Officer Cadet Wesley Chow Koh Lin- Best Performing International Cadet: Officer Cadet Sultan Omar AlbreikiCongratulations to the 31st RCC! We wish them all the best as they embark on the next phase of their lifesaving journey

[SCDF Day @ Civil Defence Academy]Yesterday evening, the SCDF Day Dining-In ceremony was held at the Civil Defence Academy. This annual event commemorates the integration of the Singapore Fire Service and SCDF on 15 April 1989, consolidating Singapores fire, rescue and emergency medical services response into a single organisation.The ceremony, which serves as a platform for our officers to rededicate their commitment to our lifesaving mission and reaffirm our core values of Pride and Care, was attended by SCDF regular officers, full-time National Servicemen, Operationally Ready National Servicemen and civilian staff. Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS), Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, graced the event as the Guest of Honour. In his speech, MOS Faishal recognised and commended SCDF personnel who have exemplified SCDFs core values in and beyond their duties. He also spoke about SCDFs Operation Lionheart contingent, who were recently deployed to Myanmar for disaster relief efforts, and praised the team for their professionalism, compassion and dedication to saving lives. Congratulations to all award winners! As we honour their achievements, we also reaffirm our dedication and commitment towards our mission to protect and save lives and property. PrideandCare OurPeopleOurPride

This annual event commemorates the integration of the Singapore Fire Service and SCDF on 15 April 1989, consolidating Singapores fire, rescue and emergency medical services response into a single organisation.The ceremony, which serves as a platform for our officers to rededicate their commitment to our lifesaving mission and reaffirm our core values of Pride and Care, was attended by SCDF regular officers, full-time National Servicemen, Operationally Ready National Servicemen and civilian staff. Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS), Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, graced the event as the Guest of Honour. In his speech, MOS Faishal recognised and commended SCDF personnel who have exemplified SCDFs core values in and beyond their duties. He also spoke about SCDFs Operation Lionheart contingent, who were recently deployed to Myanmar for disaster relief efforts, and praised the team for their professionalism, compassion and dedication to saving lives. Congratulations to all award winners! As we honour their achievements, we also reaffirm our dedication and commitment towards our mission to protect and save lives and property. [Final update: Fire @ No. 23 Gul Drive]Earlier this morning at about 6:15am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.The fire involved waste materials in a warehouse measuring about 40 metres by 20 metres. Firefighters deployed two water jets and a firefighting machine to contain the fire. The fire was extinguished in about an hour. Firefighters are damping down the affected area.There were no reported injuries. The cause of the fire is under investigation.*Damping down refers to the application of water to wet burnt surfaces immediately after a fire is put out. It is to prevent any potential rekindle of fire from the hot burnt surfaces.

[Update 9: Operation Lionhearts Homecoming] Earlier today (8 April) at about 4pm, the SCDFs Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent returned to Singapore. The OLH contingent, comprising 80 members and four search canines, was deployed to support search and rescue efforts in Myanmar on 29 March, a day after the country was hit by the devastating earthquake. A welcome reception was held at Changi Airport, where Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law, and Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State, Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development received the contingent members. Families and loved ones were also present to warmly welcome them home. In his welcome address, Minister Shanmugam expressed his heartfelt gratitude to the OLH contingent, along with officers from the Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX), for assisting with search and rescue operations in Myanmar. He commended the contingent for their dedication to service. Minister Shanmugam also expressed his appreciation to the families and loved ones of the contingent members for their support. To our OLH contingent, you have truly embodied the spirit of being a Lifesaver, not only in Singapore but also beyond borders. Welcome home, our Lifesavers We would like to express our utmost appreciation to the Singapore Embassy in Yangon for facilitating the OLH contingents deployment in Myanmar. We would also like to thank Singapore Airlines, Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore, Changi Airport Group, Myanmar Airways International, ST Logistics and SATS Ltd Singapore Hub team for facilitating the contingents flight and logistical arrangements on short notice. The people of Myanmar will always be in our hearts and minds. Though the road to recovery may be challenging, their admirable resilience in the face of adversity will guide them through, and we are confident that they will emerge stronger and recover from this disaster.

[Fire @ 278, River Valley Road] Earlier today at about 9:45am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at 278, River Valley Road.Upon arrival, the fire was raging on the second and third floors of a 3-storey shophouse. Several persons were on a ledge outside the third-floor unit. Members of the public, including construction workers, used a metal scaffolding and a ladder to reach those stranded and brought a number of them to safety. SCDF immediately deployed rescue ladders and a Combined Platform Ladder to rescue the rest of the stranded persons on the ledge. At the same time, firefighters proceeded to the second and third floor to fight the fire. The fire was extinguished with three water jets within 30 minutes.About 80 persons from the affected shophouse and nearby premises were evacuated by the Police and SCDF.A total of 18 casualties (four adults and 14 children) were conveyed to the hospital. The cause of the fire is under investigation.We would like to thank the members of the public who assisted in the rescue of the stranded persons for their quick actions and bravery.

[Update 8: Stand down of Operation Lionheart in Myanmar] The 80-member Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent has begun preparations to return home. Over the last two days, the OLH contingent has been handing over essential supplies such as tents, canned food and ready-to-eat rations, to the Myanmar Fire Services Department (MFSD). The OLH contingent also donated two tents to Naypyidaw Womens Hospital, and five tents along with medical drugs and medical supplies to Naypyidaw General Hospital. It is hoped that these supplies will continue to help the relief and recovery efforts as the people of Myanmar work to rebuild their community. On behalf of SCDF, Team Leader COL Tay Zhi Wei, gifted a battery-operated hydraulic cutter to U Myat Thu, Director General MFSD. This cutter was instrumental in rescuing a man trapped underneath concrete slabs in a semi-collapsed three-storey residential building on 30 March. Despite its compact size, the cutters powerful capability enabled it to cut through the rebar in the concrete slabs within an extremely confined area, freeing the man and saving his life. This cutter is now an enduring symbol of friendship between the SCDF and MFSD, where it will continue to serve, saving lives in the good hands of MFSD. An appreciation ceremony organised by the National Disaster Management Committee (NDMC) in Naypyidaw, brought together Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) teams from Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Vietnam and Philippines. A moment of silence was observed in memory of the earthquake victims. The OLH contingent will be returning home tomorrow (8 April) at 4:10pm, on Singapore Airlines at Changi Airport Terminal 3.

The OLH contingent also donated two tents to Naypyidaw Womens Hospital, and five tents along with medical drugs and medical supplies to Naypyidaw General Hospital. It is hoped that these supplies will continue to help the relief and recovery efforts as the people of Myanmar work to rebuild their community. On behalf of SCDF, Team Leader COL Tay Zhi Wei, gifted a battery-operated hydraulic cutter to U Myat Thu, Director General MFSD. This cutter was instrumental in rescuing a man trapped underneath concrete slabs in a semi-collapsed three-storey residential building on 30 March. Despite its compact size, the cutters powerful capability enabled it to cut through the rebar in the concrete slabs within an extremely confined area, freeing the man and saving his life. This cutter is now an enduring symbol of friendship between the SCDF and MFSD, where it will continue to serve, saving lives in the good hands of MFSD. An appreciation ceremony organised by the National Disaster Management Committee (NDMC) in Naypyidaw, brought together Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) teams from Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Vietnam and Philippines. A moment of silence was observed in memory of the earthquake victims. The OLH contingent will be returning home tomorrow (8 April) at 4:10pm, on Singapore Airlines at Changi Airport Terminal 3.

[Update 7: Operation Lionheart Search Operations and Medical Care in Naypyidaw]Over the past two days, the Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent has been actively involved in search operations in Ottara Thiri Township, Naypyidaw.At a partially-collapsed nine-storey hotel, the OLH contingent conducted a joint risk assessment with the Myanmar Earthquake Relief Contingent from Vietnam before commencing search operations. After an extensive search effort, a body was discovered beneath layers of concrete and steel. The OLH contingent worked with Indonesias National Search and Rescue Agency (BASARNAS) to recover the body by breaking through the debris.In addition to the search operations, the OLH contingent also established medical outposts in Pyokkon and Dhakhinna Thiri Townships to provide medical care to locals affected by the disaster. The medical outposts were set up at a monastery in Pyokkon and on the open ground of a hotel in Dhakhinna Thiri Township. The OLH contingents doctors and paramedics, assisted by the rescuers, provided wound care to promote healing and prevent infection. They also attended to patients experiencing acute post-earthquake symptoms such as dizziness as well as musculoskeletal issues which were aggravated by carrying heavy loads while seeking refuge from the earthquake.Since the OLH contingents arrival in Naypyidaw on 29 March, they have searched a total of 26 sites and provided medical care to approximately 130 local residents affected by the disaster.

On 4th April 2025, we were honoured to host Prime Minister Lawrence Wong at Punggol Neighbourhood Police Centre and Punggol Fire Station During the visit, our officers showcased the latest operational capabilities. PM Wong witnessed hands-on demonstrations including SPFs Counter-Drone Capability and Next-generation Fast Response Car and SCDFs Smart Classroom with Virtual Reality and Extended Reality training systems, High-Performance Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and the Electric Pump Ladder. PM also had engagements with our Home Team National Servicemen (NSmen), who are part of more than 50,000 operationally ready NSmen and Full-time National Servicemen. They have all played a crucial role in keeping Singapore safe and secure over the past decades. This year also marks 50 years of Police National Service for SPF.We thank PM Wong for taking the time to visit us! OneHomeTeam safegaurdingeveryday thelifesavingforce

[Update 5: Operation Lionhearts Ongoing Search for Survivors]Over the past two days, the Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent has continued with search missions at 12 additional sites in Naypyidaw. Since the OLH deployment on 29 March 2025, they have searched a total of 25 sites. The OLH contingent continues to work closely with Myanmars National Disaster Management Office (NDMO), the Myanmar Fire Services Department, and other international rescue teams.In addition to deploying search canines and life detection equipment, the OLH contingent also used a drone to enhance search operations. Coupled with the ground assessment and aerial view, rescuers are able to get a holistic appreciation of the site and this helps them to better strategize search and rescue efforts. The OLH contingent remains steadfast in its mission, determined to search every assigned location in the hope of finding survivors.

[Update 3: Operation Lionhearts Search & Rescue Efforts in Myanmar]Over the past 36 hours, the Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent, working with Myanmars National Disaster Management Office (NDMO) and Myanmar Fire Services Department, responded to seven sites in Naypyidaw and one site in Mandalay.The contingent divided into two teams, worked in shifts to ensure sustained search and rescue efforts at the eight sites, while at the same time, ensuring sufficient rest for our officers. No lives were detected at these sites.For such large scale disasters, all search and rescue efforts are coordinated through the NDMO. This coordination ensures resources are optimized and that there is no duplication of efforts at the same site.At the moment, there are a few international teams including OLH, operating in Naypyidaw, while other international teams are operating in Mandalay. The OLH contingent will continue with its search and rescue operations in Naypyidaw.

Festive snacks were also distributed by Minister Josephine Teo as a token of appreciation. From all of us here at The Life Saving Force, we wish all our Muslim colleagues and friends, Selamat Hari Raya.

[SCDFs Operation Lionheart Deployment to Myanmar]In response to the request for humanitarian assistance in the aftermath of an earthquake in Myanmar yesterday (28 Mar), SCDF has deployed the Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent to assist in disaster rescue efforts. The contingent departed from Changi Airport at about 1:20pm today (29 Mar).Led by Team Leader, COL Tay Zhi Wei, the 80-member OLH contingent comprises rescuers from the elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART), Operationally Ready National Servicemen (ORNS), full-time National Servicemen medical doctors, paramedics, search specialists with four canines, hazardous materials specialists, and support officers. The pre-departure briefing and preparation began early this morning at HQ SCDF. The OLH contingent is carrying an array of portable Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) equipment such as cutting, breaking and lifting equipment, as well as life detection devices and fibre-optic scopes. These equipment which are battery operated will allow the team to be swiftly deployed to affected areas to begin immediate USAR operations. In addition, three SCDF officers are also deployed to Myanmar as part of the ASEAN Emergency Response and Assessment Team (ERAT) under the auspices of the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on Disaster Management (AHA Centre). The ASEAN-ERATs primary function is to provide rapid assessment and determine the critical resources required for the areas affected by the earthquake. Prior to the contingents departure, Associate Professor , Minister of State, Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development met with the team at HQ SCDF to express his appreciation to the officers and to see them off, together with their family and loved ones.We would like to thank for facilitating the flight arrangements on short notice, especially during such major disasters where prompt assistance is crucial to those in need. We would also like to thank and SATS Ltd Singapore Hub team for their assistance.We wish our OLH contingent a safe and successful mission.

The contingent departed from Changi Airport at about 1:20pm today (29 Mar).Led by Team Leader, COL Tay Zhi Wei, the 80-member OLH contingent comprises rescuers from the elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART), Operationally Ready National Servicemen (ORNS), full-time National Servicemen medical doctors, paramedics, search specialists with four canines, hazardous materials specialists, and support officers. The pre-departure briefing and preparation began early this morning at HQ SCDF. The OLH contingent is carrying an array of portable Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) equipment such as cutting, breaking and lifting equipment, as well as life detection devices and fibre-optic scopes. These equipment which are battery operated will allow the team to be swiftly deployed to affected areas to begin immediate USAR operations. In addition, three SCDF officers are also deployed to Myanmar as part of the ASEAN Emergency Response and Assessment Team (ERAT) under the auspices of the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on Disaster Management (AHA Centre). The ASEAN-ERATs primary function is to provide rapid assessment and determine the critical resources required for the areas affected by the earthquake. [Pre-Dawn and Break Fast Meals with SCDF Officers]Yesterday (24 Mar) morning, Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS) for Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, joined our officers at Bukit Batok Fire Station and 4th SCDF Division for their pre-dawn meal (sahur). Despite the early hours, camaraderie was strong as officers came together with MOS Faishal to share a meal and bond.Later in the evening, Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law, and Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim, Chairman of the Home Affairs and Law Government Parliamentary Committee, visited the Civil Defence Academy (CDA) for the breaking of fast (iftar). They expressed their appreciation to the CDA officers and trainees for their unwavering dedication and hard work in training to become Lifesavers at the frontline. Our heartfelt thanks to Mr K Shanmugam, Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, and Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim for their visit and support! Our personnel remain steadfast in their lifesaving mission, always ready to respond and protect our community.

[Final Update: Fire at 10 Tuas Avenue 18A]Earlier this evening (8 Mar) at about 7:30pm, SCDF responded to a fire at the above mentioned location. The fire involved paint associated products in an area measuring about 30m x 15m on the first floor of a two-storey industrial building. SCDF firefighters extinguished the fire using 4 water jets in about 1 hour. 6 persons evacuated from the premises before SCDFs arrival. Two persons were assessed for smoke inhalation by an SCDF paramedic and declined to be sent to the hospital.The affected area is being damped down using an unmanned firefighting machine and water jets. The cause of fire is under investigation.

[Final Update: Fire at 11 Kranji Crescent]On 19 February 2025, SCDF responded to a fire involving waste materials at the above mentioned location. The fire has been extinguished. Over the past four days, SCDF worked round-the-clock to douse the deep-seated pockets of fire within the waste heaps.SCDF is scaling down our resources. As a precautionary measure, a fire engine and crew will remain at the premises to watch over the area that was affected by the fire. SCDF will also progressively hand over the site to the premises owner for their recovery operations.

[Responders, Partners and Volunteers Appreciation Event 2025]On Tuesday (18 Feb), the Responders, Partners and Volunteers Appreciation Event was held at HomeTeamNS Khatib.The event, jointly organised by the Ministry of Home Affairs and SCDF, recognises SGSecure Responders, SCDF Community First Responders (CFRs) and SCDF volunteers who have helped save lives and property, as well as community partners who have played a significant role in building the pool of Responders.Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS), Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, graced the event as the Guest of Honour.In his speech, MOS Faishal highlighted the Lifesavers Emergency Point (LEP) initiative, a joint effort between SCDF, Temasek Foundation, the Housing Development Board and Town Councils, in strengthening the communitys readiness towards emergencies. Situated at the lift lobbies of HDB blocks, these LEPs are equipped with Automated External Defibrillators and fire extinguishers for public use. Since 2023, over 4,000 fire extinguishers have been installed across one in every two HDB blocks. These fire extinguishes have already been used in more than 70 minor fire incidents.During the event, 27 Responders received appreciation plaques for their contributions towards saving lives. 52 community partners, including all 17 Town Councils, were recognised for their partnership with the Home Team to strengthen emergency preparedness initiatives. 26 SCDF Volunteers comprising Civil Defence Auxiliary Unit Exemplary Officers, National Civil Defence Cadet Corps Honorary Officers and Senior Cadet Lieutenants as well as Civil Defence Lionhearter Clubs were also presented appreciation plaques for their dedication and efforts.Thank you to all our Responders, volunteers and community partners! We look forward to the continued collaboration in empowering the community to step forward to help during emergencies.CommunityFirstResponderCommunityLifesaversANationofLifesaversOurCFRsOurHeroesWhatsYourRoleSGSecure

[Electric Vehicle Fire along BKE]On 17 February 2025 at about 9:20pm, SCDF was alerted to a car fire along BKE towards Woodlands near Dairy Farm Road exit. The fire involved an electric vehicle (EV). Upon arrival, SCDF firefighters covered the EV with a vehicle fire blanket to isolate the fire and contain the spread of smoke. Three water jets were deployed to cool the EV and a specialised equipment was used to penetrate the EV's undercarriage battery housing and inject water directly to the burning battery to extinguish the fire. [SCDF Annual Statistics 2024] The SCDF annual statistics for Emergency Medical Services (EMS), Fire Incidents, and Fire Safety Enforcement Checks for Year 2024 were released today.Key takeaways: 1 SCDF responded to 245,279 EMS calls in 2024, a decrease of 0.6% or 1,553 calls from 2023. While demand for SCDFs EMS has alleviated slightly, we are observing a general upwards trend over the past five years. The increase in demand is expected to continue beyond 2025, given the ageing population in Singapore. 2 The overall number of fire calls increased by 1.8% to 1,990 calls in 2024. 3 There were 968 fires in residential premises in 2024, a decrease of 0.2% from 2023. Fires due to unattended cooking and electrical origin remained the top two causes of fires in residential premises in 2024. 4 There were 67 fires involving Active Mobility Devices (AMDs) in 2024, an increase of 21.8% or 12 calls from 2023. AMD fires remain an area of concern especially for those that occur at residential premises. 5 SCDF stepped up the number of fire safety enforcement checks in 2024, with a total of 15,075 fire safety enforcement checks conducted. Read more via the link in our bio.

[Three Heroes Commended for Saving 5-year-old Girl] On 5 May 2024, Mr Jimmy Tan Chu Lok was at a condominium pool when he spotted a child drowning at the bottom the pool. Without hesitation, he dove in to rescue the child. Mr Parthiban Periasamy witnessed the incident and assisted Mr Jimmy in pulling the unconscious child out of the pool.Upon being alerted to the situation, another member of the public, Mr. Abhinav Venkateswaran, swiftly approached them. He immediately commenced CPR, and the child regained consciousness before SCDFs arrival. The child's life was saved due to the timely lifesaving interventions of Mr Jimmy, Mr Parthiban and Mr Abhinav. On 16 January 2025, the three men were presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. The awards were presented by COL Ser Boon Hui, Commander, 2nd SCDF Division.You too can make a difference during an emergency. Download the SCDF myResponder app and register as a Community First Responder via the app. You can also learn essential lifesaving skills through SCDFs Responders Plus Programme at go.gov.sg/scdfrpp. Lets build ANationOfLifesavers together! [Rescue Incident @ 11 Toa Payoh Industrial Park]Earlier today, at approximately 5:50pm, SCDF was alerted to an incident at 11 Toa Payoh Industrial Park. A few persons were reportedly trapped under piles of rugs after a mezzanine, along with storage racks, collapsed inside a warehouse unit on the first floor.One person had managed to free himself before SCDF arrived and informed that three other persons were still trapped.Firefighters from Bishan Fire Station, rescuers from the Special Response Unit and the Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) commenced a search within the affected area, measuring approximately 20 meters by 10 metres. SCDF search dogs were also deployed. The firefighters and rescuers removed piles of rugs and cut through storage racks to reach the three trapped persons. After an operation lasting about 90 minutes, all three persons, two of whom were children, were rescued. Two persons were conveyed to Tan Tock Seng Hospital, while the two children were taken to KK Women's and Children's Hospital. All four persons were conscious when conveyed to the hospitals.

[Fire @ Blk 224A, Sumang Lane]Earlier this morning at about 5:05am, firefighters from Punggol Fire Station, SengKang Fire Station and Tampines Fire Station responded to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon arrival, black smoke was emitting from a unit on the seventh floor. The fire, which involved a bedroom, was extinguished with a water jet. Four persons had evacuated from the unit before SCDFs arrival. About 60 persons from the neighbouring units were evacuated by the police and SCDF as a precautionary measure.A person was assessed by an SCDF paramedic for smoke inhalation and conveyed to Singapore General Hospital.Preliminary findings indicate that the fire was likely caused by an electrical origin in the bedroom. SCDF would like to remind the public to adopt the following good practices to prevent electrical fires:a) Do not overload power sockets with electrical appliances;b) Switch off electrical appliances when not in use;c) Check the condition of wires regularly. Frayed wires should be replaced or repaired immediately; d) Do not run wires under carpets or mats and keep wires away from hot surfaces; e) Use appliances and electrical plugs bearing the Safety Mark. [30th Rota Commander Course Commissioning Parade]Yesterday morning, 35 officer cadets from the 30th Rota Commander Course (RCC) were commissioned as Senior Officers at the Civil Defence Academy (CDA).Over the past seven months, these cadets have undergone a comprehensive training programme to acquire knowledge and skills in firefighting, rescue and hazardous materials mitigation operations.In his speech, the guest of honour, Mr Zhulkarnain Bin Abdul Rahim, Chairman of the Home Affairs and Law Government Parliamentary Committee, shared about CDAs redevelopment project. The final phase of redevelopment concluded in December 2024 with the reopening of the Furnace building and its new fire simulators, providing cadets with enhanced and realistic training. Mr Zhulkarnain also shared about how technology such as robotics can be leveraged to help SCDF optimise manpower resources during operations. During the event, four Officer Cadets were presented with awards to recognise their achievements in the following categories:- Overall Best Trainee: Officer Cadet Sulaiman Bin Ahmad- Best in Physical Training: Officer Cadet Md Akid Danial Bin Masri- Best in Knowledge: Officer Cadet Ng Shu Jie Sylvester- Best in Practical: Officer Cadet Dovyn Gan Kang JieCongratulations to the 30th RCC! We wish them all the best as they begin the next phase of their journey with the Life Saving Force

[Final update: Fire @ Block 971 Hougang Street 91]Earlier today (9 Jan) at about 12:40pm, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.SCDF resources from Sengkang Fire Station and Ang Mo Kio Fire Station responded to this fire. SCDF arrived at the location in eight minutes.The fire involved a unit on the 3rd floor and was extinguished using three water jets. A firefighting robot was also used to ventilate the unit. The fire was extinguished at about 3:15pm.Two persons were found inside a bedroom by firefighters. Both persons were pronounced dead by an SCDF paramedic.A cat, a bird and eight rabbits were also brought out of the unit alive by the firefighters.SCDF is continuing its search within the unit. SCDFs fire investigators are also at the scene investigating the cause of fire.[Additional update] SCDF firefighters have found a third person in a bedroom. The person has been pronounced dead by an SCDF paramedic.

[Fire @ 10A Jalan Tampang]Earlier this evening (8 Jan) at about 8:25pm, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location. [SCDF Fire Safety Enforcement Blitz]Yesterday, SCDF conducted a fire safety enforcement blitz as part of its ongoing efforts to maintain a high level of fire safety standards in buildings and premises.During the inspection, there were several fire safety non-compliances detected at two commercial premises. These non-compliances include the non-maintenance of fire safety provisions such as exit lights, fire extinguishers and hosereels, and obstructions to emergency escape routes due to poor housekeeping. There were also unauthorised fire safety works involving installation of partitions and unauthorised change of use such as the conversion of a carpark space to a storage area without approval in one of the premises.Enforcement actions will be taken against the responsible entities for the various non-compliances.SCDF will continue to step up enforcement checks at premises where increased footfall is expected amidst the festive season. Premises owners are reminded to practice good housekeeping and adhere to the fire safety regulations, so as to ensure the safety of everyone.

[Fire @ Blk 921 Tampines Street 91]At about 9:40pm today (24 Dec), firefighters from Tampines Fire Station and Changi Fire Station responded to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon arrival, black smoke was emitting from a unit on the first floor. The fire, which involved a bedroom inside the unit, was extinguished with a water jet. There was no one inside the unit. About 50 residents from neighbouring units were evacuated by the SCDF and the police as a precautionary measure.No ambulance assistance was required. Preliminary findings indicate that the fire had likely originated from a Power Assisted Bicycle (PAB) battery which was charging inside the bedroom. To prevent such fires, the public is reminded not to leave batteries or devices charging for a prolonged period or leave them charging unattended. In addition, do not purchase or use non-original batteries for your active mobility devices.

We are gathering more information and will provide an update in the post.[Secondary School Student Commended for Saving A Life]On 7 Sep 2024 at about 11:30am, Mark Eli Fernando was alerted to a cardiac arrest incident in a residential unit along Pasir Ris Street 21 via the SCDF myResponder app.Without hesitation, Mark quickly rushed to the scene and saw a man unconscious inside the unit. Drawing on his first aid training as part of his involvement with the Pathlight Hummingbird Scouts from .sg, Mark immediately rushed to the lift lobby to retrieve an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) and commenced Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) on the man. Mark also administered the AED on the man, who subsequently regained consciousness before the arrival of SCDFs Emergency Medical Services.Thanks to Marks timely intervention and lifesaving actions, the man survived and is alive today.On 24 Oct 2024, Mark was awarded the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. [SCDF-ITE Memorandum of Understanding Signing and Launch of the Work-Study Diploma in Paramedicine ] Earlier today (19 Nov), a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) was signed between the SCDF and the , marking a strategic partnership that provides Work-Study Diploma opportunities for aspiring trainees to join the Life Saving Force. Following the MOU signing, the new Work-Study Diploma (WSDip) in Paramedicine was officially launched. Developed in collaboration with the ITE and other industry partners, this programme provides a unique opportunity for aspiring trainees to kickstart their careers with the SCDF while pursuing a nationally recognised diploma. With a dynamic curriculum, the programme equips trainees with advanced medical knowledge and skills for handling complex medical emergencies, while offering an academic upgrading pathway to become SCDF Paramedic Specialists.Just earlier this year, the SCDF and ITE successfully launched the inaugural WSDip in Facilities Management, which attracted over 400 applicants to become Fire and Rescue Section Commanders. The strong response to this programme paves the way for even more work-and-learn opportunities through other WSDip programmes, including the newly launched WSDip in Paramedicine commencing in April 2025 and the upcoming WSDip in Logistics and Supply Chain Management launching in April 2026. [SCDF Welcomes SBS Transit for the AED-on-Buses Programme]As part of SCDFs efforts to strengthen community response to emergencies, we are excited to announce that we have partnered with to launch the AED-on-Buses Programme earlier today (8 Nov) Launched in 2015, the AED-on-Wheels programme is an extension of the SCDFs Save-a-Life initiative, which aims to enhance community first response to out-of-hospital cardiac arrest cases by increasing the availability of roving AEDs within the community. The SCDF - SBS Transit AED-on-Buses programme brings the total number of AED-equipped vehicles in the transport, logistics and courier industries to 441!The AED-on-Buses programme plays a vital role in providing lifesaving help, while providing transport services to the community. In the event someone suffers a cardiac arrest onboard a bus, an AED can be used by the SBS Transit Bus Captain or commuters to resuscitate the victim before SCDFs Emergency Medical Services arrive. All SBS Transit Bus Captains are CPR-AED trained.This programme, in partnership with SBS Transit and sponsored by the , reflects our shared commitment to enhancing community response and empowering the community to step up in times of need. Together, we can make a meaningful difference in saving lives and ensuring that help is always within reach

[Two Heroes Commended for Saving Toddler]Earlier this week, a heartwarming clip went viral showing a man rescuing a toddler at 350C Canberra Road. On 20 October, Mr Jahir was on his way to buy lunch when he spotted a young child standing on a ledge outside a 3rd floor unit. Without hesitation, Mr Jahir, along with another passerby Mr Sa Thu Ya Aung, stepped in to assist. Working together, Mr Sa Thu Ya Aung managed to reach the boy and brought him to safety before SCDF's arrival. The two men were awarded the Community Lifesaver Award earlier today for their courageous actions and swift response in saving a life. The award was presented by COL Lim Beng Hui, Commander of 3rd SCDF Division.We understand that there were other members of the public who had also assisted in this incident. We hope they can reach out to 3rd SCDF Division community engagement branch at 6852 2823 during weekdays (Monday to Thursday - 8:30am to 6:00pm, Friday - 8:30am to 5:30pm) so that we can duly recognise them for their good deed.CommunityLifesaverswhatsyourrole Pic: Mr Sa Thu Ya Aung (left) and Mr Jahir (right), holding their certificate and medal

[Fire @ 48, Woodlands Drive 16]Earlier today at about 1:25pm, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.The fire, which involved the household shelter and the kitchen of a unit on the 10th floor, was extinguished by firefighters with a water jet. There was no one inside the unit.As a result of the fire, the rest of the unit also sustained heat and smoke damage.About 50 persons from the neighbouring units were evacuated by the police and SCDF as a precautionary measure.A person was assessed by a paramedic for smoke inhalation and conveyed to Woodlands Health Campus. Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire was likely caused by an electrical origin in the household shelter.SCDF would like to remind the public to adopt the following good practices to prevent electrical fires:a) Do not overload power sockets with electrical appliances;b) Switch off electrical appliances when not in use;c) Check the condition of wires regularly. Frayed wires should be replaced or repaired immediately; d) Do not run wires under carpets or mats and keep wires away from hot surfaces; e) Use appliances and electrical plugs bearing the Safety Mark. The categories of appliances can be found at Do not leave batteries or devices to charge unattended for an extended period of time or leave it charging overnight.

[Final Update: Marine Firefighting Operation @ East of Singapore]This morning (21 Oct) at about 10:30am, SCDF was alerted to a fire onboard a vessel anchored in the East Johor Straits.Upon SCDFs arrival, all crew members of the affected vessel had been accounted for and there were no reported injuries. A water monitor from SCDFs Heavy Rescue Vessel was used to conduct defensive firefighting and cool the exterior of the vessel. Once there were no visible signs of fire, marine firefighting specialists boarded the vessel with a water jet to ensure that the fire, which involved the vessels exhaust funnel, had been fully extinguished. Damping down operations* are ongoing. The cause of the fire is under investigation. *Damping down refers to the application of water to wet burnt surfaces immediately after a fire has been put out. This is to ensure that deep-seated embers are fully extinguished to prevent any rekindling of the fire.

[Marine Firefighting Operation @ East of Singapore]This morning (21 Oct) at about 10:30am, SCDF was alerted to a fire onboard a vessel anchored in the East Johor Straits.A total of three SCDF marine firefighting and rescue vessels and about 30 marine firefighting specialists from Brani Marine Fire Station and West Coast Marine Fire Station were deployed to the incident. Upon arrival, SCDF used a water monitor to cool the exterior of the vessel. Cooling of the vessels exterior is known as boundary cooling, this helps to reduce the temperature of the vessels metal structure. All crew members of the affected vessel are accounted for. There are no reported injuries at the time of this report. Firefighting operation is ongoing.

[Junior Civil Defence Lionhearter Appointment Ceremony 2024]The Junior Civil Defence Lionhearter (JCDLH) Appointment Ceremony was held at Rivervale Primary School yesterday (17 Oct). This annual event formally inducts new JCDLHs as Emergency Preparedness ambassadors for their schools. Upper primary students from 14 schools were present yesterday. They took part in an Emergency Preparedness-themed carnival, had hands-on training in CPR-AED and fire extinguishers, and watched stage performances on Musical CPR and the SCDF K-9 team. The appointment ceremony ended with the recitation of the JCDLH pledge. No one is too young to learn life saving! We look forward to these students joining us in our journey towards ANationOfLifesavers

[Collapsed Structure @ 84 & 85, Syed Alwi Road]Earlier this morning (8 October 2024) at about 1:30am, SCDF was alerted to an incident involving two, 2-storey shophouse units, that had partially collapsed at the abovementioned location. Upon arrival, SCDF immediately commenced a search of the area to ascertain if anyone was trapped under the debris. Two search dogs and a drone were also deployed to augment the search operation.Firefighters rescued a person from the second floor of the affected shophouse unit (84, Syed Alwi Road) using a ladder. The person was unable to evacuate due to the blocked staircase. As some passersby had reportedly heard a loud blast during the incident, a firefighting machine was deployed as a precautionary measure, to disperse any potential build up of flammable gases using its water mist spray function. No persons were found trapped under the debris.Two persons were assessed by paramedics for minor injuries and conveyed to Singapore General Hospital and Tan Tock Seng Hospital. Four other persons were also assessed for minor injuries but they declined to be sent to the hospital. [Update]: Preliminary fire investigation findings indicate that a likely buildup of flammable gas within 84 Syed Alwi Road (operated as a restaurant) led to the blast and partial collapse of both units at 84 & 85 Syed Alwi Road. SCDF is still at the incident site. There are currently no flammable gas readings detected at the incident site.[Final Update]: SCDF resources have returned back to their fire stations. The incident site has been handed over to BCA to work with the owners of the two shophouses and their appointed Professional Engineers to ensure safety of the structure.

[Off-Duty Nurse commended for saving the life of a cardiac arrest patient; 5 others recognised for fighting a fire]On 26 July 2024 at about 4:15pm, an off-duty nurse from .sg , Ms Wong Wai Ting was at Causeway Point when she saw Mr Subhan lying unconscious on the floor. After assessing that Mr Subhan had no pulse and was not breathing, Ms Wong immediately commenced Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR). With the help of another person, CPR continued until the arrival of SCDFs Emergency Medical Services. Through their swift action in rendering assistance, Mr Subhan is alive today. SCDF would also like to thank the unidentified member of the public who assisted in this incident. We hope the person can reach out to us so that we can accord due recognition for stepping forward to assist in this incident. In a separate fire incident that occured at Blk 870 Woodlands Street 81 on 1 September 2024, upon receiving a notification via the myResponder app, Mr Izz Ziyad Bin Sharel and Mr Amirul Sufyan rushed to the scene, retrieved a fire extinguisher from a nearby Lifesavers Emergency Point and proceeded to fight the fire which involved a skip bin near the block.Mr Ryan Nicholas Santiago, who had seen the fire from his window, teamed with town council worker Mr Md Mizanur Rahman and his supervisor, Mr Rahman Md Arifur who were nearby, to retrieve the hosereel. Together, the five courageous men helped to contain the fire before SCDF's arrival.On 25 September 2024, the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award was presented to Ms Wong. The SCDF Community First Responder Award were presented to Mr Rahman, Mr Mizanur Rahman, Mr Amirul and Mr Ryan. The awards were presented by COL Bob Tan, Deputy Commander, 4th SCDF Division. As Mr Izz Ziyad is an SCDF civilian officer from Ang Mo Kio Fire Station, he will be commended separately for rendering assistance beyond the call of duty. [Be Device-Safe Programme 2024]Did you know that in 2023, 60% of Active Mobility Device (AMD) fires resulted from illegally modified devices? AMDs, such as Personal Mobility Devices (PMDs) and Power-Assisted Bicycles (PABs), are fire risks when modifications are made to their electrical circuitry such as using non-original parts or installing additional batteries.Earlier today (14 Sep), Ms Poh Li San, Grassroots Adviser to Sembawang West Grassroots Organisations unveiled a refreshed visual for the Be Device-Safe programme. Together with the Land Transport Authority, SCDF, and Peoples Association Sembawang West Community Emergency and Engagement Committee, the unveiling was part of the Sembawang West Community Resilience Day held at Woodlands Mart.The Be Device-Safe programme aims to educate AMD users about the risks of AMD fires, and how to safely use and maintain them. Illegally modified AMDs are a severe fire risk. Visit and to find out more and Be Device-Safe!

[Fire @ Block 104 Jalan Bukit Merah]On 10 September 2024 at about 11:20am, SCDF responded to a fire at Block 104 Jalan Bukit Merah.The fire, which involved a bedroom in a 9th-floor unit, was extinguished by firefighters using a water jet. As a result of the fire, the rest of the unit also sustained heat and smoke damage.Two persons had evacuated from the unit before SCDFs arrival.About 35 residents from the 9th to the 11th floor were evacuated by SCDF as a precautionary measure.Six persons from neighbouring units were assessed by paramedics for smoke inhalation. All six persons were conveyed to Singapore General Hospital.The fire is likely to have started in the bedroom. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

[Two Community First Responders recognised for extinguishing a fire] On 4 Aug 2024, at about 11:50pm, community first responders (CFRs) Mr Ruwayfi Bin Muhammad Noh and Mr Hng Ze Tang were in their homes when they received a myResponder alert for a fire in the centralised refuse chute (CRC) at Block 665B Jurong West Street 64.Both CFRs immediately responded. Arriving at the scene, they could see smoke emitting from the CRC. They proceeded to open the shutters to the CRC, and extinguished the fire using a water hose before SCDFs arrival. Their prompt actions were instrumental in extinguishing the fire. On 3 September 2024, the two CFRs were awarded the SCDF Community First Responder Award. The awards were presented by AC Goh Boon Han, Commander, 4th SCDF Division. [Fire @ Block 469 Admiralty Drive; One person rescued from unit]At about 2:35pm today, firefighters from Yishun Fire Station, supported by Woodlands Fire Station, responded to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon arrival, the kitchen of a unit on the fourth floor was on fire. Firefighters entered the smoke-filled unit to conduct the firefighting operation. The fire, which was confined to the kitchen area, was extinguished with a water jet. As a result of the fire, the living room sustained heat and smoke damage. While the firefighting operation was ongoing, firefighters searched the unit and found a person in one of the bedrooms. The person was rescued out of the unit. The rescued person was assessed for smoke inhalation and conveyed to Singapore General Hospital.About 50 persons from the affected block were evacuated by the Police as a precautionary measure.The cause of the fire is under investigation.

[Have you downloaded the new myResponder app?] ! Existing registered users will need to download the new version of the myResponder app to continue receiving emergency alerts and updates.First launched in 2015, the myResponder app enables registered community first responders (CFRs) to be alerted to nearby minor fire and suspected cardiac arrest cases, locate automated external defibrillators (AEDs) and respond to such incidents before SCDF's arrival.This latest version of the app will also allow users to see the location of other responding CFRs and choose their mode of response (by foot, bicycle, or motor vehicle), allowing the app to adjust the alert it sends out according to the mode of travel. Since the launch of the first myResponder mobile app, at least 80 cardiac arrest victims have been saved by CFRs who were alerted through the app. Download the new myResponder app and be part of ANationofLifesavers today! You can make a difference in someone's life The mobile app was jointly developed by SCDF and .

[Ferry Rescue Exercise (FEREX) 2024] Yesterday (22 Aug), SCDF participated in the FEREX 2024, an annual exercise organised by Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore as part of Singapore Safety Week. The exercise involved over 200 personnel from eight government agencies and industry partners. The multi-agency exercise simulated the collision of two ferries, resulting in a fire onboard one of the ferries and the other ferry at risk of sinking. As part of the exercise, a Rapid Response Fire Vessel, which can reach a top speed of up to 40 knots with high manoeuvrability, was deployed for firefighting, as well as the search and rescue operation. A Heavy Rescue Vessel was also deployed to evacuate passengers, with emergency medical services personnel onboard to triage and render medical assistance to the casualties. FEREX 2024 was a good opportunity for all participating agencies to validate our operational plans and procedures, and test our multi-agency operational response and coordination during a maritime incident. [Fire @ Block 313, Hougang Avenue 5]Early this morning at about 12:50am (16 Aug), SCDF firefighters from Sengkang Fire Station and Paya Lebar Fire Station responded to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon SCDFs arrival, the living room of a unit on the second floor was on fire, and one person was reported trapped inside the unit.Firefighters immediately conducted forcible entry through the front door and entered the smoke-logged unit. A team of firefighters found the person in the kitchen and brought the person out to safety. The fire was extinguished with a water jet. As a result of the fire, the entire living room was damaged and the rest of the unit sustained heat and soot damage. Four persons were assesed by SCDF paramedics. Two were sent to Singapore General Hospital and one was sent to Changi General Hospital. One person declined to be sent to hospital. About 30 people from the neighbouring units were evacuated by the police as a precautionary measure. Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire had likely started from a Personal Mobility Device (PMD) that was in the living room. The cause of the fire is still under investigation. SCDF would like to remind the public not to charge the batteries for an extended period of time or leave them charging overnight. In addition, do not purchase or use non-original batteries. See the accompanying infographic for more fire safety tips.

[Stay Fire Safe this Seventh Month]As the Lunar Seventh Month or Hungry Ghost Festival approaches, religious activities such as burning of incense paper and joss sticks are expected to increase. Do stay fire safe during this period by observing the following fire safety tips.Remember, fire safety is our collective responsibility!

[Fire @ Block 612, Ang Mo Kio Avenue 4]Earlier this morning at 1:55am, SCDF was alerted to the fire at the abovementioned location.Firefighters from Ang Mo Kio Fire Station, supported by Bishan Fire Station, entered the smoke-filled unit on the 11th floor to fight the fire. The fire, which involved a bedroom, was extinguished with a water jet. As a result of the fire, the rest of the unit sustained heat and soot damage. 5 persons from the affected unit had evacuated prior to SCDFs arrival. SCDF conveyed two persons to Singapore General Hospital and two persons to KK Womens and Childrens Hospital for smoke inhalation. Another person declined to be sent to hospital. About 30 residents from the block were evacuated by the Police and SCDF as a precautionary measure. Preliminary investigation indicates that the cause of the fire is of electrical origin, likely from an electrical socket in the bedroom.The cause of the fire is under investigation. SCDF would like to remind the public on good practices to prevent electrical fires from occurring: a) Do not overload electrical sockets with electrical appliances; b) Switch off electrical appliances when not in use; c) Check for frayed wires or cracked cords. If observed, the electrical appliance should be repaired or replaced. Do not use faulty appliances; d) Do not run wires under carpets or mats and keep wires away from hot surfaces; e) Use appliances and electrical plugs bearing the Safety Mark. The categories of appliances can be found at

[Fire @ 37, Lor 20 Geylang; three persons rescued]Earlier this morning at 3:30am, firefighters from Kallang Fire Station, Paya Lebar Fire Station, and Central Fire Station responded to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon arrival, the fire was raging inside a unit on the fifth floor. Two persons were seen standing precariously on the window ledge of the affected unit and shouting for help. SCDF firefighters immediately deployed a Combined Platform Ladder and rescued the two persons.While fighting the fire inside the unit, firefighters found another person in one of the bedrooms and brought the person out to safety. The fire, which involved the living room, was extinguished using a water jet. As a result of the fire, the rest of the unit sustained heat and smoke damage. Two persons were conveyed to Tan Tock Seng Hospital, and the other person was conveyed to Singapore General Hospital. During the firefighting operation, a firefighter sustained a minor injury when a piece of false ceiling landed on his neck and shoulder area. He was assessed by a paramedic and conveyed to Tan Tock Seng Hospital as a precautionary measure. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

[Fire @ 11, Kian Teck Road] Earlier today at about 1:40pm, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon arrival, a section of solar panels (measuring about 15 metres by 10 metres) mounted on the zinc roof of a single-storey factory was on fire. As such rooftop solar panel fires can spread quickly across the rooftop, firefighters immediately used two water jets to contain the fire and prevent it from spreading. The fire was fully extinguished within 20 minutes. 76 staff had evacuated the premises before SCDFs arrival.There were no reported injuries. Preliminary investigations indicate that the fire is likely to be of electrical origin from the solar panels.

[Final Update: Fire @ 21, Seletar West Farmway 1] At about 2:35am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.The fire involved a single-storey warehouse measuring about 30 metres by 20 metres. The warehouse comprises an office and storage of scaffolding materials. The fire was extinguished in about two hours with three water jets and an unmanned firefighting machine. A total of 10 emergency vehicles and about 50 firefighters were deployed to this incident.There were no reported injuries SCDF is currently damping down* the affected area. The cause of the fire is under investigation.*Damping down refers to the application of water to wet burnt surfaces immediately after a fire has been put out. This is to ensure that deep-seated embers are fully extinguished to prevent any rekindling of the fire.

[29th Rota Commander Course Commissioning Parade] Yesterday (2 Jul), 47 Officer Cadets from the 29th Rota Commander Course (RCC) were commissioned as SCDF Senior Officers in a ceremonial parade held at the Civil Defence Academy. COMR Eric Yap, Commissioner SCDF, graced the event as the Event Officiating Officer. The RCC Commissioning Parade is a significant milestone for these graduating cadets, who have undergone a comprehensive training programme to develop their knowledge and skills in firefighting, rescue, and emergency medical response over the course of seven months. As Senior Officers, their tasks include leading their fellow officers in SCDFs lifesaving mission of protecting and saving lives and property. Amongst the graduating cadets were nine Officer Cadets from the Direct-Entry Paramedic Senior Officer scheme. Before joining the 29th RCC, these nine Officer Cadets attended a 12-month Diploma programme in Paramedicine Science at Nanyang Polytechnic, and a 3-month operational attachment at the fire stations. This scheme underscores the transformation of SCDFs Emergency Medical Services (EMS) to meet increasing operational demands while further elevating the service delivery of our EMS to the public. Speaking to the graduating cadets, COMR Eric Yap underlined the importance of the training and development of SCDF officers, guided by SCDFs training philosophy - Train as we would operate; Learn as we innovate. COMR Eric Yap also expressed his appreciation to the families and loved ones of the cadets for their support and encouragement throughout the course.Congratulations to the 29th RCC! We wish them all the best as they embark on the next phase of their journey with the Life Saving Force

[Prioritising SCDFs Emergency Medical Services Resources for Life-threatening Emergencies] Demand for SCDFs Emergency Medical Services (EMS) has significantly increased over the years and is expected to continue to trend upwards due to the increasing and ageing population. With this rising demand for SCDFs EMS, SCDF has been prioritising the deployment of our emergency medical resources and response based on the severity of the medical emergency through the SCDFs EMS Tiered Response Framework. First introduced in 2017, various initiatives under the EMS Tiered Response Framework were progressively implemented over the years enhanced medical call triaging by 995 call-takers at SCDF Operations Centre using the advanced medical protocol system, non-conveyance policy and non-dispatch policy for emergency ambulances. These initiatives allow SCDF to manage and prioritise our stretched EMS resources for life-threatening medical emergencies that require more immediate medical attention, and where every second matters. We would like to thank the public for their understanding and support over the years. SCDF remains committed to meet the increasing EMS demand whilst ensuring operational excellence. At the upcoming SCDF Workplan Seminar on 4 July, SCDF will announce two new EMS initiatives which will build on the existing initiatives rolled out under the EMS Tiered Response Framework and continue to prioritise our response for life-threatening medical emergencies. Stay tuned and remember Call995OnlyForEmergencies

[40th Anniversary of the 995 Emergency Number]On 1 July 1984, 995 was established as Singapores fire and ambulance emergency number. At the time, all 995 calls would go to the control room located at Central Fire Station. Today, all 995 calls are handled by the Operations Centre located at SCDFs headquarters at 91, Ubi Avenue 4. The Operations Centre has evolved over the decades, harnessing technology to increase its efficiency. One such technology is the Advanced Command, Control and Communications (C3) Emergency System, which enables SCDF to dispatch emergency vehicles with the fastest arrival time to fire, rescue, or emergency medical incidents, based on live traffic conditions. The system also allows for real-time monitoring on the location of the fleet of emergency vehicles to enhance deployment efficiency. In 2023, the Emergency Video System (EVS) was launched in collaboration with the Singapore Police Force, Home Team Science and Technology Agency, and ST Engineering, enabling 995 callers to transmit live footage of an incident to the Operations Centre. The EVS enhances the Operations Centres situational awareness of the incidents, and also helps to facilitate the decision-making of emergency responders when responding to these incidents. Today, as we commemorate the 40th anniversary of the 995 emergency number, we also salute the Operations Centre Specialists and emergency responders who remain steadfast in our mission to protect and save lives for a safe and secure nation. TheLifeSavingForce

[Thomson-East Coast Line Stage 4 (TEL4) Opening Ceremony: Civil Defence Shelter at Siglap MRT Station]Earlier today, Prime Minister and Minister for Finance attended the TEL4 opening ceremony as the Guest-of-Honour. As part of the ceremony, PM Wong was briefed on the Civil Defence (CD) Shelters, and SCDFs community engagement efforts to promote lifesaving skills such as applying Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), using an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) and Improvised First Aid Skills.CD Public Shelters are prepared, converted, and managed by Operationally Ready National Servicemen (ORNSmen) from the SCDFs Public Shelter and Resilience Units (PSRUs). During peacetime, the PSRUs attend annual In-Camp Training (ICT) to ensure their competency and readiness in CD Public Shelter operations. As part of their In-Camp Training, 21A PSRU, was deployed to prepare and facilitate the booths at the event. If you couldnt make it to the event, you can learn basic firefighting, first aid and CPR-AED in the physical session of the SCDFs Responders Plus Programme or attend its online programme at go.gov.sg/scdfrpp. You can also check out our Virtual CD Shelter Tour at go.gov.sg/sheltertypes.Check out the pictures below for the event highlights!TEL4TEL4PublicPreviewANationOfLifesavers

[Fire @ Block 407 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10]On 11 June at about 2:40am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at Block 407 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10. Officers from Ang Mo Kio Fire Station and Bishan Fire Station responded to the incident.The fire involved a coffee shop at the block. The fire was extinguished with 4 water jets.Most of the stalls in the coffee shop were damaged by the fire. The rest of the coffee shop had sustained considerable heat and smoke damage. 18 residents from the units on level 2 were evacuated by the Police. There were no reported injuries.Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire had likely originated from unattended cooking in one of the stalls in the coffee shop. :SCDF would like to remind the public on some good practices to prevent such fires:- Do not leave cooking unattended- Do not place any flammable materials near heat sources- Keep the stove and its surrounding area free from grease and oil stains

[Fire @ 541, Bedok North Street 3]At about 10:10pm yesterday, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon SCDFs arrival, fire was raging inside a unit on the seventh floor. Firefighters from Paya Lebar Fire Station and Changi Fire Station conducted forcible entry and entered the smoke-logged unit to fight the fire. The fire, which involved the contents of a bedroom, was extinguished with a water jet. No one was inside the unit at the time of fire. As a result of the fire, the entire bedroom was damaged and the rest of the affected unit sustained heat and soot damage. About 100 residents from the affected block were evacuated by the Police and SCDF as a precautionary measure. There were no reported injuries. The cause of the fire is under investigation.
