[Road Traffic Accident near the junction of Loyang Avenue and Pasir Ris Drive 1]Earlier today (30 May) at about 9:30am, SCDF received a call for a road traffic accident at the abovementioned location. The accident involved the collision of two buses and a lorry. Firefighters from Changi Fire Station and Tampines Fire Station responded to the incident.Upon SCDFs arrival, a bus driver was trapped in the drivers seat of the bus.During the rescue operation, a firefighter postitioned himself inside the bus to ensure the safety of the bus driver. This was necessary as hydraulic rescue equipment were being used to pull back the dashboard and steering wheel that was forced inwards due to the impact of the collision. About 40 passengers from both buses had evacuated before SCDFs arrival.The bus driver who was trapped and the lorry driver were both conveyed to Changi General Hospital.

[Fire @ 93, Yishun Street 81]At about 11:40am today, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon SCDFs arrival, black smoke was emitting from a unit on the third floor. SCDF firefighters from Yishun Fire Station and Ang Mo Kio Fire Station conducted forcible entry and entered the smoke-logged unit to fight the fire. The fire, which involved a dryer and a washing machine at the service yard, was extinguished with a water jet. No one was inside the unit at the time of fire. As a result of the fire, the service yard sustained heat and soot damages.About 50 residents from the neighbouring units were evacuated by the police and SCDF as a precautionary measure. SCDF conveyed a person to Singapore General Hospital for smoke inhalation. Preliminary investigation indicates that the cause of the fire was of electrical origin from the dryer.SCDF would like to remind the public on good practices to prevent electrical fires from occurring:a) Do not overload electrical outlets with electrical appliances;b) Always switch off appliances when they are not in use;c) Check the appliance for frayed wires or cracked cords. If observed, the appliance should be repaired or replaced. Do not use faulty appliances;d) Do not run wires under carpets or mats and keep wires away from hot surfaces; e) Use appliances and electrical plugs bearing the Safety Mark. [Fire @ No.25 Mugliston Road]At about 11:35am today, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon SCDFs arrival, the fire was well alight and had affected a terrace house. SCDF firefighters deployed water jets in front and at the rear of the affected house, including three adjacent houses, to contain the fire. At the height of the firefighting operation, a total of seven water jets were deployed.The occupants from the affected unit, as well as neighbouring units had evacuated prior to SCDFs arrival.The fire was largely contained to the affected house. As a result of the fire, two adjacent houses sustained burn damage.There were no reported injuries.The cause of the fire is under investigation.Damping down operations* are ongoing. The cause of the fire is under investigation. *Damping down refers to the application of water to wet burnt surfaces immediately after a fire has been put out. This is to ensure that deep-seated embers are fully extinguished to prevent any rekindling of the fire.

At the height of the firefighting operation, a total of seven water jets were deployed.The occupants from the affected unit, as well as neighbouring units had evacuated prior to SCDFs arrival.The fire was largely contained to the affected house. As a result of the fire, two adjacent houses sustained burn damage.There were no reported injuries.The cause of the fire is under investigation.Damping down operations* are ongoing. The cause of the fire is under investigation. *Damping down refers to the application of water to wet burnt surfaces immediately after a fire has been put out. This is to ensure that deep-seated embers are fully extinguished to prevent any rekindling of the fire.

[Final Update: Fire @ 3, Toa Payoh Industrial Park] At about 9:40pm yesterday (9 May), SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.The fire, measuring about four basketball courts, involved two units. The first unit is a car workshop and the second unit is an industrial workshop. The fire was extinguished in about 1 1/2 hours with six water jets and one unmanned firefighting machine. A total of 15 emergency vehicles and about 60 firefighters were deployed to this incident.In the course of the firefighting operation, a firefighter experienced cramps in his legs. He was conscious and stable, and conveyed to Tan Tock Seng Hospital as a precautionary measure. There were no other reported injuries.SCDF is currently carrying out the damping down* operation of the affected area.*Damping down refers to the application of water to wet burnt surfaces immediately after a fire has been put out. This is to ensure that deep-seated embers are fully extinguished to prevent any rekindling of the fire.

[Fire @ Block 76 Lor Limau]Earlier this morning (6 May) at about 2:30am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the above mentioned location.Upon SCDFs arrival, the fire could be seen raging inside a unit on the sixth floor. Firefighters conducted forcible entry to gain access into the unit. The fire, which affected the entire unit, was extinguished by firefighters from Central Fire Station and Bishan Fire Station with two water jets.Two persons were found in the utility room in the kitchen area and were rescued by the firefighters. They were conveyed to Singapore General Hospital.Another person was found inside one of the bedrooms and was pronounced dead at the scene by an SCDF paramedic.About 200 people from neighbouring units were evacuated by the police and SCDF as a precautionary measure. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

[SCDF Commemorates International Firefighters Day]Every year on 4th of May, SCDF commemorates International Firefighters Day (IFFD) - a day where we recognise and honour the sacrifices made by firefighters and emergency medical services personnel around the world. This morning, SCDF frontline personnel donned a red and blue ribbon, stood in solidarity and observed a minute of silence. The ribbon colours symbolise fire and water, elements that are closely related to firefighters work. They are also widely recognised to represent emergency services globally.As we commemorate IFFD today, let us take a moment to remember and thank all emergency responders, both past and present, for their selfless commitment, sacrifice, and dedication to duty. InternationalFirefightersDay TheLifeSavingForce

[Community First Responders saved the lives of two people who suffered a cardiac arrest] On 17 Feb 2024 at about 9:10pm, Mr Kenneth Wong Kuo Fong was visiting Ms Joanne Hoo Yuen Yuen at her home when Ms Joannes mother, Mdm Ng Lian Koon collapsed. Quickly determining that she was in cardiac arrest, Mr Kenneth asked the visitors in the household to call 995 and he immediately performed Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) with Ms Hoos assistance. Mr Chia Jun Wei , Mr Keefe Tan Yu En and Mr Lokesh Prasad Chinna Chandragari responded upon receiving a notification on the myResponder app. Working as a team, they continued CPR and used an Automated External Defibrillator (AED), which was retrieved from a Lifesavers Emergency Point* at the lift lobby of a nearby block. In another incident on 16 Mar 2024 at about 4:30pm, Mr Law Ghee Beng collapsed from a cardiac arrest at Sengkang Swimming Complex. Springing into action, Senior Lifeguard Donguines Larni Olandesca, Lifeguard Zhu Zhou and Lifeguard Mi Qiang rushed to assist Mr Law. They performed CPR and used an AED. Mr Law subsequently regained consciousness before SCDFs arrival. Thanks to their timely lifesaving actions, both Mdm Ng and Mr Law are alive today. In recognition of their public spiritedness, these Community First Responders were each presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award on 26 Apr 2024. The awards were presented by COL Lim Beng Hui, Commander, 3rd SCDF Division. The presentation was graced by the attendance of the two cardiac arrest survivors who gave their heartfelt thanks to their lifesavers. You too can make a difference. Learn basic firefighting, first aid and CPR-AED in the physical session of the SCDF's Responders Plus Programme or attend its online programme at go.gov.sg/scdfrpp *The Lifesavers' Emergency Point is an initiative by the Singapore Civil Defence Force, Temasek Foundation, Housing & Development Board and Town Councils to progressively install fire extinguishers at the lift lobbies of every one in two HDB blocks. These fire extinguishers will be placed together with AEDs that are already installed at the HDB blocks.

[SCDF Day - 35 Years of Protecting and Saving Lives and Property for a Safe and Secure Singapore]On 15 April 1989, the Singapore Fire Service and Singapore Civil Defence Force merged as one, consolidating Singapores fire, rescue and emergency medical services response into a single organisation.To commemorate the merger, the SCDF Day Dining-In ceremony was held at the Civil Defence Academy yesterday evening. This annual ceremony serves as a platform for our officers to rededicate their commitment to our lifesaving mission and reaffirm our core values of Pride and Care. The event was attended by SCDF regular officers, full-time National Servicemen, Operationally Ready National Servicemen and civilian staff.The SCDF Day Dining-In Ceremony was graced by Mrs Josephine Teo, Minister for Communications and Information and Second Minister for Home Affairs. In her speech, Minister Josephine Teo acknowledged and commended SCDF personnel who exemplified SCDFs core values in and beyond the course of their duties. Congratulations to all award winners and wishing all SCDF officers a Happy SCDF Day!

[Second Lease of Life to our Firefighting Hoses and Nozzles] As part of SCDFs upcycling and sustainability efforts, we donated decommissioned firefighting hoses and nozzles to Night Safari at ! Made of durable and flexible materials, the firefighting hoses are used to construct housing enhancements for the animals as well as enrichment devices to keep them physically and mentally stimulated. The firefighting hoses and nozzles are also used to clean the animal living areas.This meaningful initiative gives the old firefighting equipment a second lease of life, and reaffirms The Life Saving Forces commitment to environmental sustainability. [Abuse of SCDF Frontliners] On 17 May 2023 at about 10:15pm, SCDF responded to a medical case along Jalan Pemimpin involving a man who was reportedly drunk, and sitting on the pavement.While the ambulance crew was assessing the man after assisting him into the ambulance, he suddenly turned aggressive and tried to choke the Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) by grabbing his neck. The paramedic immediately intervened but the person continued his aggression, and tried to choke the EMT again despite attempts to calm him down.Police assistance was sought and the person was arrested. For using criminal force against public servants, the person was sentenced to two months imprisonment in March 2024.Every emergency call matters to us and we will do our utmost to serve the public with the best of our abilities. However, physical or verbal abuse hinders our emergency responders from carrying out their duty. SCDF does not take lightly such abuse to our emergency responders, and we will not hesitate to make a police report.

[Community First Responders Commended for Saving Lives] On 18 Feb 2024 at about 1:45am, Mr Chua Fu Shun and Mr Chua Fu Qin were about to head home after visiting their mother when they saw a fire at Block 287A Jurong East Street 21. Without hesitation, the Chua brothers called 995 and rushed to the affected unit on the 8th floor. They quickly called out to the occupants from the affected unit to evacuate. The two brothers also alerted other neighbouring units of the fire. Fortunately, the occupants evacuated in the nick of time and there were no reported injuries. On 24 Feb 2024 at about 8:10am, Assistant Station Manager (ASM) Grace Lim Yen Ling noticed a crowd gathering outside Woodlands MRT station. ASM Grace soon realised that a man had collapsed. ASM Grace immediately called 995 and alerted her colleagues for assistance. Senior Station Manager (SSM) Steven Lim Lin Keat quickly retrieved an Automated External Defibrillator (AED). When ASM Abdul Hadi Bin Ngadino arrived at the scene, he assessed that the collapsed man had no pulse and showed no sign of breathing; ASM Hadi promptly commenced Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR). SSM Andrew Chua Joo Chai, who was off-duty from his night shift, took turns with ASM Hadi to perform CPR. The man was resuscitated before the arrival of SCDFs Emergency Medical Services. On 28 March 2024, these Community First Responders were awarded the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. The award was presented by AC Goh Boon Han, Commander, 4th SCDF Division. The presentation was graced by Senior Parliamentary Secretary Mdm Rahayu Mahzam, Advisor to Jurong GRC GROs (Bukit Batok East). You too can make a difference. [Electrificationof SCDF Emergency Vehicles]We are excited to witness the launch of Singapore's first electric emergency vehicle at the Milipol Asia-Pacific - Tech X Summit (MAP-TXS) earlier today! Jointly developed by , , and Rosenbauer, the Electric Pump Ladder (more commonly known as a fire engine ) was unveiled by Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law, and Mrs Josephine Teo, Minister for Communications and Information and Second Minister for Home Affairs, at the MAP-TXS. With its lower centre of gravity and balanced axle load distribution, the EPL has greater stability and agility than vehicles of similar sizes. It also has an all-wheel steering function, allowing it to navigate tight spaces with ease!The EPL also has a fully digitalised platform that will enable firefighters to oversee the vehicle's functions conveniently using a tablet, enhancing operational efficiency in operating the EPL. We look forward to this newest addition to our fleet of emergency vehicles upon completion of its trials.

[Final Update: Fire @ 30, Defu Lane 9] At about 12:20am today (3 Apr), SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.The fire, which involved contents of a two-storey industrial building measuring about 30 metres by 30 metres, was extinguished in about two hours with four water jets and two unmanned firefighting machines. A total of 19 emergency vehicles and about 70 firefighters were deployed to this incident.Five persons had evacuated the building before SCDFs arrival. SCDF assessed a person for smoke inhalation and conveyed the person to Sengkang General Hospital. Another person was also assessed for smoke inhalation but the person declined to be sent to the hospital. In the course of the firefighting operation, a firefighter experienced heat exhaustion and was conveyed to Sengkang General Hospital as a precautionary measure. There were no other reported injuries.SCDF is currently carrying out damping down* operations.*Damping down refers to the application of water to wet burnt surfaces immediately after a fire has been put out. This is to ensure that deep-seated embers are fully extinguished to prevent any rekindling of the fire.*UPDATE: The firefighter has been discharged from the hospital and currently resting at home.

[Final Update: Fire @ 1049, Eunos Avenue 6] At about 9:15pm yesterday (2 Apr), SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon SCDF's arrival, the fire was raging and had affected three units along a row of terrace workshops. Once the fire was under control, firefighters equipped with breathing apparatus proceeded cautiously into the smoke-logged units to locate the seat of fire. Firefighters had to exercise extreme caution as the roof of one of the units had collapsed.The fire, involving building materials and office equipment inside the three units, was extinguished in about four hours. As a result of the fire, two adjacent units sustained heat and smoke damages.SCDF deployed 19 emergency vehicles and about 70 firefighters for this incident. At the height of the firefighting operation, nine water jets, an aerial water monitor and an unmanned firefighting machine were deployed.There were no reported injuries. SCDF is currently carrying out damping down* operations.*Damping down refers to the application of water to wet burnt surfaces immediately after a fire has been put out. This is to ensure that deep-seated embers are fully extinguished to prevent any rekindling of the fire.*UPDATE: A firefighter was assessed for smoke inhalation and conveyed to Singapore General Hospital as a precautionary measure. **UPDATE: The firefighter has been discharged from the hospital and currently resting at home.

[1st International Rota Commander Course Graduation Ceremony]Earlier this evening, 65 cadets graduated from SCDFs first International Rota Commander Course (I-RCC) at the Civil Defence Academy (CDA).The graduating cohort, comprising cadets from the Abu Dhabi Civil Defence Authority (ADCDA) , have spent the last 6 months undergoing a comprehensive training programme to acquire the necessary skills and knowledge to perform the role of frontline commanders.The I-RCC follows the same training and assessment framework as SCDFs Rota Commander Course, with the cadets undergoing training in areas such as firefighting, medical training, urban search and rescue, and hazardous materials mitigation operations. Upon graduation, the cadets will continue their training at the Abu Dhabi Police Academy, before commissioning as Senior Officers of the ADCDA.Present at the ceremony were H.E. Mr Jamal Abdulla AlSuwaidi, Ambassador of the United Arab Emirates to Singapore, and H.E. Brigadier General Salem Abdullah Bin Barak Al Dhaheri, Director General (DG), Abu Dhabi Civil Defence Authority. A day before the ceremony, DG Salem visited CDA and Home Team Tactical Centre (HTTC) to tour the training facilities and see firsthand the training that the cadets had undergone. Congratulations to the 1st I-RCC graduates! We wish you all the best as you move on to the next phase of your lifesaving journey

[Fire @ 11, Kranji Crescent]Early this morning at about 2.25am, SCDF responded to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon SCDF's arrival, the fire was well alight and involved waste materials in a sorting/processing area of the premises measuring about 20m by 20m. At the height of the firefighting operation, four water jets, two foam jets, and an unmanned firefighting machine were deployed to contain the fire.The fire was extinguished within three hours. Firefighters are currently damping down* the affected area. A total of 10 emergency vehicles and about 50 personnel were deployed for this firefighting operation.25 persons had evacuated the premises before SCDF's arrival. There were no reported injuries. The cause of the fire is under investigation. *Damping down refers to using water to wet burnt surfaces immediately after a fire is put out. It is to prevent any potential rekindle of fire from the hot burnt surfaces.

[Rubbish Bin Fire Extinguished by a Family of Community First Responders]On 11 Feb 2024 at about 8:55pm, Mr Aeson Chua and his family saw a rubbish bin on fire at Block 932B, Hougang Avenue 9. The fire was threatening to spread to another bin nearby. Springing into action, Mr Aeson accessed a hosereel from a nearby void deck, and fought the fire. His brave young children, Anduin (age 7) and Arwen (age 11) assisted him to uncoil the hosereel drum while he pulled the hosereel towards the fire. His wife, Mdm Sinithra alerted 995 and looked out for the safety of her family. Thanks to their courageous act, the fire was extinguished. SCDF would also like to thank the other members of public who assisted in this incident. We hope they will reach out to us so that we can recognise them as well for their public spiritedness.On 22 March 2024, Mr Aeson and his family were presented with the SCDF Community First Responder Award. The award was presented by COL Lim Beng Hui, Commander, 3rd SCDF Division.You too can make a difference. Learn basic firefighting, first aid and CPR-AED in the physical session of the SCDF's Responders Plus Programme or attend its online programme at CommunityFirstResponderCommunityLifesaversANationofLivesaversOurCFRsOurHeroesWhatsYourRoleSGSecureFrom L to R LTC Md Shafi Rafie, Head, Community Engagement, 3rd SCDF Division; Mdm Sinithra Chua; Anduin and Arwen Chua; Mr Aeson Chua; COL Lim Beng Hui, Commander, 3rd SCDF Division; COL Bob Tan, Deputy Director, Volunteer and Community Partnership Department.

[Fire @ Block 112, Jalan Bukit Merah]At about 5:35pm today (19 Mar), SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.The fire involved a Power Assisted Bicycle (PAB) that was parked near a market stall on the ground floor. The fire was extinguished by firefighters from Central Fire Station with a water jet. As a result of the fire, three stalls sustained fire and smoke damage.There were no reported injuries.Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire had likely originated from the battery pack of the PAB.To prevent PAB fires, the public is reminded not to leave batteries or devices charging for a prolonged period or charging them unattended overnight. In addition, do not purchase or use non-original batteries. See the accompanying infographic for more fire safety tips.

[Fire @ Block 706, Clementi West Street 2]At about 2:10pm today (19 Mar), SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon SCDFs arrival, black smoke was emitting from a 4th floor unit. The fire, which involved contents of a room, was extinguished by firefighters from Clementi Fire Station using a water jet. As a result of the fire, the living room area also sustained heat and smoke damage.The occupants had evacuated the unit before SCDFs arrival. Three persons from the unit were assessed for smoke inhalation and conveyed to the Singapore General Hospital.Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire had likely originated from a Personal Mobility Aid (PMA) which was charging in the room. SCDF would like to remind the public that motorised devices that are modified, not properly maintained or do not use the original chargers are fire risks.

[Old fire hoses dog toys]Last week, Changi Fire Station donated dog toys made from old fire hoses to the Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals ().The material of these fire hoses are extremely durable and versatile. After years of keeping flames at bay, hoses which have reached the end of their operational lifespan are decommissioned and will now be sparking joy in the lives of our furry, four-legged pals! This is part of SCDFs commitment to environmental sustainability, where fire hoses have been donated to several organisations such as Wildlife Reserves Singapore and SEA Aquarium as part of similar upcycling projects. SCDF will continue to embrace sustainability efforts in our course of work and explore more ways to contribute to a eco-friendly, paw-some future!

[Junior Civil Defence Lionhearter (JCDLH) Challenge 2024]The Junior Civil Defence Lionhearter (JCDLH) Challenge 2024 was held virtually over Zoom last Friday (23 Feb), with almost 150 JCDLHs from 29 schools participating in a series of exciting activities. Associate Professor Ho Peng Kee, Chairman of the Home Team Volunteer Network graced the event as the Guest-of-Honour. As one of the Challenges pre-event components, the JCDLHs were tasked to prepare their most creative rendition of a Ready Bag, containing the essential items required for swift evacuation in a crisis. The Challenge's finale concluded with a nail-biting virtual quiz, where students were tested on their knowledge of emergency preparedness in different scenarios. Congratulations to Rivervale Primary School for emerging as champions of the JCDLH Challenge 2024! While the JCDLH Challenge 2024 may have come to an end, we urge our JCDLHs to continue serving as Emergency Preparedness (EP) ambassadors in their schools, spreading the importance of lifesaving skills amongst their fellow schoolmates, family and friends, and strive towards building ANationofLifesavers

[Exercise SG Ready: Civil Defence Shelter Open House]Earlier today (23 Feb), three MRT Civil Defence (CD) Shelters, namely Dakota MRT Station, Potong Pasir MRT Station, and Tan Kah Kee MRT Station, were opened for the public to visit as part of Exercise SG Ready and 40 years of Total Defence (TD40). Exercise SG Ready aims to increase Singapores readiness for crises and disruptions. The event was graced by Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, who visited Tan Kah Kee MRT Station. At the Shelter Open House, visitors learnt more about the public CD Shelters and its features, as well as lifesaving skills such as applying Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation, using an Automated External Defibrillator and Improvised First Aid Skills. [SCDF Annual Statistics 2023]The SCDF annual statistics for Emergency Medical Services (EMS), Fire Incidents, and Fire Safety Enforcement Checks for Year 2023 were released today.Key takeaways:1 SCDF responded to 246,832 EMS calls in 2023, a decrease of 3.9% from 2022. However, the overall EMS demand remained high, with an average of 676 EMS calls daily, which was 30% higher than in 2019 (pre-pandemic). 2 The total number of fire calls increased by 8.6% to 1,954 cases in 2023. 3 There were 970 fires in residential buildings in 2023, an increase of 3.7% from 2022.Fires due to unattended cooking and electrical origin remained the top two causes of fires in residential buildings in 2023. 4 While non-residential fires decreased by 6.9% in 2023, the number of fires in non-building premises rose by 34.9% to 580 cases. These fires in non-building premises included vegetation fires, vehicle fires, as well as fires involving discarded items.5 SCDF stepped up the number of fire safety enforcement checks in 2023. A total of 15,044 fire safety enforcement checks were conducted, an increase of 17.6% from 12,792 in 2022.Read more at

Earlier today, we recognised the efforts of seven remarkable staff of (MBS), for their public-spiritedness in responding to a medical emergency at their hotel. When a guest was found to be suffering from a cardiac arrest during his stay at the hotel, seven staff from MBS security team immediately sprung into action and coordinated their response to the emergency by carrying out the following actions: applying Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) on the guest, facilitating lift access and escorting the ambulance crew to the hotel room. These actions not only played a crucial role in expediting our ambulance crews response, but is essential to better the chances of survival, especially in cardiac arrest situation. In recognition of their public-spirited acts, the seven staff were awarded the Community Lifesaver Award at Marina Bay Sands. The awards were presented by COL Mohamed Firoz Bin Ramjan, Commander, 1st SCDF Division. Their swift response during the medical emergency exemplifies strong teamwork and also the importance of equipping ourselves with livesaving skills, such as CPR.CommunityFirstResponders CommunityLifesavers ANationofLifesavers OurCFRsOurHeroesWhatsYourRoleSGSecure

[Fire @ 287A, Jurong East Street 21] On 18 February 2024 at about 1:50am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location. The fire was raging inside a unit on the 8th floor when firefighters from Clementi, Bukit Batok and Jurong Fire Station arrived. The fire, which involved the living room, was extinguished with two water jets.Two persons self-evacuated from the affected unit before SCDF arrived. A person from a neighbouring unit was assessed for smoke inhalation and conveyed to Singapore General Hospital.The cause of the fire is under investigation.Common causes of household fires include unattended cooking, fires caused by electrical origin, and lighted materials like candlelight and burning incense that are left unattended. More information on fire prevention (pg 24-25) is available in the Civil Defence Emergency Handbook, which can be downloaded from the SCDF website.

[SCDF participates in Exercise SG Ready] In commemoration of 40 years of Total Defence (TD40) today (15 Feb 2024), SCDF participated in the inaugural island-wide Exercise SG Ready. Exercise SG Ready simulates disruption activities to increase Singaporeans readiness for crises and disruptions. Some of the disruption activities conducted at SCDF units include; Evacuation of Building, Water Disruption and Power Disruption. Though SCDFs infrastructures, including frontline units, have built-in redundancies and contingency plans to ensure operational readiness, these simulated disruptions remind our personnel the importance of being emergency ready. Check out the pictures below on SCDFs simulated disruption activities! TD40 AreYouReadyForDisruptions TotalDefence TogetherWeKeepSingaporeStrong ExerciseSGReady WeAreTotalDefence

[Fire @ Block 202, Bedok North Street 1]At about 3:45am today (13 Feb), SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.The fire, which was along the common corridor outside a 11th-floor unit, involved a Power Assisted Bicycle (PAB). The fire was extinguished by firefighters from Changi Fire Station using a fire extinguisher. The occupants of the affected unit had evacuated the unit before SCDFs arrival. Three persons from the affected unit were assessed for smoke inhalation and two of them were conveyed to the Singapore General Hospital. The third person declined to be sent to the hospital.Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire had likely originated from the battery pack of a Power Assisted Bicycle (PAB) which was charging.To prevent PMD/PAB fires, the SCDF would like to remind the public not to charge the batteries for an extended period of time or leave them charging overnight. In addition, do not purchase or use non-original batteries. See the accompanying infographic for more fire safety tips.

[Visit to Marine Division by Minister Shanmugam]Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law, visited the SCDF Marine Division yesterday (30 Jan) as part of his regular ground engagement with SCDF frontliners.During his visit, Minister Shanmugam boarded the Heavy Rescue Vessel (HRV), codenamed Red Manta, where he was briefed on the operational capabilities of SCDFs Marine Division.The visit was followed with a dynamic display of various firefighting vessels and their capabilities, including the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle and Unmanned Surface Vessel. The visit ended with a guided tour of the HRV, where Minister Shanmugam interacted with the personnel from Marine Division. He acknowledged their hard work and thanked them for their dedication to the Life Saving Force.

[Joint Exercise @ Raffles Lighthouse]Yesterday, , (MPA), and Police Coast Guard (PCG), conducted a joint exercise at Raffles Lighthouse located at Pulau Satumu. Codenamed Exercise Bluewhale, the exercise simulated responding to contingency scenarios which included a fire at the lighthouse, as well as the rescue of three persons who fell overboard from a ferry. As part of the exercise, a rescue jet ski and a remote-control flotation device were deployed by SCDFs Marine Firefighting Specialists to locate and rescue the casualties. Marine vessels from MPA and PCG were also deployed for cordoning and search operations. Such joint exercises serve to validate and update the respective agencies' joint operational plans and procedures, and also tests the agencies' coordination and response to a major maritime incident. MPA's tour operator, Lionheartlanders, and ferry operator, Marina South Ferries, were also involved in the exercise to practice their emergency procedures should an incident happen during one of the Raffles Lighthouse tours.Check out the photos of the exercise to see our responders in action!

[28th Rota Commander Course (RCC) Commissioning Parade]Earlier today, 44 cadets graduated from the 28th Rota Commander Course (RCC) at the Civil Defence Academy (CDA). Amongst the graduating cohort were two trainees from the General Directorate of Civil Defence, Kingdom of Bahrain, and three trainees from the Brunei Fire and Rescue Department. Over the course of seven months, these cadets have undergone a comprehensive training programme to acquire skills and knowledge in firefighting, rescue and hazardous materials mitigation operations. In his speech, the guest of honour, Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS) for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, shared about the second phase of CDAs redevelopment effort, which was completed in July last year. Four new training facilities have been operationalised, which provide RCC cadets with enhanced firefighting and rescue training through realistic simulations using advanced technology. MOS Faishal also spoke about strengthening of community partnerships, emphasising the importance of communitys role as first responders, and highlighted the opening of the Lifesavers Connect Zone at Joo Seng Fire Post in September last year as a significant milestone in SCDFs efforts to enhance community engagement. Congratulations to the 28th RCC! We look forward to your contributions in the Life Saving Force

[Fire Safety Enforcement Blitz at Commercial Premises]As part of SCDFs ongoing efforts to maintain and enforce a high standard of fire safety in buildings and premises, a fire safety enforcement blitz was conducted yesterday. During the enforcement blitz, SCDF detected common fire safety non-compliances at two commercial premises. These non-compliances include the non-maintenance of fire safety measures such as exit lights, fire extinguishers and main fire alarm panels, obstruction to hose reel, dry riser and emergency escape routes, as well as unauthorised change of use.Enforcement actions will be taken against the responsible entities for the various non-compliances.SCDF will continue with its stepped up enforcement checks at premises where an increased footfall is expected amidst the festive season. Premises owners are also reminded to ensure full compliance with the fire safety regulations. Remember, fire safety is a collective responsibility!

[SCDF donates old fire hoses]SCDFs fire hoses that are no longer serviceable have been given a new lease of life! As part of SCDFs commitment to environmental sustainability, some of SCDFs old fire hoses were donated to the Lao Conservation Trust for Wildlife (LCTW) yesterday, through the Animal Concerns Research and Education Society (ACRES). Soon, these hoses will be repurposed into toys and educational tools for rescued animals. Similar donations have also been made in recent years to organisations such as the Sumatran Ranger Project, Wildlife Reserves Singapore and SEA Aquarium. SCDF will continue to embrace sustainability efforts in our course of work and explore ways to contribute to a sustainable and eco-friendly future.Pictured: AC Anthony Toh, Director of Logistics, SCDF with Mr Kalaivanan Balakrishan, Co-CEO (Wildlife Rescue), ACRES, on behalf of LCTW during the donation of old fire hoses at SCDF HQ.

[Three Community First Responders commended for saving a life] On the afternoon of 17 September 2023, Dr Vianne Lau, a doctor with , was playing badminton at Heartbeat ActiveSG Sport Hall when she saw a man collapsed nearby. After ascertaining that the man had no pulse or breathing, Dr Lau immediately commenced Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR). Mr Chow Wei Jun, a Guest Officer from who was in the vicinity, also sprang into action and joined Dr Lau in administering CPR. Lifeguard, Mr Lionel Lo Chee Voon, was also alerted of the incident. He promptly retrieved an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) and medical equipment. The trio used the AED to deliver a shock to the man and the man regained consciousness before the arrival of SCDFs Emergency Medical Services. Thanks to their timely lifesaving actions, the man is alive. Kudos to Dr Lau, Mr Chow and Mr Lo! In recognition of their public-spirited act, the trio were presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award on 4 December 2023. The award was presented by COL Chew Keng Tok, Commander, 2nd SCDF Division. You too can help someone in distress by downloading SCDFs myResponder app and registering as a CFR via the app. Through the app, you can be alerted to nearby emergencies such as cardiac arrest incidents or minor fires that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity. [Impersonating as SCDF Officers to Conduct Sale of Home Fire Alarm Device (HFAD)]SCDF has received public feedback about persons claiming to be endorsed by the SCDF to sell HFADs in the Bedok area. These persons reportedly go door-to-door showing a pass with an SCDF logo, giving the false impression that they are authorised representatives from a government organisation. While SCDF encourages homeowners who have yet to install the HFAD in their homes to do so, we would like to inform members of the public that SCDF officers are not involved in any sale of HFADs or other fire safety related products. SCDF has also not authorised any company to conduct such activities on our behalf. Do exercise caution and be careful of such deceitful sales tactics.Members of the public can contact SCDF general enquiries (1800-286-5555) for clarifications if they encounter any person(s) claiming to be representing SCDF and purportedly conducting such sales on SCDFs behalf. For cases involving the impersonation of SCDF officers, members of the public are advised to lodge a police report.

[Fire @ Block 463, Crawford Lane] Yesterday night at about 11:50pm, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon SCDFs arrival, black smoke was emitting from a unit on the 15th floor.SCDF firefighters from Kallang Fire Station conducted forcible entry into the unit. There were no occupants inside the unit at the time of fire. The fire, which involved the living room, was extinguished by SCDF with a water jet. About 35 residents from the affected block had evacuated before SCDFs arrival.There were no reported injuries. Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire originated from the battery pack of a Power Assisted Bicycle that was charging in the living room. SCDF would like to remind the public not to leave the PMD/PAB batteries charging for an extended period of time or leave them charging overnight. Do not purchase or use non-original batteries. See the accompanying infographic for more fire safety tips.

[Surge in 995 EMS Calls] 995 Emergency Medical Services (EMS) calls to SCDF have surged to a high of nearly 750 calls a day on average in the first week of December.This is about 100 cases more than the average daily EMS calls between July to September 2023 (Note: Average daily number of EMS calls pre-COVID was about 550).And do you know that almost 5% of medical calls to the 995 hotline are non-emergencies? If EMS calls continue to climb, the public may experience delays in ambulance response, particularly for less critical medical incidents as the SCDF needs to continue prioritising our limited resources for life-threatening medical emergenciesWe are monitoring the situation closely. Measures have also been put in place to manage the increase in EMS Calls, some of which are: Redeploying ambulances to areas with higher rates of medical emergency calls Assessing 995 emergency calls and dispatching ambulances only for emergencies Not conveying to hospital patients who have been assessed by SCDF paramedics to have non-emergency medical conditionsOur 995 call takers, paramedics and frontliners are doing their best to provide swift conveyance to hospital for people with life-threatening and emergency medical conditions.Here's what YOU can do to help. Refrain from calling 995 if you are not suffering any life-threatening or emergency medical condition. Visit a nearby clinic to seek medical advice instead.Doing so will allow the SCDF to continue providing swift response and conveyance to those who require our emergency medical services the most.See picture for examples of critical, life-threatening medical emergencies.

[13 Persons in the Marine Community Commended for their Public-Spirited Acts during Emergencies at Sea] On 13 September 2023 at about 4:30pm, Mr Ahmad Bonda, a yacht crew member, was out at sea off Lazarus Island when he noticed an unconscious person floating face down. Mr Ahmad Bonda immediately paddled out and brought the person to shore with the help of his friends, Ms Flora Lee, Mr Jay Leong and Mr Benjamin Leong. Upon reaching the shore, Mr Ahmad Bonda promptly commenced cardiopulmonary resuscitation on the person. Three members of the public, Mr Wayne Liew, Mr Bruce Ong and Mr Mithu Muhammad Saminul Alam, who were in the vicinity, also quickly stepped forward to render assistance and ferried the person to St Johns jetty, where he was evacuated to Marina South Pier by SCDF. As a result of their prompt and coordinated lifesaving actions, the person survived and is alive today. In a separate incident on 4 September 2023 at about 1pm, a vessel off Seraya Buoy, located off the south-western coast of Singapore, caught fire. Two tugboats with six crew members onboard responded to the call for assistance. The crew on the first tugboat, Mr Daning Setiawan, Mr Syafei and Mr Dedi Masluhi, conducted the firefighting operation, while Mr Harimurti Raharjo, Mr Abdul Kadir and Mr Rahman were on standby on the second tugboat to provide additional support if required. For their civic-minded actions, the 13 Good Samaritans were presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award and the SCDF Community First Responder Award. The awards were presented by COL Ryan Ong, Commander of SCDFs Marine Division, and SUPT Desmond Ong, Commanding Officer, Brani Region, 's Police Coast Guard, on 29 November 2023. The presentation was also attended by Capt. Chong Jia Chyuan, Senior Deputy Director (Operations), Port Master, . You too can help by downloading the SCDFs myResponder app and register as a CFR via the app. Through the app, you can be alerted to nearby emergencies such as cardiac arrest incidents or minor fires that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity.

[Rescue Operation @ 1 Pandan Crescent] Yesterday evening, at about 4:50pm, SCDF emergency responders comprising firefighters and an ambulance crew from Clementi Fire Station, and specialists from the Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) were activated for a rescue operation at the abovementioned location.Upon SCDFs arrival, a man was found sitting at the bottom of a sprinkler pump room, about four metres in depth. The man was reportedly about to conduct maintenance for the sprinkler pump system when he fell through the opening of the pump room. Five SCDF personnel, including a paramedic, climbed down the cat ladder to assess the mans condition. As the man was feeling immense pain at his back area and his left leg, the paramedic administered medication to relieve his pain.DART specialists proceeded to set up the rescue equipment while the paramedic continued to work on immobilising the injured man to prevent further injuries when he is lifted out of the pump room. A DART specialist was lowered into the pump room and secured the man onto him, before they were both lifted out of the pump room. The man was conveyed to National University Hospital.

[Abuse of SCDF Frontliners]In the early hours of 1 December 2019 at about 1:40am, SCDF responded to a medical case where a man had collapsed on the pavement along Circular Road. Upon SCDFs arrival, the man was found lying on the pavement. While the ambulance crew was assessing the mans condition, he turned aggressive towards the ambulance crew. Despite attempts to calm the man down, he started hurling vulgarities at the crew and punched the paramedic in the face. The man was arrested at the scene by the Police. Earlier this month, the perpetrator was sentenced to five weeks of imprisonment for voluntarily causing hurt to a public servant. Every emergency call matters to us and we will do our utmost to serve the public with the best of our abilities. However, physical or verbal abuse hinders our emergency responders from carrying out their duty. SCDF does not take lightly such abuse to our emergency responders, and we will not hesitate to make a police report.

Held as part of the - & () , this flagship event reaffirms SCDF personnels allegiance and commitment to The Life Saving Force. It also serves as a platform for SCDF to show appreciation to our valued partners and volunteers. About 650 participants will participate in this years SCDF Parade, comprising a Guard-of-Honour contingent, a Flag Party comprising the flags of our units, and nine marching contingents representing the SCDF Divisions, SCDF Marine Command, Civil Defence Academy, Civil Defence (CD) Lionhearters Club, and Operationally Ready National Servicemen (ORNS) unit. [Final Update: Industrial Fire @ 46 Tech Park Crescent]Earlier this morning at about 7:15am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon SCDF's arrival, the fire was raging inside an area measuring about 20m by 20m on the first floor of a two-storey industrial building. The fire involved contents of an office, and a storage space for tools and materials used in metal works.At the height of the firefighting operation, four water jets were deployed to surround the fire and prevent it from spreading to the neighbouring premises. The fire was extinguished at about 8:40am. Damping down* is still ongoing at the time of this post. Six persons had evacuated the affected premises before SCDFs arrival. Another person on the second floor of the building was evacuated by SCDF. There were no reported injuries. A total of 15 SCDF emergency vehicles and about 80 SCDF personnel were deployed for this incident. The cause of the fire is under investigation.*Damping down refers to the application of water to wet burnt surfaces immediately after a fire is put out. This is to prevent any rekindling of the fire from the hot burnt surfaces.

[Ministers Awards Presentation Ceremony 2023]SCDF is honoured to be presented 52 awards at the Ministers Awards Presentation Ceremony (MAPC) 2023 held yesterday at the Home Team Academy. The MAPC recognises Home Team Departments and officers for their exemplary work and dedication in going above and beyond the call of duty. Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law, graced the ceremony as the Guest of Honour.Among the awards received was the MHA Distinguished Star Service Award (DSSA) which was awarded to SSG Muhammad Tamimi Bin Mohamad Mamsi. SSG Tamimi was part of the Operation Lionheart contingent deployed to Trkiye in Feb 2023 to assist in disaster rescue efforts.During the rescue mission in Trkiye, SSG Tamimi, together with fellow officers from SCDFs elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) and rescuers from Trkiye and Spain, successfully rescued a boy beneath the rubble of a collapsed building. For exemplifying tenacity and resolve during the rescue mission, SSG Tamimi is truly deserving of the MHA DSSA.Here at SCDF, we remain committed towards giving our utmost in our lifesaving mission of protecting and saving lives and property.Congratulations to all our award recipients!

[Fire @ Block 415 Ang Mo Kio Avenue 10] At about 9:15am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon SCDF's arrival, black smoke was seen billowing from a window on the 4th floor. There were no occupants in the unit at the time of the fire. SCDF firefighters equipped with breathing apparatus penetrated into the smoke-logged unit. The fire, which involved the contents of a unit, was extinguished by SCDF with two water jets. To aid in the firefighting effort, a Combined Platform Ladder was deployed at the rear of the block to provide external coverage with the second water jet.About 60 residents from the affected block were evacuated by the Police and SCDF as a precautionary measure. There were no reported injuries. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

[Joint Operational Exercise @ Singapore Cable Car]Our SCDF rescuers are well-trained to respond to complex height rescue scenarios Earlier today, officers from the SCDFs elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART), including officers from 1st SCDF Division and Brani marine fire station took part in a joint exercise with and . The exercise simulated the rescue of "passengers" in two cable car cabins within the vicinity of Habourfront Station and Selegu Tower.As part of the rescue scenario, DART officers had to traverse along the cable and rescued six "passengers" in one of the cable car cabins by bringing them back into the Harbourfront Station. The other two "passengers" in the other cable car cabin were safely lowered onto an SCDF Marine Rescue Vessel. Check out the pictures and video highlights of the exercise here!

[Fire @ Block 662 Buffalo Road]At about 8:05pm yesterday (17 Oct), SCDF was alerted to a fire in a 3rd floor unit at the abovementioned location.Before SCDFs arrival, a man who was inside one of the bedrooms in the affected unit was rescued by police officers and members of the public, through the bedroom window that was facing the corridor. The man was conveyed to Tan Tock Seng Hospital.The fire, which involved contents of the living room and kitchen, was extinguished by SCDF using two water jets. As a result of the fire, the rest of the unit sustained heat and soot damage. About 20 occupants from the affected block were evacuated by the police officers and SCDF as a precautionary measure. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

[Graduation Ceremony for the Inaugural CDAU Emergency Medical Technician Course] Yesterday afternoon (11 Oct), 12 Civil Defence Auxiliary Unit (CDAU) officers graduated from the inaugural CDAU Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) Course.These newly minted CDAU officers will perform frontline duties at the fire stations by responding to medical emergencies as an EMT alongside the paramedic in an ambulance. Apart from emergency medical services, CDAU officers serve an important role in complementing SCDF regular and full-time National Servicemen (NSF) in vocations such as Firefighting and Rescue, Public Education, Enforcement and Heritage Gallery Guides. The CDAU EMT course was conducted during weekday evenings and weekends over a period of about 20 weeks at the SCDFs National EMS Training Centre (NETC). CDAU officers undergo the same training syllabus and assessments that SCDF regular officers and NSFs go through. The graduation ceremony was officiated by SAC Abdul Razak, Director, Volunteer and Community Partnership Department. I am very proud of the inaugural batch of CDAU officers who have qualified as Emergency Medical Technicians. Their commitment to the spirit of volunteerism by undergoing this advanced pre-hospital care training reflects that Singapore is well on its way to become a Nation of Lifesavers. I hope these officers will inspire others to step forward and upskill themselves in the lifesaving mission. - SAC Abdul Razak. Find out more about how to be a CDAU officer and volunteer to save lives in the Home Team Volunteer Network website at . [Final Update: Fire @ 61 Yishun Industrial Park A]Earlier this evening, SCDF was alerted to a fire involving two workshop units on the sixth floor of a six-storey industrial building. About 80 SCDF officers and 20 emergency vehicles were deployed for the incident. At the height of the firefighting operation, firefighters used two water jets to fight the fire from inside the building, and two aerial water monitors were deployed to contain the fire from the exterior of the building.The fire, which involved furniture and alcohol products within the two workshop units, was extinguished by SCDF at 10pm. SCDF is currently carrying out the damping down operation at the affected floor.There were no reported injuries. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

[Five Persons Commended for Sea Rescue at Sentosa]On the morning of 9 July 2023, a group of six persons were using a kayak in the waters off Tanjong Beach, Sentosa when strong currents capsized their kayak. The kayakers kept themselves afloat by holding on to their capsized kayak and nearby floating barriers.Mr Ang Eng Leng, Mr Tan Han Leng and Mr Nicholas Teo Han Wei, who were fishing nearby on board their jet skis, saw the distressed group of kayakers and immediately proceeded to render assistance. They managed to rescue four of the kayakers.Mr Ahmad Hamim Bin Mohammad Hanib and Mr Jasmil Bin Jaafar who were working at the Ola Beach club nearby also responded to help using jet skis and rescued the last two kayakers. All six kayakers sustained minor injuries and declined to be sent to the hospital.In recognition of their quick actions to assist others, the five Good Samaritans were each presented with the SCDF Community First Responder (CFR) Award on 25 September 2023. The awards were presented by COL Ryan Ong, Commander Marine Division, SCDF, and SUPT Desmond Ong, Commanding Officer, Brani Region, Police Coast Guard. The presentation was also attended by COL Bob Tan, Deputy Director, Volunteer and Community Partnership Department, SCDF, and Ms Regina Lim, Deputy Director (Safety Governance & Promotion), Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore.You too can help by downloading the SCDFs myResponder app and register as a CFR via the app. Through the app, you can be alerted to nearby emergencies such as a cardiac arrest incident or minor fires that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity.CommunityFirstResponderCommunityLifesaversANationofLifesavers OurCFRsOurHeroesWhatsYourRoleSGSecure

[Mass Fire Evacuation Drill Closing Ceremony 2023] Yesterday (26 Sep), CDG ZIG Holdings Pte Ltd hosted the annual Mass Fire Evacuation Drill (MFED) closing ceremony at their premises. Organised by the .sg and supported by the SCDF, the event marked the end of the month-long campaign to promote fire safety and emergency preparedness in commercial and industrial buildings, as well as public buildings.As part of the closing ceremony, a fire evacuation drill was conducted at the Comfort Transportation Building along Sin Ming Drive. The drill included a simulated fire scenario in the car workshop equipment area which saw the Company Emergency Response Team (CERT) spring into action as the first line of response before the arrival of the SCDF. Subsequently, the CERT worked together with SCDF to continue the firefighting operation and casualty evacuation. Since its inception in 2004, the MFED campaign has garnered overwhelming support. This year, more than 89,000 participants from over 400 industrial and commercial premises, as well as educational institutions have conducted the fire evacuation drill in the month of September. MFEDs are pivotal in testing and validating the premises response plans and evacuation procedures, as well as the joint response and interoperability between different stakeholders during an emergency. [Community First Responder Commended for Saving a Life] On the morning of 16 Jul 2023, Mr Patrick Cheong was driving to work when he received an alert on the myResponder app notifying him of a case of cardiac arrest at Block 10, Chai Chee Road. Without hesitation, he acknowledged the alert and responded to the location. Upon arrival, he found a lady suffering from cardiac arrest inside a residential unit and her husband was performing Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) on her. Mr Patrick immediately rendered assistance to the lady by using an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) that he had retrieved from a nearby block. Three shocks were administered to the patient using the AED. Mr Patrick and the patient's husband continued CPR until the arrival of SCDF's Emergency Medical Services.Thanks to Mr Patrick's lifesaving actions, the patient survived and is alive today. Today (8 Sep), Mr Patrick was presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. The award was presented by COL Chew Keng Tok, Commander, 2nd SCDF Division. The patient attended the presentation and expressed her gratitude to Mr Patrick in person. As SCDF commemorates World First Aid Day tomorrow (9 Sep), Mr Patrick's actions serves as a stellar example that anyone can help to save a life and demonstrate the importance of first aid in a medical emergency. "Thanks to your help, I woke up. I recognised all my loved ones. I can walk, talk, sing, read, write and play with my daughter. My husband and I are so grateful to you. There are no words to describe it. You could have ignored the myResponder app alert, been too scared or not wanted the drama on a Sunday morning. Instead, you responded and became a hero." - Quote from cardiac arrest survivor to Mr Patrick. You too can help by downloading the SCDFs myResponder app and register as a CFR via the app. Through the app, you can be alerted to nearby emergencies such as a cardiac arrest incident or minor fires that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity. [Official Opening of Joo Seng Fire Post with Lifesavers Connect Zone] The Joo Seng Fire Post (JSFP) with the first Lifesavers Connect Zone (LCZ) co-located with it, was officially opened today (5 Sep) by Assoc Prof Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State, Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development. Located at Blk 9 Joo Seng Road, the JSFP provides emergency response to fire, rescue and emergency medical incidents around the Macpherson-Woodleigh area. SCDF now has a network of 23 fire stations and 28 fire posts providing islandwide emergency services coverage. At the LCZ which features interactive kiosks, members of the public can engage in self-directed learning or hands-on practice on lifesaving skills. These skills include Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), Improvised First Aid Skills, and In-Place Protection procedures. In our vision to build ANationOfLifesavers, SCDF will continue to deepen public engagement and increase touch-points in the heartlands for our community to learn emergency preparedness skills by co-locating more LCZs with fire posts in the near future.

[Height Rescue Operation @ 71A Tuas Nexus Drive] Earlier today at about 2:25pm, SCDF firefighters and specialists from the elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) were activated for a height rescue operation at a construction site at the abovementioned location.A man who was working on top of an approximately 40-metre high tower crane was feeling unwell and was unable to climb down safely on his own. A team of four DART specialists climbed up the crane via a cat ladder to reach the man who was sitting inside the crane cabin. The DART specialists then set up the height rescue equipment.The DART specialists secured the man onto a stretcher and lowered him down together with a DART specialist who attached himself to the stretcher to ensure the safety of the man while descending to the ground.The man was assessed by an SCDF paramedic and conveyed to National University Hospital.

[NFEC Fire Safety Seminar 2023]The annual National Fire and Emergency Preparedness Council (NFEC) Fire Safety Seminar 2023 was held early this morning (25 Aug) at Marina Bay Sands Convention Centre. The seminar is a platform for participants to be equipped with knowledge of preventing fires and handling emergencies at the workplace. More than 1000 participants comprising fire safety managers and practitioners were in attendance, together with Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, who graced the seminar as the Guest of Honour. This year, the 9th edition of the Fire Code was also launched at the Seminar. The Fire Code is a comprehensive set of standards that were first introduced in 1974 to ensure that organisations put in place appropriate and sufficient fire prevention and safety measures within their buildings and premises.Six speakers from various professional agencies and institutions were also invited to share their expertise on the latest fire safety developments and trends.Congratulations NFEC on the conduct of a successful and meaningful Fire Safety Seminar!

[ASEAN Strategic Policy Dialogue on Disaster Management 2023] As part of the ASEAN Disaster Management Week (ADMW) 2023, the ASEAN Strategic Policy Dialogue on Disaster Management (SPDDM) was held today (24 Aug). Hosted by Singapore since 2015, the SPDDM is the pinnacle event of the week-long ADMW to sharpen ASEANs disaster management policies and formulate long-term strategies. The theme for the ASEAN SPDDM 2023 is Disaster Resilience: Investing Today for a Sustainable Region. It underscores the need for forward-looking ideas that can enhance disaster resilience in ASEAN, especially with increasing occurrences of natural disasters that can bring about catastrophic consequences. The event concluded with an official dinner, which was graced by Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS) for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development. In delivering his closing remarks, MOS Faishal shared about the ASEAN Framework on Anticipatory Action in Disaster Management. Developed last year, the framework is a product of the strong partnerships and knowledge sharing between ASEAN partners to guide them on proactive disaster management measures. This year also marks the 20th anniversary of the ASEAN Committee on Disaster Management (ACDM). Comprising the National Disaster Management Organisations (NDMOs) of the ten ASEAN Member States, the ACDM was established to enhance ASEANs cooperation across all aspects of disaster management. SCDF is Singapores National Focal Point for the ACDM since its establishment in 2003. With that, the ADMW 2023 has successfully concluded! SCDF will continue to work in synergy together with our fellow NDMOs towards advancing disaster management in ASEAN.

It underscores the need for forward-looking ideas that can enhance disaster resilience in ASEAN, especially with increasing occurrences of natural disasters that can bring about catastrophic consequences. The event concluded with an official dinner, which was graced by Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS) for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development. In delivering his closing remarks, MOS Faishal shared about the ASEAN Framework on Anticipatory Action in Disaster Management. Developed last year, the framework is a product of the strong partnerships and knowledge sharing between ASEAN partners to guide them on proactive disaster management measures. This year also marks the 20th anniversary of the ASEAN Committee on Disaster Management (ACDM). Comprising the National Disaster Management Organisations (NDMOs) of the ten ASEAN Member States, the ACDM was established to enhance ASEANs cooperation across all aspects of disaster management. SCDF is Singapores National Focal Point for the ACDM since its establishment in 2003. With that, the ADMW 2023 has successfully concluded! SCDF will continue to work in synergy together with our fellow NDMOs towards advancing disaster management in ASEAN.

[ASEAN Disaster Management Week]The inaugural ASEAN Disaster Management Week (ADMW) 2023 is a week-long event held from 21 to 24 August 2023 with activities of the ASEAN Committee on Disaster Management (ACDM). Themed Disaster Resilience in ASEAN Now and Beyond, the ADMW 2023 serves as a platform to commemorate the achievements of ASEAN in disaster management and disaster risk reduction efforts, and charts ASEANs progress and strategies in disaster resilience. Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law, graced the official opening of the ADMW 2023 as the Guest-of-Honour earlier today (22 Aug). Also in attendance was Her Excellency Iwona Pirko, European Union Ambassador to Singapore. In his opening remarks, Minister Shanmugam reaffirmed the importance of the cooperation and coordination among ASEAN Member States to further strengthen our resilience and collective response to disasters in the ASEAN region and beyond. The ADMW 2023 is co-organised by SCDF, the National Focal Point for the ACDM Singapore, the ASEAN Secretariat, the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on disaster management (), European Union, Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation, Asian Development Bank, and Temasek Foundation. Around 200 guests including Ambassadors, and representatives from the ACDM, ASEANs Partners, United Nations, as well as the private sector and non-governmental organisations, will be attending the key events during the ADMW in Singapore.

[Fire @ Block 28, Ghim Moh Link]At about 7:35am today, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon arrival, the fire was raging inside a unit on the 36th floor. An occupant from the unit had evacuated before SCDFs arrival. The fire had engulfed the entire unit. SCDF firefighters from Clementi Fire Station and Alexandra Fire Station extinguished the fire with two water jets.About 60 occupants from the affected block were evacuated by the Police as a precautionary measure. SCDF conveyed two persons to the National University Hospital. One person had sustained smoke inhalation. Another person had sustained minor cuts and was conveyed as a precautionary measure.The cause of the fire is under investigation.

[Stay Fire Safe this Seventh Month]Tomorrow marks the start of the Lunar Seventh Month or Hungry Ghost Festival. For those who conduct religious activities like the burning of joss sticks and incense papers, do exercise caution! Here are some fire safety tips to observe during this period. Remember, fire safety is our collective responsibility!

[Launch of Lifesavers' Connect Zone]For residents living around Blk 9 Joo Seng Road, you may have noticed a new pop up in the hood - the Lifesavers' Connect Zone (LCZ)! Located right beside the existing Joo Seng Fire Post, the LCZ features interactive and hands-on kiosks for members of the public to learn In-Place Protection procedures, Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and Improvised First Aid. The LCZ will be officially launched early next month. However, members of the public can get early access to the facility and learn pertinent emergency preparedness skills, so do drop by if you are around in the neighbourhood!We look forward to spreading essential knowledge and skills on emergency preparedness within our heartlands. See you soon at the LCZ!ANationOfLifesavers

[Fire @ Blk 71, Redhill Road]At about 7:20am today, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon arrival, SCDF firefighters were alerted by residents that there were occupants trapped inside the smoke-logged unit on the 7th floor. SCDF firefighters from Alexandra Fire Station and Marina Bay Fire Station immediately conducted forcible entry into the unit by breaking the padlock of the metal gate.The fire was located at the corner of the living room and was extinguished by SCDF with several buckets of water. While the fire was being extinguished, another team of firefighters that were searching the premises found three children inside the toilet at the back of the kitchen. The children were carried out from the unit by the firefighters and assessed by an ambulance crew. All three children were conveyed to KK Women's and Children's Hospital for smoke inhalation. Before SCDFs arrival, two persons from the affected unit managed to evacuate through a bedroom window. They were assessed for smoke inhalation but declined to be sent to the hospital. In the midst of SCDF's operation, five cats were also brought out of the affected unit.About 25 persons from neighbouring units were evacuated by the SCDF and Police as a precautionary measure.Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire had likely originated from the batteries of two personal mobility devices (PMD) that were charging in the living room.SCDF would like to remind the public on the prevention of PMD/PAB fires, including not to charge batteries for an extended period of time or overnight. Do not purchase or use non-original batteries. See the accompanying infographic for more fire safety tips.

[Cardiac Arrest Patient Saved by Three Community First Responders] On 3 June 2023, Mr Nabil Bin Juraimi was at VivoCity Shopping Mall with his wife, Ms Nur Syafiqah Binte Mazlan and his brother, Mr Nafis Bin Juraimi, when they encountered a person who had collapsed at the basement (B2) of the mall. The trio immediately sprung into action to render aid to the collapsed person. Working as a team, they performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and used an automated external defibrillator on the person. Upon SCDF's arrival, they also assisted to direct the ambulance crew to the collapsed person. Mr Nabil and Ms Nur Syafiqah are nurses from Ng Teng Fong General Hospital, while Mr Nafis is an SCDF Operationally Ready National Serviceman. As a result of their timely lifesaving actions, the patient is alive today. Kudos to Mr Nabil, Ms Nur Syafiqah and Mr Nafis. On 26 July 2023, Mr Nabil, Ms Nur Syafiqah and Mr Nafis were presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. The awards were presented by Colonel Bob Tan, Deputy Director, Volunteer and Community Partnership Department. You too can help by downloading SCDFs myResponder app and register as a CFR via the app. Through the app, you can be alerted to nearby emergencies such as a cardiac arrest incident or minor fires that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity. [Home Team National Day Observance Ceremony 2023] Yesterday (4 Aug), the Home Team National Day Observance Ceremony was held at the Home Team Academy. Organised annually, the ceremony recognises and celebrates the exemplary work by fellow Home Team officers, volunteers, partners and members of the public. Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law, graced the ceremony as the Guest of Honour. In his National Day message, Minister Shanmugam thanked everyone for their dedication and commitment in keeping Singapore safe and secure. This year, 10 officers from the Singapore Civil Defence Force were commended for their accomplishments in their respective areas of work. Several Community First Responders were also awarded with the Public Spiritedness Award for their bravery and willingness to render assistance to those in need. Congratulations to all our award recipients!

[Two Community First Responders commended for saving a life] On 11 June 2023 at about 10:00pm, Mr Lim Kim Thia and Mr Lum Guang Ye were in their own homes when they received an alert on the myResponder app for a cardiac arrest incident at Block 259 Bukit Batok East Avenue 4. Both Community First Responders (CFRs) sprang into action and rushed to the abovementioned location. Mr Lim was the first to arrive at the scene and commenced Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) after assessing that the patient had no pulse and was not breathing. Mr Lum retrieved an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) from the void deck of a nearby block and arrived soon after Mr Lim. Mr Lum prepared the AED while Mr Lim continued CPR. The CFRs then used the AED to deliver a shock to the patient before the arrival of an SCDF ambulance. As a result of their prompt and timely lifesaving actions, the patient is alive today. Kudos to Mr Lim and Mr Lum! On 4 July 2023, the two CFRs were presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. The awards were presented by Lieutenant Colonel Khaisarah Mansor, Head Community Engagement, 4th SCDF Division. You too can help by downloading the SCDFs myResponder app and register as a CFR via the app. Through the app, you can be alerted to nearby emergencies such as a cardiac arrest incident or minor fires that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity. [Road Traffic Accident along SLE]On 2 August 2023 at about 3:20pm, SCDF was alerted to a road traffic accident involving a lorry and a truck along the SLE towards BKE, before the Lentor Avenue exit. Upon SCDF's arrival, a man was found trapped in the driver's seat of the lorry. As the front of the lorry was severely crushed inwards, the man's lower limbs were pinned under the dashboard. An SCDF ambulance crew rendered medical aid to stabilise the man's injuries while rescuers, including officers from the elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART), conducted the rescue operation. To rescue the man, SCDF rescuers used two hydraulic extendable ramps to exert force on the dashboard, pushing it away from him and creating sufficient space to free his lower limbs. Cutting equipment was also used by rescuers to carefully remove the clutch pedal that had trapped the man's left foot.The man was rescued and conveyed to Khoo Teck Puat Hospital.

[Community Visits SCDFs Workplan 2023]As part of SCDFs Workplan Seminar 2023, we were thrilled to welcome members of the public to tour our redeveloped Field Training Area at the Civil Defence Academy over the past two days!Visitors were able to see first-hand our latest training and research facilities which focus on emergency medical services, fire and rescue skillsets, and fire science and research. Apart from trying their hands on mixed-reality technology used to enhance the training of our emergency responders, visitors also got the opportunity to interact with our SCDF officers to find out more about how the new facilities are going to prepare us for future challenges.Among those who visited included our valued community partners such as Grassroots Leaders, Community Emergency and Engagement Committee (C2E) members, students from the National Civil Defence Cadet Corps (NCDCC) and Civil Defence Lionhearter (CDLH) Club, as well as volunteers from our Civil Defence Auxiliary Unit (CDAU).Thank you all for visiting us! We hope that it was an eye-opening experience for all, and we look forward to sharing with you more about SCDF at future opportunities SCDFworkplan2023

[Elevating Training, Learning and Development - SCDF's Workplan Seminar 2023]SCDF's Workplan Seminar (WPS) 2023 was held yesterday (31 Jul), where more than 300 guests were in attendance at the Civil Defence Academy (CDA). Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law graced the event as our Guest-of-Honour. Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development was also present at the WPS, along with representatives from international fire departments. In line with this year's WPS theme of "Elevating Training, Learning and Development", the seminar showcased how we will be preparing our officers for future challenges through our redeveloped Field Training Area (FTA). One of the centrepiece of the FTAs is the National Emergency Medical Services Training Centre, which is built to replicate the real-world pre-hospital emergency care environment. This helps our EMS responders train for diverse emergencies from onsite medical intervention to end-to-end clinical care. The redeveloped FTA also comprises the Fire Research Centre, which is a purpose-built environment for burn testing and enhanced fire modelling capability to aid SCDF in developing improved firefighting techniques. These are two of the seven purpose-built facilities at CDA that will offer enhanced learning and training realism for emergency responders.The third and final phase of CDA's redevelopment will entail the refitting of new fire simulators in our nine-storey furnace building. Phase three is targeted to be ready by next year. SCDFworkplan2023

[Fire @ 61, Geylang Lorong 27]At about 7:30am today, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon SCDF's arrival, fire was raging at the 3rd floor of a shophouse unit. The fire had burnt through the roof and was spreading to the adjacent unit via the rooftop. SCDF deployed 12 emergency vehicles and about 50 firefighters to the incident. At the height of the firefighting operation, four water jets were used to bring the fire under control. About 30 occupants from the neighbouring shophouse units were evacuated by the Police and SCDF. The fire was fully extinguished within an hour and there were no reported injuries. Damping down operation* is ongoing.The cause of fire is under investigation. *Damping down refers to the application of water to wet burnt surfaces immediately after a fire is put out. It is to prevent any potential rekindle of fire from the hot burnt surfaces.

[Fire @ Block 34 Cassia Crescent] At about 12:45pm today, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon SCDF's arrival, black smoke was emitting from a unit on the 2nd floor. SCDF firefighters immediately entered the smoke-logged unit through the front window using a ladder, and the rear entrance via the staircase. The fire which involved the kitchen was extinguished with a water jet. While the firefighting was ongoing, another team of firefighters conducting search of the premises found a person lying on the floor in a bedroom. The person was carried out of the unit to the ground floor. A team of firefighters assessed the person and conducted Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR). An ambulance crew took over the resuscitation efforts and continued with the CPR while enroute to Tan Tock Seng Hospital.About 30 persons from neighbouring units were evacuated by the Police and SCDF as a precautionary measure.The cause of fire is under investigation.

[Exercise Chembridge 2023] Earlier today (26 Jul), SCDF participated in an emergency response exercise at Tuas Second Link. Together with , , Malaysia's Department of Environment and other supporting agencies, this multi-agency exercise simulated a chemical spillage incident as a result of a road traffic accident.
