[Fire @ Blk 618 Bedok Reservoir Road] Early this morning (21 July) at about 3:40am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon SCDF's arrival, black smoke was seen emitting from a unit on the 7th floor. Donned with breathing apparatuses, firefighters quickly entered the smoke-logged unit to fight the fire. The fire, which involved a bedroom and part of the living room, was extinguished by SCDF with a water jet. Due to the intense heat of the fire, the rest of the unit sustained heat and smoke damage. Two persons had evacuated the affected unit before SCDF's arrival. Both were assessed by an SCDF paramedic for smoke inhalation. One of them was conveyed to the Singapore General Hospital and the other declined to be sent to the hospital. About 90 residents from the affected block were evacuated by the Police and SCDF as a precautionary measure. Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire was caused by an electrical origin in the affected bedroom.*Fire Safety Tips:*SCDF would like to remind the public on some good practices to adopt in the household to prevent electrical fires from occurring:a) Never overload electrical outlets with electrical appliances;b) Always switch off electrical appliances when not in use;c) Check the condition of wires regularly. Wires that are frayed or cracked should be replaced or repaired immediately;d) Do not run wires under carpets or mats and keep wires away from hot surfaces;e) Use appliances and electrical plugs bearing the Safety Mark. The categories of appliances can be found at ; f) Do not leave batteries or devices charging unattended for an extended period of time or overnight.

Firefighters from Sengkang Fire Station and Punggol Fire Station immediately conducted forcible entry through the front door to conduct the firefighting and rescue operation. The unit was smoked-logged and the firefighters had to carefully manoeuvre their way into the unit. Five persons (two adults, an infant and two children) were found inside one of the bedrooms and rescued out of the unit by the firefighters. The fire, which involved contents of a kitchen, was extinguished with a water jet. As a result of the intense heat from the fire, the rest of the unit sustained heat and smoke damage. The five persons rescued were conveyed to Singapore General Hospital for smoke inhalation. One of the adults also sustained minor burn injuries.About 50 residents from the affected block were evacuated by the Police and SCDF as a precautionary measure. Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire is likely to have been caused by an electrical origin in the kitchen. ============================Fire Safety Tips:SCDF would like to remind the public on some good practices to adopt in the household to prevent electrical fires from occurring:a) Never overload electrical outlets with electrical appliances;b) Always switch off electrical appliances when not in use;c) Check the condition of wires regularly. *Wires that are frayed or cracked* should be replaced or repaired immediately;d) Do not run wires under carpets or mats and keep wires away from hot surfaces;e) Use appliances and electrical plugs bearing the Safety Mark. The categories of appliances can be found at ; f) Do not leave batteries or devices charging unattended for an extended period of time or overnight.

[Fire @ 124 Pioneer Road]Earlier this morning (17 July) at about 3:30 a.m., SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon SCDFs arrival, the fire had engulfed a large office on the second floor of a building. Additionally, two water jets were set up at the exterior of the building to help contain the fire. The fire was extinguished at about 4:30 a.m.This operation involved the deployment of 13 emergency vehicles and about 50 firefighters. There were no reported injuries.The cause of the fire is under investigation.

[Marine Firefighting Operation @ Southeast of Singapore]Last night (11 July) at about 9:35 p.m., SCDF was alerted to a fire on a vessel anchored off the southeast of Singapore, near Tanah Merah Ferry Terminal.A total of four SCDF marine firefighting and rescue vessels and about 40 marine firefighting specialists from Brani and West Coast Marine Fire Stations were deployed to the incident. Arriving alongside the anchored vessel, the marine firefighting specialists boarded the vessel and using a water jet, they extinguished the fire which was confined to two accommodation decks.Before SCDF's arrival, the vessel's crew had set up three water jets to cool the exterior of the vessel and two water jets to control the fire. Cooling of the vessel's exterior is known as boundary cooling, this helps to reduce the temperature of the vessel's metal structure.After the fire was extinguished, the damping down* operation continued until about 5:00 a.m. today.There were no reported injuries and all crew members of the affected vessel were accounted for. The cause of the fire is under investigation. *Damping down refers to the application of water to wet burnt surfaces immediately after a fire is put out. It is to prevent the potential rekindling of the fire.

[Fire @ Block 508A, Wellington Circle]Earlier this morning at about 1:40 a.m., SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon SCDF's arrival, black smoke was emitting from a unit on the 2nd floor. Firefighters from Yishun Fire Station wearing breathing apparatus equipment entered the smoke-logged unit. The fire, which was confined to a bedroom, was extinguished with a water jet. Four persons from the affected unit had evacuated prior to SCDF's arrival. Two were conveyed by SCDF to Singapore General Hospital for smoke inhalation and burn injuries. About 80 residents from the affected block were evacuated as a precautionary measure.Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire had likely originated from the battery of a power-assisted bicycle (PAB) that was charging in the bedroom.SCDF would like to remind the public on the prevention of PMD/PAB fires, including not to charge batteries for an extended period of time or overnight. Do not purchase or use non-original batteries. See the accompanying infographic for more fire safety tips.

[Two neighbours commended for rendering assistance during a fire] On 20 April 2023, a fire broke out in a 9th floor unit at Block 10 Jalan Batu. Ms Mangacoy Ruffa Mae, who is a caretaker of an elderly lady residing on the 12th floor, saw black smoke issuing out from the affected unit below. She reacted quickly and evacuated the elderly lady to safety by carrying her to the ground floor. Mr Louis Cheong Wen Yang was resting at home when he heard a commotion outside his unit. He rushed out and saw his neighbours unit on fire. Mr Louis immediately alerted his neighbouring units to evacuate and attempted to put out the fire using buckets of water until SCDFs arrival. For their courageous and public-spirited actions, Ms Ruffa Mae and Mr Louis were each awarded the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. You too can make a difference and lend a helping hand to those in need during an emergency. Register as a Community First Responder (CFR) via the SCDFs myResponder app. Through the app, you can be alerted of nearby emergencies such as a cardiac arrest incident or a minor fire that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity. Being trained in basic firefighting, first aid and CPR is useful but not mandatory to qualify as a CFR! Anyone who is willing can do something to help . Everyone counts; every action matters! Find out more about CFR and the myResponder app here: CommunityFirstResponderCommuityLifesaversANationOfLifesaversOurCFRsOurHeroesOurResponseMattersWeMakeSGSecure

[27th Rota Commander Course (RCC) Commissioning Parade]Yesterday, 48 Officer Cadets from the 27th Rota Commander Course (RCC) were commissioned as Senior Officers at the Civil Defence Academy. Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim, Deputy Chairperson, Government Parliamentary Committee (Home Affairs & Law), graced the event as the Guest-of-Honour.The RCC commissioning ceremony is a significant milestone that marks the transition of Officer Cadets into Senior Officers after a 28-week residential course. During the course, the Officer Cadets, comprising both Regular Officers, Full-time National Servicemen as well as international trainees hailing from Bahrain and Vietnam, were equipped with the requisite operational skills and knowledge to perform the role of frontline commanders.The 27th RCC is also the first batch of Officer Cadets to include nine Direct-Entry Paramedic Senior Officers. Prior to joining the 27th RCC, the nine Paramedic Officer Cadets went through a 12-month paramedicine training course at Nanyang Polytechnic and a three month operational attachment at the frontline fire stations. The SCDF Paramedic Senior Officer scheme underscores the transformation of SCDFs Emergency Medical Services (EMS) to meet increasing operational demands while further elevating the service delivery of our EMS to the public.In speaking to the graduating cadets, Mr Zhulkarnain emphasised the importance of leadership, responsibility and upholding high operational standards while carrying out their respective lifesaving roles and responsibilities. [Fire @ Block 308 Hougang Ave 5]Earlier this evening at about 7:30p.m., SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon SCDF's arrival, the fire was raging in a bedroom of a 13th-floor unit. Equipped with breathing apparatus, firefighters from Sengkang Fire Station entered the smoke-logged unit and extinguished the fire with a water jet. As a result of the fire, the rest of the unit also sustained heat and soot damage.An occupant from the affected unit had evacuated prior to SCDF's arrival.As a precautionary measure, about 10 residents from neighbouring units were evacuated by the police.An SCDF paramedic assessed a person from the affected unit for smoke inhalation but the person declined to be conveyed to the hospital. A passerby, who had assisted in the evacuation of residents from the neighbouring units, was also assessed for smoke inhalation and conveyed to Singapore General Hospital. Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire is likely to be caused by an electrical origin from the affected bedroom.SCDF would like to remind the public on good practices to adopt to prevent electrical fires from occurring:a) Do not overload electrical outlets with electrical appliances;b) Always switch off appliances when they are not in use;c) Check the appliance for frayed wires or cracked cords. If observed the appliance should be repaired or replaced. Do not use faulty appliances;d) Do not run wires under carpets or mats and keep wires away from hot surfaces; e) Use appliances and electrical plugs bearing the Safety Mark. The categories of appliances can be found at Do not leave batteries or devices to charge unattended for an extended period of time or overnight.

[Fire @ 260, Kim Keat Avenue]Yesterday night (16 June) around 11.15 p.m., SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon arrival, fire can be seen raging within a closed coffee shop on the first floor. Equipped with breathing apparatus, SCDF firefighters from Bishan Fire Station entered the smoke-logged coffee shop to conduct firefighting. The fire, which involved contents of several stalls inside the coffee shop, was extinguished by SCDF using two water jets. The Pumper Firefighting Machine was also deployed by SCDF for smoke ventilation. No one was inside the coffee shop during the fire. Seven people from a shop unit opposite the coffee shop were evacuated by the police. There were no reported injuries. The cause of fire is under investigation.

[Final Update: Collapsed structure incident along Bernam Street]SCDF officially completed our operation around 8:00 a.m. today. This follows a thorough search throughout the night where SCDF officers combed through the collapsed structure with the assistance of heavy machineries from the construction site, and we can ascertain that there is no other person trapped beneath the debris. We would like to extend our deepest condolences to the family of the worker who passed on yesterday. We would like to thank the SPF, BCA, and MOM for their assistance and close ground coordination which facilitated SCDF's entire search operation.

[Update 3: Collapsed structure incident along Bernam Street]Earlier in the afternoon, all other workers from the worksite had been accounted for, and none of them had reported being injured. Police investigations into the unnatural death of the 20-year-old worker are ongoing.Through review of CCTV footage by SPF and SCDF, there appears to be no other persons trapped under the structure. Nevertheless, the SCDF will continue to work through the night to search the rubble to be certain. The operation will be supported by the deployment of the SCDF's search canines.

[Update 2: Collapsed Structure Incident Along Bernam Street]Following an intensive search operation, a worker who was earlier reported missing, was sighted to be pinned under the collapsed reinforced concrete structure around 1800hrs. The worker had no pulse and breathing. The SCDF immediately conducted cutting and breaking operations to free the casualty. The operation also required the Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) personnel to dig their way through the rubble to create space and assess where parts of the body may have been trapped. This was further complicated due to the weight of the concrete slab which was in excess of 50 tonnes (estimated) as well as mangled scaffolding around the body. The casualty was finally freed after nearly four hours around 2145hrs. He was pronounced dead at the scene by a paramedic. Earlier in the search operation, CCTV footages from the surrounding buildings were obtained by the Police to assist in the assessment of the situation. A fibre optic scope, life detection equipment and search canines were also deployed to detect for signs of life. The operation involved the coordinated use of heavy machinery from the construction site as well as rescue equipment to cut and lift the reinforced concrete slab. 11 SCDF emergency vehicles and about 70 personnel, including rescuers from the DART were deployed at the scene for this operation.

[Update 1: Collapsed Structure Incident @ 1 Bernam Street]SCDF officers from 1st SCDF Division, Marina Bay Fire Station and rescuers from the elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) are currently at scene conducting search operations to locate a worker who was reported missing. Two SCDF search canines have also been deployed to assist in the search in an area of about 20 metres by 10 metres.

[Four Nurses Presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award] On 4 February 2023, two off-duty nurses from , Ms Suraidah Binte Selamat and Ms Norazlin Binte Dawood were travelling along Sumang Walk when they noticed a group of people attending to a man, Mr Lee Chee Hoe, who was lying unconscious on the ground. The duo suspected that Mr Lee was suffering from a cardiac arrest, and immediately carried out Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) on him. Another member of public also assisted to retrieve a nearby AED. Upon receiving the AED, the two nurses administered shocks to Mr Lee using the AED, and continued to administer CPR on him prior to SCDFs arrival. As a result of their prompt actions, Mr Lee Chee Hoe survived. On 17 May 2023, Ms Suraidah and Ms Norazlin were each presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. I am very fortunate that I have been saved and it is like a second chance at life. I feel really blessed and I would like to give a big thank you to all of you. Mr Lee Chee Hoe, cardiac arrest survivor SCDF understands that there are other members of the public who have helped out during the abovementioned incident. We would greatly appreciate if these lifesavers could reach out to us so that we can also recognise their good deeds. In another incident on 3 March 2023, another two off-duty nurses from , Ms Ng Siok Qi and Ms Cherie Koh, rendered medical assistance to a person who felt unwell at Changi Airport Terminal 3. Ms Ng Siok Qi and Ms Cherie Koh were each presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award by COL Chew Keng Tok, Commander, 2nd SCDF Division on 17 May. Being trained in basic firefighting, first aid and CPR is useful but not mandatory to qualify as a Community First Responder (CFR)! Anyone who is willing can do something to help Everyone counts; every action matters! [Abuse of SCDF Frontliners]On 12 February 2023, SCDF responded to a medical case along Hougang Avenue 3. While the paramedic was assessing a male patient at the void deck, he became uncooperative and started hurling vulgarities at the paramedic. Despite attempts to calm the patient down, he became violent and slapped the paramedic on the face. He also kicked the paramedic multiple times before being arrested by the Police. In a separate medical incident on 15 March 2023, a paramedic was assessing a male patient at Kallang Wave Mall when he suddenly turned aggressive and shoved the paramedic against the wall. He was subsequently arrested by the Police. For using criminal force against public servants, the abovementioned perpetrators were sentenced to 14 weeks and 6 weeks imprisonment respectively. These are just two of the 15 reported cases of abuse against our frontliners since January this year.Every emergency call matters to us and we will do our utmost in serving you. However, physical or verbal harassment hinders our emergency responders from carrying out their duties to the best of their ability.Have a heart. Stand with our emergency responders in their mission to protect and save lives and property.ANationOfLifesavers

[Tampines West Community Resilience Day]Yesterday (21 May), more than400 participantsattended the Tampines West Community Resilience (CR) Day.Held at Tampines West Community Centre, the event was graced by Mr Masagos Zulkifli,Minister for Social and Family Development, Second Minister for Health & Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs, Advisor to Tampines Grassroots Organisations (GROs). Jointly organised by 2nd SCDF Division, National Fire and Emergency Preparedness Council (NFEC), Peoples Association, and the Tampines West Community Emergency and Engagement (C2E) Committee, the CR Day aims to impart members of the public with Emergency Preparedness (EP) knowledge and skills. This includes basic firefighting using a fire extinguisher, Improvised First Aid Skills (IFAS), administering Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), and using an Automated External Defibrillator (AED).During the event, Mr Masagos also presented three members of the public with the Community First Responder Award and five members of the public with the Community Lifesaver Award. Their quick thinking and willingness to step forward and render help to others during an emergency is truly commendable.Don't fret if you have missed this CR Day, members of the public are strongly encouraged to join us at our next CR Day on 28 May 2023, at 175A, Lompang Road. Apart from the CR Day, the public can also learn essential EP knowledge and skills through SCDFs Community Emergency Preparedness Programme (CEPP) and register as a Community First Responder (CFR) via SCDFs myResponder app.Register for the CEPP through the link in our bio and join us towards building ANationofLifesavers!

[Fire @ Block 511 West Coast Drive]At about 11:15 p.m. yesterday (20 May), SCDF was alerted to a fire in a 12th floor unit at the abovementioned location.The fire, which involved the contents of a bedroom, was extinguished by firefighters from Clementi Fire Station using a water jet.Six occupants from the affected unit evacuated prior to SCDFs arrival. There were no reported injuries.Approximately 160 residents from the block had evacuated prior to SCDFs arrival. Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire had likely originated from the battery pack of a Power Assisted Bicycle (PAB) which was charging in the bedroom.SCDF would like to remind the public on the prevention of PMD/PAB fires, including not charging batteries for an extended period of time or overnight. Do not purchase or use non-original batteries. See the accompanying infographic for more fire safety tips.

[Four Gurkha Contingent Officers Commended for Saving the Life of a Cardiac Arrest Victim] On 25 Mar 2023, at about 11:30 a.m., four officers from Gurkha Contingent (GC) of the were driving in the vicinity of Woodlands Industrial Park, where they saw a man lying motionless by the roadside of Woodlands Industrial Park D Street 1. Team Leader Senior Staff Sergeant (SSS) Man Kumar Limbu and Operator Corporal (CPL) Dinesh Limbu quickly approached the unconscious man and found him in a state of cardiac arrest. SSS Man Kumar immediately called for an ambulance and directed CPL Dinesh and Operator CPL Jeevan Gharti Magar to perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) on the man. At the same time, Deputy Team Leader Sergeant (SGT) Sabin Gurung managed the oncoming traffic for the safety of the man and the officers rendering CPR. The officers continued with the CPR on the unconscious man until the arrival of an SCDF ambulance. As a result of the prompt and timely lifesaving actions by the GC officers, the man is recovering well today. Yesterday (17 May), the four officers were each presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. The awards were presented by Colonel Goh Boon Han, Commander, 4th SCDF Division. You too can help by downloading the SCDFs myResponder app and register as a Community First Responder (CFR) via the app. Through the app, you can be alerted of nearby emergencies such as a cardiac arrest incident or minor fires that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity. [Rescue 995 Honouring and Remembering SCDFs Fallen Heroes]As SCDF commemorated International Firefighters Day on 4th May 2023, SCDF personnel force-wide wore red and blue ribbons on their left chest, honouring the courage, commitment and sacrifices of firefighters and emergency medical personnel worldwide. These personnel put their lives on the line to protect us, our families and our homes.They are more than just firefighters and paramedics; they are our neighbours, friends and family, who step forward in times of danger, turning chaos into calm, replacing fear with hope.Rescue 995 joins SCDF in observing a moment of silence to honour the unwavering dedication of our emergency responders and those who have fallen in the line of duty. They may no longer be with us, but their sacrifices will never be forgotten. We also present a poem from Ms A. B. Goh, a teacher of the late SGT1 Edward H Go, as a moving tribute to her former student.Read more on the story through the link in our bio. [An 8-minute read]

[SCDF Participates in SG Clean Day] More than 200 SCDF officers from HQ SCDF, Civil Defence Academy, and SCDFs Land and Marine Division HQs participated in the Largest Clean Up Event earlier today (13 May), held in conjunction with the annual Keep Clean, Singapore! (KCS) launch at the F1 Pit Building. Organised by the Public Hygiene Council, this is the first time SCDF has participated in this event. Ms Denise Phua, Mayor for Central District Singapore and Member of Parliament for Jalan Besar GRC, graced the Largest Clean-Up Event where she thanked the supporting partners, various community groups and organisations for their participation. Here in SCDF, we are committed towards a liveable and sustainable environment for all. We are glad to have played a part in the largest island-wide clean-up. Lets all continue to uphold higher standards of hygiene and cleanliness in Singapore! SGCleanDay

[Memorandum of Understanding between SCDF and SIT]Earlier today (12 May), a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Singapore Civil Defence Force and Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT) was signed. The MoU was signed by Assistant Commissioner (AC) Francis Ng, Director of Training & Professional Development Department, SCDF and Mr Bernard Nee, Deputy President (Industry & Community), SIT.The MoU provides a collaborative framework for SCDF and SIT to pursue research projects and develop training courses in industrial fire safety. The SIT Electrical Safety Symposium held in January 2023 had embarked on the professional exchanges between SCDF and SIT to benefit the larger community of practice that pursues industrial fire safety.AC Francis Ng, Director of Training & Professional Development Department, SCDF, shared that building strategic partnerships with valued partners remains one of SCDFs top priorities. "The signing of this MoU represents our commitment to growth, progress and excellence, and provides a collaborative framework to leverage our unique strengths, expertise, and resources to achieve shared goals.The SCDFs Fire Research Centre located in the Civil Defence Academy would be commissioned in mid-2023 to provide a state-of-the-art facility for research and development for fire science and fire safety. The MoU will facilitate mutual benefitting projects to enhance the knowledge capacity of both organisations and elevate overall industrial fire safety standards in Singapore.

[Fire @ Blk 303 Woodlands Street 31]On 8 May 2023 at about 2:50 p.m., SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location. The fire, which involved the contents of a bedroom in a fourth-floor unit, was extinguished by firefighters from Woodlands Fire Station using a water jet. Three occupants from the affected unit evacuated prior to SCDFs arrival. A cat was found in the living room of the affected unit by SCDF firefighters and brought out to safety.About 30 residents from the affected block were evacuated by the Police as a precautionary measure.A person from the affected block was assessed by an SCDF paramedic for breathlessness and conveyed to Khoo Teck Puat Hospital. The cause of fire is under investigation.

[Unveiling of Memorial Garden at Civil Defence Heritage Gallery]An outdoor Memorial Garden paying tribute to SCDF officers who lost their lives in the line of duty was unveiled at the Civil Defence Heritage Gallery this evening. A lighted black marble rectangular monument with a flowing water feature serves as the centrepiece of the Memorial Garden. It depicts the innate character of emergency responders - Strength, Courage, and Purity, and it symbolises the brave sacrifice and selfless nature of our fallen heroes. As a lasting tribute for their sacrifices, the names of our late firefighters SGT Shaik Amran Bin Shaik Jamal and SGT1 Edward H Go are inscribed on the marble stone column. SGT Shaik passed away in a road traffic accident while responding to a case of fire in January 2006 while SGT1 Edward lost his life during a firefighting operation in December 2022. The family members of SGT1 Edward were present at the unveiling of the Memorial Garden earlier this evening. The family of SGT Shaik was unable to attend the ceremony and will be visiting the Memorial Garden on another day. The solemn occasion was witnessed by Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law. During the unveiling of the monument, Minister Shanmugam shared that the Memorial Garden represents our gratitude and memory of these officers who lost their lives in the line of duty, and is a physical testament that we have not forgotten and will never forget them. The Memorial Garden is open to members of the public when they visit the Civil Defence Heritage Gallery.

[SCDF Commemorates International Firefighters' Day]Today (4 May) is International Firefighters Day (IFFD).It is a day where we recognise and honour the sacrifices made by the global fraternity of firefighters and emergency medical personnel as they selflessly go about their daily duties responding to emergencies, saving lives and property.This morning, all SCDF personnel across HQ SCDF, Civil Defence Academy, SCDFs Land and Marine Division HQs, and emergency responders at the fire stations and fire posts, donned a red and blue ribbon, and stood in solidarity to commemorate IFFD. The ribbon colours symbolise fire and water respectively, and are also internationally associated with the emergency services across the globe.Commanders of the frontline units read out a message to their personnel during an observance ceremony held this morning to mark IFFD where they remembered the late SGT Shaik Amran Bin Shaik Jamal and SGT1 Edward H Go. SGT Shaik passed away in a road traffic accident while responding to an incident in January 2006, while SGT1 Edward lost his life during a firefighting operation in December 2022.Every day, our firefighters and paramedics put their lives on the line to keep Singapore safe. To all our lifesavers, both past and present, thank you for your dedication to duty.InternationalFirefightersDayTheLifeSavingForce

[SCDF Conferred Medal of Appreciation by the Republic of Trkiye]Earlier this evening, SCDF was conferred the Medal of Appreciation by the Vice President of the Republic of Trkiye, H.E. Fuat Oktay. The Medal of Appreciation is in recognition of SCDFs search and rescue efforts following an earthquake in Trkiye in February 2023. Two days after the devastating earthquake, a 68-member Operation Lionheart Contingent comprising rescuers from the elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART), paramedic and medical specialists, search specialists and operation support officers were deployed in two waves. LTC Lok Wee Keong, DART Commander, represented SCDF to receive the award at the Presidency of the Republic of Trkiye in Ankara, Trkiye. COMR Eric Yap, Commissioner SCDF expressed his appreciation for the recognition by the Republic of Trkiye. "The SCDF is honoured to be conferred with the Medal of Appreciation from the Vice President of the Republic of Trkiye, H.E. Fuat Oktay. The medal recognises the search and rescue efforts by SCDFs Operation Lionheart Contingent that was deployed to Trkiye in February this year as part of Singapores humanitarian assistance and disaster relief efforts. The SCDF values the strong friendship and bonds forged with our Trkiye counterparts during the deployment. The people of Trkiye have demonstrated admirable resilience and fortitude, and we are confident they would emerge much stronger as they rebuild their lives and homes." - Commissioner Eric Yap, Commissioner SCDF

[Earth Day 2023]In addition to the celebrations of Hari Raya Puasa, today happens to be Earth Day as well! Earth Day is an annual event on 22 April to raise awareness and demonstrate support for environmental protection. This global movement brings people from all walks of life together to advance sustainability and climate action.Here in the Life Saving Force, we are committed to building a sustainable and equitable future for our planet. In addition to reducing plastic waste and organising clean ups of our waterways, SCDF has also actively collaborated with other organisations to upcycle our equipment and give them a new lease of life.Check out our initiatives here! EarthDay2023ANationofLifesaversPic 1: AC Wesley Ho, Director Logistics Department, SCDF (left) with Jane Neo, Animal Care Specialist, RWS S.E.A. Aquarium (right) during the delivery of the firefighting hoses to RWS S.E.A. Aquarium. SCDF's fire fighting hoses which are no longer serviceable given a new lease of life at .e.a.aquarium where they will soon be repurposed into "furniture" and enrichment devices for animals Pic 2: Through a collaboration with SCDF's fire fighting hoses which are no longer serviceable are repurposed into fences for allotment gardens or protection for newly replanted trees at Coney Island. Pic 3: SCDF's upcycling efforts are on display at a showcase booth till end June in the newly opened Punggol Regional Library. Go check it out and learn more!

[Rescue 995 Beyond the Call of Duty]On 14 April 2023, over 400 guests, including SCDF officers, volunteers, and strategic partners gathered to commemorate SCDF Day 2023, which marks the 1989 merger of Singapore Fire Service & SCDF. President Halimah Yacob graced the event and thanked SCDF officers for their commitment to duty and service to the public. Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs & for Law was also in attendance and in his speech, he expressed thanks for the commitment and service of SCDF officers, including thanking SCDF strategic partners and volunteers for supporting SCDF in its lifesaving mission. Rescue 995 spoke to CPT Jadyn Toh, LTC (NS) Marcus Lee and SGT(2) Andrew Chua who were among the 102 outstanding SCDF officers recognised for their dedication and commitment to duty. Read more on their story through the link in our bio. [A 7-minute read]

[SCDF Day @ The Istana] In commemoration of SCDF Day 2023, a Garden Reception was held earlier this evening at The Istana.Celebrated annually on 15 April, SCDF Day recognises the integration of the Singapore Fire Service and SCDF 34 years ago, and celebrates the significant milestones achieved by SCDF over the years.The SCDF Garden Reception was graced by President Halimah Yacob. Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law, together with more than 400 SCDF officers, SCDFs strategic partners and volunteers, and officers from the Minister of Home Affairs, were also present at this momentous event. In his opening address, Minister Shanmugam thanked all SCDF officers for their unwavering dedication to the Life Saving mission. He also reaffirmed the importance of our collective commitment to a safe and secure Singapore, and expressed his confidence in SCDF's operational capabilities. 16 awards were presented by Minister Shanmugam during the Reception to recognise the exemplary performance of SCDF officers who have gone beyond the call of duty and have embodied the SCDFs core values of Pride and Care. These recipients comprised Regulars, Full-time National Servicemen (NSF), and Operationally Ready National Servicemen (NSmen).During the Reception, President Halimah Yacob interacted with some of the award recipients, NSmen, SCDFs strategic partners and volunteers, as well as SCDFs Operation Lionheart contingent which was deployed to Trkiye for disaster relief efforts in February 2023. SCDF has come a long way since its founding years. As we give recognition to our SCDF officers today, we also reaffirm our dedication to our Life Saving mission, and will remain committed to our Transformation journey towards ANationOfLifesavers.PrideandCare OurPeopleOurPride

These recipients comprised Regulars, Full-time National Servicemen (NSF), and Operationally Ready National Servicemen (NSmen).During the Reception, President Halimah Yacob interacted with some of the award recipients, NSmen, SCDFs strategic partners and volunteers, as well as SCDFs Operation Lionheart contingent which was deployed to Trkiye for disaster relief efforts in February 2023. [Resident Puts Out Kitchen Stove Fire] On 6 Mar 2023, at about 5:15 p.m., Mr Bryan Toh was washing his car at the outdoor carpark of his condominium along Cashew Road when he noticed smoke coming out of a unit on the ground floor. Mr Bryan went to investigate and noticed that the kitchen stove in the unit was on fire. Springing into action, he alerted the neighbouring units to evacuate and called 995. He then rushed back to his car to get his domestic water hose, which he connected to a water tap, about 20 meters away from the affected unit and fought the fire. Mr Bryan successfully extinguished the fire before SCDFs arrival and there were no reported casualties. Kudos to Mr Bryan! On 3 Apr 2023, Mr Bryan was presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award for his prompt and timely actions. The award was presented by COL Goh Boon Han, Commander, 4th SCDF Division. You too can help by downloading SCDFs myResponder app and register as a Community First Responder via the app. Through the app, you can be alerted to nearby emergencies such as a cardiac arrest incident or a minor fire that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity. [Memorandum of Understanding between DFES and SCDF]Earlier this week, a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) was signed between the Department of Fire and Emergency Services (DFES), Western Australia, and SCDF at the Civil Defence Academy.The MOU signing ceremony was witnessed by Hon. Minister Stephen Dawson MLC, Minister for Emergency Services, Western Australia, and Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS) for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development. This MOU signing marks our continued partnership with DFES, where it was first established in 2005. The MOU aims to facilitate the sharing of information and ideas on the delivery of firefighting and emergency services. It also encourages the exchange of knowledge and expertise on Urban Search and Rescue (USAR), and Chemical, Biological and Radiological (CBR) threats. With this MOU, it also reaffirms our partnership with DFES through the attachment of officers for professional and personal development.We look forward to the close collaboration with DFES as both agencies work towards our shared mission of protecting and saving lives and property! Photos 1-4: LCP Muhammad Syukri B Mohd Salim, SCDF Corporate Communications Department Photos 5-8: LCP Goh Rhy Yan, Civil Defence Academy

[Exercise Northstar XI @ Jurong Island] Earlier today, Exercise Northstar XI (XNS11) was held at Jurong Island to validate multi-agency emergency response plans and hone coordination among national agencies. More than 300 personnel from SCDF, various key government agencies and industry partners participated in the exercise. The XNS11 began with an armed adversary scenario and a sea interdiction response, where the perpetrators were jointly neutralised by SAFs Island Defence Task Force and SPFs Ground Response Force, Emergency Response Team, and Police Coast Guard. Albeit that the perpetrators were neutralised, improvised explosive devices planted on Jurong Island were detonated remotely causing a chemical pipeline rupture and two oil tank fires. These scenarios were mitigated with the response of SCDF resources, among which were the HazMat Control Vehicle, HazMat Mitigation Vehicle, and SCDFs latest Modular Oil Tank Firefighting System. Mr Lee Hsien Loong, Prime Minister (PM) of Singapore, together with Cabinet members, were present to observe the exercise. In speaking to the media after the exercise, PM Lee reaffirmed the importance of inter-agency response during major emergencies to safeguard Singapores national security. In pursuing our shared mission of a safe and secure Singapore, XNS11 was an enriching opportunity for SCDF to work alongside other agencies to test and validate the Whole-of-Government response framework in the event of major crises and potential threat scenarios. Check out the photos to see what transpired during XNS11!XNS11ANationofLifesavers

[Final update: Height Rescue Operation @ No. 168, Robinson Rd]Earlier this afternoon, at about 1:40 p.m., SCDF was activated for a height rescue incident involving two workers who were stranded on a gondola which was stuck at the 40th floor of the abovementioned location.SCDF firefighters from Marina Bay Fire Station were the first to arrive and proceeded to the 41st floor to assess the gondola's stability and the condition of the two workers. SCDFs elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) was also activated and set up their height rescue system on the rooftop. Rescue ropes were lowered to a platform on the 41st floor where DART mounted the rescue operation from.A DART specialist descended onto the gondola and secured the first worker before hoisting him up to safety on the 41st floor. The second worker who had difficulty moving, was secured onto a rescue stretcher and brought up safely to the 41st floor.Both workers were assessed by an SCDF paramedic and conveyed to the Singapore General Hospital.

[Memorandum of Understanding between BASARNAS and SCDF]Earlier today, a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) was signed between the National Search and Rescue Agency (BASARNAS) of Indonesia and SCDF.This MOU was one of several MOUs signed at the Singapore-Indonesia Leaders Retreat held at the Istana, where Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong met Indonesian President Joko Widodo, and reaffirmed the excellent state of relations between Singapore and Indonesia.The signing of the MOU between BASARNAS and SCDF was represented by Air Marshal Henri Alfiandi, Head of the National Search and Rescue Agency, and COMR Eric Yap, Commissioner SCDF.Under the MOU, both agencies will explore new areas of collaboration and growth opportunities, including Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) capacity building, exchange of knowledge and expertise in USAR, as well as provision of mutual assistance in the event of a natural disaster.Todays signing marks yet another milestone in the partnership between BASARNAS and SCDF. We look forward to this MOU paving the way for more collaborations in the future as we work towards our common goal of saving lives.Pictured from L to R: Indonesian President Joko Widodo, Air Marshal Henri Alfiandi, Head of the National Search and Rescue Agency, COMR Eric Yap, Commissioner SCDF, and Prime Minister Lee Hsien LoongPhoto credits: Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI)

[Lifesavers on the Move] Since 2015, SCDF has been galvanising the business community from the transport, logistics and courier industries to support and participate in the SCDF AED-on-Wheels programme - an important component of the SCDFs Save-A-Life initiative. Yesterday (13 March), we welcomed our latest partner - SingPost. To date, this programme has a membership of 310 participants, comprising private hire drivers, drivers from the logistics and courier service industry, such as Strides Taxi, Grab, ComfortDelGro and Ninja Van, as well as drivers from the general community. With SingPost joining the programme, there will be more AED equipped vehicles. Providers from the logistics and courier service industry have an extensive presence on our roads and hence they can play a critical life-saving role in our community while plying the roads. The participants under the AED-on-Wheels programme are also registered Community First Responders (CFRs). As CFRs, they are trained in basic firefighting, first aid, cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and the use of AED under the SCDFs Community Emergency Preparedness Programme. When alerted of cardiac arrests cases via the SCDFs myResponder App, drivers in the vicinity can proceed to the scene, perform CPR and administer AED on the cardiac arrest victim thereby improving the chances of survival. SCDF is grateful to the public, stakeholders and partners in supporting our mission of protecting and saving lives and property. We will endeavour to grow and expand the various community partnership programmes, including the AED-on-Wheels programme further! [Final Update: Fire @ 28, Tuas South Avenue 8]At about 6:15 p.m. yesterday (13 March), SCDF was alerted to a fire at the above location. The fire, the size of about one and a half football fields, had engulfed an industrial building consisting of warehouse and production areas, including a six-storey production unit. The fire involved chemical solvents and flammable construction materials. A total of 26 emergency vehicles and about 80 personnel were deployed for this incident. At the height of the firefighting operation, SCDF firefighters deployed eight water jets and an Unmanned Firefighting Machine. The fire was brought under control at about 8:15 p.m. Earlier in the evening, two workers were assessed by an SCDF paramedic for blisters on the hands and forehead respectively. They refused conveyance to the hospital. There were no other reported persons who had sustained injuries. The firefighting operation is still ongoing. Once the fire has been extinguished, firefighters will remain at the site to damp down* the affected areas with water. *Damp down refers to the application of water to wet burnt surfaces immediately after a fire is put out. It is to prevent the potential rekindling of the fire.

[Six Migrant Workers Commended for Assisting in a Road Traffic Accident]You may have read recently on the newspapers that on 1 Nov 2022 at about 2:45 p.m., an accident occurred at a carpark in Yishun, where six migrant workers stepped forward to lift a car to rescue Ms Kaelyn Ho who was trapped underneath it.Yesterday (6 Mar), Mr Mohammad Abuhaiat Nurnobi, Mr Miah Eadhu, Mr Alam Jahangir, Mr Molla Mohammad Sayem, Mr Belal Mohammad Shababuddin and Mr Khobir were presented SCDF Community Lifesaver Awards by COL Lim Beng Hui, Commander, 3rd SCDF Division. Expressing her gratitude at the ceremony, Mdm Lim Xiaoli, the mother of Ms Kaelyn, said, Im very glad we are able to recognise them for their brave acts in helping my daughter that day. They are truly deserving of our admiration and respect. Thank you to everyone from the bottom of my heart.COL Lim Beng Hui said, We are moved by such acts of selflessness and courage. This is the spirit of community first response. Kudos to these six brave gentlemen for being excellent examples of community first responders where their actions made all the difference before SCDFs arrival.CommunityFirstResponderCommunityLifesaversANationOfLifesaversOurCFRsOurHeroesOurResponseMattersWeMakeSGSecure

[National Civil Defence Cadet Corps Precision Drill Challenge 2023]On 25 February 2023, 24 schools participated in the annual National Civil Defence Cadet Corps (NCDCC) Precision Drill Challenge (PDC) at the Home Team Academy.Organised by HQ NCDCC, the annual PDC has seen growing number of teams participating year-on-year. The PDC provides a platform for the cadets to showcase self-choreographed precision drill sequences that display creativity, precision and sharpness. The PDC also fosters resilience, discipline and camaraderie among the cadets.With their carefully choreographed yet innovative drill sequences, Kuo Chuan Presbyterian Secondary School emerged as the overall champion in the 2023's PDC! Their efforts have not gone unnoticed after months of training and preparation.We would like to thank all the participating teams in contributing to the success of the event, and we look forward to your zealous participation in the next PDC!

[International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) Team Leaders and Working Groups Meeting 2023]The annual International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) Team Leaders and Working Groups Meeting 2023 was hosted in Singapore this year, from 28 February to 2 March 2023. Co-organised by the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) and SCDF, more than 100 participants from 46 countries gathered at the Civil Defence Academy to assess the operational capabilities of international Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) response.The opening remarks were delivered by AC Michael Chua, Director Operations, SCDF, Mr Murat Kozluklu, First Secretary, Embassy of the Republic of Trkiye, and Mr Winston Chang, INSARAG Secretariat Worldwide, Emergency Response Section, OCHA Geneva. In their remarks, they reaffirmed the importance of a coordinated USAR response and expressed their gratitude to the Team Leadersand Working Groupsfor their dedication and commitment to the INSARAG mission. COL Mehmet Baykal from the Embassy of the Republic of Trkiye also graced the event.With the recent Trkiye-Syria earthquake, this year's meeting was particularly significant as it exemplified the importance of USAR response capabilities globally in times of need. Notwithstanding the devastating impact of the earthquake, coordinated efforts from the Team Leadersand Working Groupsenabled the quick deployment of international USAR teams to render assistance to the local communities in Trkiye and Syria.To strengthen the coordination and effectiveness of international USAR response, the INSARAG Team Leadersand Working Groupsparticipated in constructive discussions to evaluate their response in an ever-evolving landscape. They also discussed training matters based on lessons gleaned from previous USAR operations and exercises.We look forward to our continued partnership with the INSARAG network and stand ever ready to contribute to the international search and rescue community when called upon.

Co-organised by the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) and SCDF, more than 100 participants from 46 countries gathered at the Civil Defence Academy to assess the operational capabilities of international Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) response.The opening remarks were delivered by AC Michael Chua, Director Operations, SCDF, Mr Murat Kozluklu, First Secretary, Embassy of the Republic of Trkiye, and Mr Winston Chang, INSARAG Secretariat Worldwide, Emergency Response Section, OCHA Geneva. [Two members of public commended for putting out fires in the neighbourhood] On 30 Jan 2023 at about 3:30 a.m., Mr Syamil Uwayis Bin Zainal Abas was resting at home when he received an alert through the SCDF myResponder app for a fire at Block 488A Choa Chu Kang Avenue 5. Mr Syamil proceeded to the Block and saw smoke coming out of the centralised rubbish chute at the ground floor. Without hesitation, he called 995 and proceeded to extinguish the fire with a fire extinguisher that was in the centralised rubbish chute room. In a separate incident on 10 Feb 2023 at about 5:20 p.m., Mr Raymond Lim Koon Siang was on his way to fetch his child from school when he saw smoke coming out from a 2nd floor unit at Block 663 Choa Chu Kang Crescent. Instinctively, Mr Raymond dashed to retrieve a fire extinguisher from his truck which was parked nearby, and rushed to the affected unit. He entered the unit and extinguished the fire involving the kitchen stove and cabinet. Yesterday (28 Feb), the two members of public were presented with the SCDF Community First Responder Award for their civic-minded actions. The awards were presented by COL Bob Tan, Deputy Director, Volunteer and Community Partnership Department. You too can help by downloading the SCDFs myResponder app and register as a Community First Responder via the app. Through the app, you can be alerted to nearby emergencies such as a cardiac arrest incident or minor fires that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity. [SCDF Volunteers at the Singapore Red Cross Fundraising Pumpathon 2023] Jointly organised by SCDF and the Singapore Red Cross (SRC), a 10-hour long Pumpathon was held at Shaw Centre today to aid disaster victims in the aftermath of the Trkiye-Syria earthquake. From 11 a.m. to 9 p.m, more than 50 SCDF Volunteers from the Civil Defence Lionhearter Club, National Civil Defence Cadet Corps and Civil Defence Auxiliary Unit pumped six water filtration devices for 10 hours continuously to garner public support and raise funds for the earthquake victims in Trkiye and Syria. This event was especially meaningful as it simulated what displaced populations in disaster stricken areas had to go through to obtain access to clean water.Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS) for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, and Associate Professor Ho Peng Kee, Chairman/Home Team Volunteer Network, Ministry of Home Affairs, graced the event and showed their support to the volunteers. His Excellency, Mr Mehmet Burin Gnenli, Turkish Ambassador to Singapore, also attended the event and expressed his appreciation to the volunteers for their hard work. Together, we can all make a difference to the earthquake victims in times of need.

[Update 16: SCDF's Operation Lionheart Homecoming] On 8 February 2023, SCDF deployed the Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent to Trkiye to assist in disaster rescue efforts in the aftermath of the Trkiye-Syria earthquake. The OLH contingent, comprising 68 members and four canines, had safely returned to Singapore early this morning (18 Feb). The contingent members were received by Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law, Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS) for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, and His Excellency Mehmet Burin Gnenli, Turkish Ambassador to Singapore at Changi Airport. Families and loved ones were also present to warmly welcome them home.In his welcome address, Minister Shanmugam commended the OLH contingent for their unwavering efforts in conducting extensive search and rescue operations across multiple rescue sites in Trkiye. He also expressed his appreciation and gratitude to the families and loved ones for supporting the contingent members during their 10-day deployment. On behalf of Trkiye, His Excellency Mehmet Burin Gnenli thanked the OLH contingent for rendering assistance to the communities affected by the earthquake. He also acknowledged the contingent members for carrying out a safe and successful mission. To our Lifesavers, thank you for your commitment and dedication to service. Welcome home! SCDF would like to express our appreciation to Singapore Embassy in Ankara and the stanbul Airport for the assistance rendered to the OLH contingents deployment in Trkiye. We would also like to thank Singapore Airlines, Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore, Changi Airport Group, and Turkish Airlines for facilitating the contingents flight and logistical arrangements on short notice. The help that has been provided to us has been pivotal in supporting the OLH contingents deployment to, and return from Trkiye.

[Update 14: Standing down of Operation Lionheart]As Operation Lionheart (OLH) draws to a close, the 68-member contingent is preparing to depart from Trkiye later today (17 Feb). A few days prior to the departure, the OLH contingent met with the Trkiye National Medical Rescue Team, otherwise known as the Ulusal Medikal Kurtarma Ekibi (UMKE). The UMKE specialises in medical disaster relief and has been rendering assistance to Trkiye following the massive earthquake. During the meeting, the OLH contingent contributed medical supplies such as trauma equipment and medical drugs, as well as other necessities like food rations, thermal wear and tents.Ambassador Jonathan Tow, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Republic of Singapore to the Republic of Trkiye also visited the OLH contingent at their Base of Operation as the OLH contingent were making preparations to stand down. The Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) suit worn by the OLH contingent represents an important element of identity among us and our commitment to saving lives. The USAR suits were presented to the locals as a gesture of our friendship and solidarity with them as they move forward to rebuild their lives following this devastating earthquake. Although the OLH contingent is leaving Trkiye, the people of Trkiye will always be in our hearts and minds

[Update 13: SCDF's Operation Lionheart Psychological Team]A disaster can trigger critical stress. This can come in the form of emotional, mental or physical exhaustion, which can potentially be traumatic to responders who are deployed to disaster sites to undertake rescue operations.For the first time, two officers from the SCDFs Emergency Behavioural Sciences and Care unit (EBSC) formed part of the Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent to provide in-situ psychological support to its responders.They monitor the contingent members morale and psychological well-being, and ensure the overall psychological readiness of rescuers during the deployment. These officers help enable appropriate and timely psychological intervention when required.Meet Home Team Specialist (HTS) Khoo Swee Giang, Lead Psychologist and LTA Khoo Chong Wee, Emergency Readiness Officer from SCDFs EBSC unit.

[Update 12: SCDF's Operation Lionheart Technician Team]Working quietly behind the scenes during the deployment are Mr Suhaimi Bin Daed and Mr Nurhadi Bin Eeban. The two technical specialists are from HTX (Home Team Science and Technology Agency) and are assigned to SCDFs Equipment Maintenance Branch.Highly specialised in multi-disciplinary engineering and technical skills, the dynamic duo plays a critical role in ensuring that all Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) equipment used by the rescuers are operating in tip-top condition and ready for deployment. All equipment at the Base of Operation (BoO) such as portable power generators and lighting systems are also maintained by this technical team. During prolonged rescues, Mr Suhaimi and Mr Nurhadi can provide the necessary technical support to the contingent at the rescue site. We thank for their contribution to Operation Lionheart (OLH), working hand in hand with SCDF.

[Update 11: SCDFs Operation Lionheart Medical Team]As part of the Operation Lionheart contingent, two Full-time National Servicemen (NSF) doctors and four paramedics are deployed with the contingent to provide medical coverage.Experienced in responding to medical emergencies, our team of paramedics are adept at providing immediate pre-hospital medical care to casualties at rescue sites. In addition, the two doctors are trained in advanced trauma life support and would augment the medical care provided at the incident site by our paramedics.The medical team has been coordinating efforts to provide the best possible care to those in need, including treating minor ailments and injuries sustained by our rescuers.

[Update 10: SCDFs Search Platoon at Operation Lionheart]As part of the Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent, search specialists and four canines from SCDFs search platoon are deployed together with DART rescuers to conduct search and rescue operations at potential rescue sites.Highly intelligent, SCDFs search canines have the aptitude for searching for survivors in the rubble of collapsed buildings. With a keen sense of smell, they are trained to search confined spaces in collapsed building structures.To ensure the well-being of our four search canines, a series of measures are in place to ensure that they receive the best care during the deployment. This includes housing them in climate-controlled cargo holds during their flight, taking them on walks for playtime, providing them a nutritious diet and giving them a wipe-down at the end of the day to keep them clean. The search canines also have their own thermal jackets and blankets to keep them warm. In addition, the two medical doctors with the OLH contingent are also trained in basic canine care.Meet Timmy, Jack, Rizzo and Frenchy.

The SCDF annual statistics for Emergency Medical Services (EMS), Fire Incidents and Fire Safety Enforcement for Year 2022 were released today. In a nutshell: 1. The total number of EMS calls increased by 20.2% in 2022. There was an increase of 20.2% and 27.5% in emergency and non-emergency calls respectively, due in part to the multiple COVID-19 waves of infection. 2. SCDF responded to 1,799 fires in 2022, a slight decline of 2.4% or 45 fire incidents from 1,844 in 2021. There were 935 fires in residential buildings (private and public), accounting for 52.0% of the total fire calls in 2022. 3. Fires caused by unattended cooking and electrical origins remained the leading causes of fires in residential buildings in 2022, accounting for 37% and 24% of fires in residential buildings respectively. 4. SCDF stepped up the number of fire safety enforcement checks in 2022 with the easing of COVID-19 restrictions and resumption of business activities. SCDF conducted a total of 12,792 fire safety enforcement checks, an increase of 15.5% from 11,075 in 2021.More useful information on fire safety can be found in the latest edition of the Civil Defence Emergency Handbook. The handbook can be found in the link on our bio and on the myResponder app, available in English, Mandarin, Malay and Tamil.

[Update 7: Operation Lionheart Base of Operations in Kahramanmara]Following the arrival of the second Operation Lionheart (OLH) team in Adana, Trkiye on 10 Feb, the OLH Base of Operation (BoO) in Kahramanmara was expanded to accommodate the full 68-member OLH contingent.Over the last 24 hours, two teams from the OLH contingent were deployed at two different sectors in the city centre. Located about 13 km from the BoO, both teams conducted assessments and identified potential rescue sites. Each team comprised eight officers from DART, two search specialists with their canines, one paramedic and two support officers. USAR life detection equipment were also deployed to locate possible casualties for these sector assessments. A total of seven sites were assessed and both teams returned back to the BoO after the OLH contingents assistance were no longer required.

[Update 5: Joint Rescue Operation at Kanldere Cd., Dulkadirolu/Kahramanmara, Trkiye]Yesterday at about 8 p.m. (10 Feb, 1 a.m., Singapore time), the advance team from SCDFs Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent was dispatched together with the Local Emergency Management Agency (LEMA) to conduct a search and rescue operation at Kanldere Cd., after reports of faint calls for help were heard coming from a semi-collapse 2-storey building.Upon arrival at the location, five elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) personnel and a paramedic worked closely with LEMA to conduct the search and rescue operation.After ensuring the stability of the semi-collapsed building, LEMA and SCDF accessed the second floor through the back of the building where the faint calls were heard. SCDF used a fibre-optic scope and confirmed that a man was trapped behind a large concrete slab. LEMA then used breaking equipment to create an opening. The man was rescued within half an hour.Throughout this operation, LEMA and SCDF were in constant contact with the trapped man. He was brought down from the building and was attended to by the locals.

[Update 4: SCDF Deploys Second Team to Trkiye]A second team, comprising 48 SCDF personnel and four canines from SCDF's K-9 unit, will depart for Adana, Trkiye at about 2 a.m. tomorrow morning (10 Feb). This team will augment the 20-member advance team that was deployed earlier this week. The 68-member strong Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent will give more scope, scale and capacity to carry out sustained and prolonged Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) operations within affected areas. To support the contingents enhanced USAR operations, additional search and rescue equipment, medical supplies, and communications and logistics support equipment, will also be brought along. The contingent was sent off by His Excellency Mehmet Burin Gnenli, Turkish Ambassador to Singapore, and Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, at SCDF Headquarters earlier this evening.More updates on OLH operations will be provided over the next few days.

[Update 3: Boy Rescued from a Collapsed Building in Dulkadirolu]The advance team of 20 SCDF officers from the Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent landed in Adana yesterday and headed to Dulkadirolu, Kahramanmara, Trkiye to begin search and rescue operations. In the course of the search and rescue operations amidst the cold weather (about 2), a boy was found in a collapsed 3-storey building.SCDF worked together with the local rescue team and a rescue team from Spain to rescue the boy. The Spanish rescue team used their search canine to pinpoint the location of the boy and SCDF used a fibre-optic scope to confirm the visuals of the boy.All three rescue teams used their cutting and breaking equipment to create an access through the rubble to reach the boy. The boy was rescued from a bedroom in the collapsed building at about 11:45 p.m. yesterday (9 Feb, 4:45 a.m., Singapore time) in a 3-hour rescue operation.

[Update 1: SCDF Operation Lionheart Mission to Trkiye]An advance team of 20 SCDF officers from the Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent will be departing for Adana, Trkiye at 2:05 a.m. today (8 Feb), to assist in the disaster rescue efforts in the aftermath of the Trkiye-Syria earthquake.Led by LTC Lok Wee Keong, commander of SCDFs elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART), the advance team comprises 14 DART rescuers, four paramedic specialists and a Full-time National Serviceman (NSF) doctor. The team was at HQ SCDF yesterday morning to begin their pre-departure briefing and preparation. They will be carrying a slew of portable Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) equipment such as cutting/breaking/lifting equipment, life detection devices and fibre-optic scopes, and this will allow the team to be quickly deployed to affected areas for USAR operations.Yesterday evening, His Excellency Mehmet Burin Gnenli, Turkish Ambassador to Singapore, visited SCDF Headquarters and met up with the OLH contingent to express his gratitude and appreciation to the team. Prior to the team's departure, Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS) for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, and COMR Eric Yap, Commissioner SCDF, were at the airport to send the team off. We would like to thank Singapore Airlines for facilitating the flight arrangements on short notice. We wish our OLH contingent a safe and successful mission.

[Basic Rescue Training Passing Out Parade - 166th Intake]Yesterday, 324 recruits from the 166th Intake stood proudly before their families and loved ones in a Passing Out Parade (POP) to mark the completion of their Basic Rescue Training (BRT) at the Civil Defence Academy. Equipped with essential lifesaving skills including the use of various rescue equipment and techniques, these recruits will now progress into the various vocational training courses in SCDF.The POP was officiated by DC Daniel Seet, Deputy Commissioner (Operations and Resilience). In his opening address, DC Daniel commended the recruits for their effort and commitment in completing the BRT, and wished them all the best as they embark on the next phase of their National Service (NS) journey. He also thanked the families and loved ones for their unwavering support in the recruits' NS journey. Our heartiest congratulations to the recruits of the 166th Intake! You have officially become Rescuers of the Life Saving Force . We look forward to your service and contributions in keeping Singapore safe and secure.ANationofLifesavers

[Exercise Redbrick 2023]Earlier this week, SCDF took part in an operational exercise that simulated a fire incident at a water reclamation plant.Operational complexity was added to the exercise scenario to include the management of multiple casualties, a vehicle accident resulting in the driver and passenger being trapped, and the presence of flammable gas in the compound. Such exercises are designed to test and validate SCDFs response as well as to test the link up between SCDF and the Company Emergency Response Team (CERT). CERTs perform a very important role in being the first response to an emergency within their premises. Their response can help prevent a fire from escalating or save someone from harm.Check out the pictures to see what transpired!ANationofLifesavers

[Rescue 995 Notre-Dame on Fire a film review]On 1 December 2022, Rescue 995 had the privilege of catching an inspirational French film preview, Notre Dame on Fire at Shaw Theatres. The film is a powerful depiction of the fire disaster that happened in Paris, France on 15 April 2019.This film preview was a charity event held by the National Fire and Emergency Preparedness Council (NFEC) to raise funds for the various fire prevention and emergency preparedness programmes and initiatives.Read more on our review of this extraordinary film and some of the key lessons on fire safety via the link on our bio.[3-minute read]

[26th Rota Commander Course (RCC) Commissioning Parade]35 officer cadets from the 26th RCC were commissioned as SCDF Senior Officers at the Civil Defence Academy this morning.The RCC commissioning parade is a significant milestone for these officers, who have undergone seven months of training to equip themselves with the knowledge and skills to respond to a wide range of fire and rescue incidents, as well as incidents involving Hazardous Materials. This RCC included eight international cadets from the Brunei Fire Rescue Department (BFRD), the Ministry of Interior, Kingdom of Bahrain, and the Vietnam Fire and Rescue Police Department (VFRPD). These eight cadets now join the ranks of many other international officers who have previously graduated from SCDFs training courses. In his speech, the guest of honour, Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS) for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, shared about the ongoing Phase Two and Phase Three redevelopment of CDA's Field Training Area, which is targeted to be completed by this year. With the completion of these two phases, officers may look forward to more advanced training facilities which will offer a wider range of realistic and challenging training scenarios. MOS Faishal also spoke about the importance of leveraging the advancements of technology like robotics and smart systems to complement SCDF's frontline operations, allowing frontliners to do their job more effectively and efficiently.On the very same training grounds where months of hard work were put in by the cadets, and where memories and bonds were forged, the cadets were officially commissioned as SCDF Senior Officers. Congratulations to the 26th RCC! We wish them all the best as they journey forward to carry out the life saving mission of the SCDF. ANationOfLifesavers

[Fire Safety Enforcement Checks at Commercial Premises]Amidst the year-end festive season, SCDF has stepped up its enforcement checks at premises where increased footfall is expected.For last weeks fire safety enforcement checks, SCDFs enforcement teams inspected commercial premises to ensure fire safety compliance.Common fire safety infringements were detected at the commercial premises. Some of the violations include the non-maintenance of fire safety measures such as exit light, emergency light and fire extinguisher, as well as the obstruction to hose reel, fireman access panel and emergency escape routes. Enforcement actions will be taken against responsible entities.SCDF will be continuing with its stepped-up fire safety enforcement checks throughout the festive season. Operators of commercial premises are reminded to always comply with fire safety requirements to protect the safety of everyone.

[Fire Safety Enforcement Checks at Commercial Premises]Amidst the year-end festive season, SCDF has stepped up its enforcement checks at premises where increased footfall is expected.For last weeks fire safety enforcement checks, SCDFs enforcement teams inspected commercial premises to ensure fire safety compliance.Common fire safety infringements were detected at the commercial premises. Some of the violations include the non-maintenance of fire safety measures such as exit light, emergency light and fire extinguisher, as well as the obstruction to hose reel, fireman access panel and emergency escape routes. Enforcement actions will be taken against responsible entities.SCDF will be continuing with its stepped-up fire safety enforcement checks throughout the festive season. Operators of commercial premises are reminded to always comply with fire safety requirements to protect the safety of everyone.

[Fire @ Block 699, Hougang Street 52]At about 2:30 p.m. today (23 Nov), SCDF was alerted to a fire at the above-mentioned location. Upon SCDF's arrival, thick black smoke was emitting from a living room of a unit on the 5th floor. Firefighters from Sengkang Fire Station conducted forcible entry to gain access into the unit. The fire, which was confined to the living room, was extinguished with a water jet.While the firefighting operation was ongoing, SCDF rescued two persons from the kitchen and carried them out of the smoke-logged unit. The two persons were conveyed by SCDF ambulances to Singapore General Hospital and KK Womens & Children Hospital for smoke inhalation. About 20 residents from the affected block were evacuated by the Police as a precautionary measure. Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire had likely originated from a personal mobility device (PMD) that was charging in the living room. SCDF would like to remind the public on the prevention of PMD/PAB fires, including not to charge batteries for an extended period of time or overnight. Do not purchase or use non-original batteries. See the accompanying infographic for more fire safety tips.

[Update 4 - Operation Lionheart (OLH) Deployment at New South Wales]The OLH Contingent Team A arrived at Condobolin town yesterday (20 Nov). After being briefed on the flood situation, the team was deployed to the sand banks near the river and lake to assist in setting up flood barriers to reduce floodwater damage to the local communities. Working closely with officers from the Australian Defence Force, Team A continued with their flood barrier operation today (21 Nov) at Condobolin town. Team B in Wagga Wagga city was redeployed to Deniliquin town earlier today. The team was deployed to assist in securing a hazardous debris (shipping container) that was drifting dangerously in the floodwaters. Working together with officers from and , the team did a quick assessment of the water conditions and managed to safely secure the shipping container to a concrete structure, and prevent it from drifting further into the main water stream. Team B was also subsequently deployed to deliver flood protection supplies to residences in the community, and assisted to set up flood protection for some of the residences together with the officers from the . Team A will be proceeding back to Parkes town while Team B will be stationed at Deniliquin town to provide further assistance as major flooding is expected in the area.

[Update 3 - SCDF Operation Lionheart (OLH) Mission to New South Wales]Yesterday evening (18 Nov), the OLH contingent, which was split into two teams i.e. Team A and Team B, arrived at Parkes town and Wagga Wagga city respectively. Earlier today (19 Nov), Team A commenced search operations at Forbes town, which is about 30km away from Parkes town. The team rendered assistance to electricians who were working in a flooded area to reinstate power supply at a power station. Following operations at Forbes town, Team A will be proceeding to Condobolin town for their next deployment. Team B in Wagga Wagga city is on standby for activation as the situation there is dynamic, with an incoming storm anticipated. While on standby, the team practised their lifesaving and boat handling techniques at the nearby Wiradjuri Reserve.Lets give our best wishes to the OLH contingent and pen your words of encouragement for them in the comments section

[Update 2 - SCDF Operation Lionheart Mission to New South Wales]The 16-member Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent arrived at New South Wales (NSW) yesterday (17 Nov) and attended a pre-operations briefing at the NSW State Emergency Service (SES) Bankstown Unit where they were given an update of the flood situation by NSW SES officers. The contingent members were also given a quick familiarisation on the various equipment used by our counterparts at the NSW SES, such as the Inflatable Rescue Boat and the Reach and Rescue Pole.Later today, the OLH contingent will be split into two 7-member teams. The teams will be travelling to Parkes Town and Wagga Wagga City respectively, to prepare for search and rescue operations scheduled to commence on Saturday (19 Nov).LTC Lok Wee Keong, the Commander of SCDFs elite Disaster Assistance, and CPT Tan Chun Hui, Operation Support Officer, will be travelling to NSW SES Headquarters at Wollongong city where they will work with their counterparts NSW SES officers to oversee and coordinate the search and rescue operations at both flood sites.We wish our OLH contingent the best in their upcoming mission. Stay tuned for further updates on the OLH operations in the next few days.

The teams will be travelling to Parkes Town and Wagga Wagga City respectively, to prepare for search and rescue operations scheduled to commence on Saturday (19 Nov).LTC Lok Wee Keong, the Commander of SCDFs elite Disaster Assistance, and CPT Tan Chun Hui, Operation Support Officer, will be travelling to NSW SES Headquarters at Wollongong city where they will work with their counterparts NSW SES officers to oversee and coordinate the search and rescue operations at both flood sites.We wish our OLH contingent the best in their upcoming mission. Stay tuned for further updates on the OLH operations in the next few days.

[SCDF Operation Lionheart Mission to New South Wales]A 16-member SCDF contingent departed for New South Wales, Australia at about 9:00 p.m. today (16 Nov). The contingent, led by LTC Lok Wee Keong, the commander of SCDFs elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART), was deployed in support of the flood rescue efforts being conducted by the Fire and Rescue New South Wales. Supporting LTC Lok are DART officers LTA Sabree Dusuki and LTA Ahmad Faizal, who each have more than 25 years of operational experience in DART. The contingent is also augmented by an operations support officer and 12 DART officers with advanced lifesaver skills, powered pleasure craft driving license, and advanced diver and rescue diver certifications. The SCDF contingent was sent off by Assoc Prof Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development. We would like to thank Singapore Airlines for facilitating the flight arrangements on short notice. We wish our Operation Lionheart contingent a successful mission.

SCDF Operationally Ready National Servicemen (ORNSmen) from CRU HQ, Bravo Company, served as SCDFs charity ambassadors and passionately contributed their time and efforts during the event. [Basic Rescue Training Passing Out Parade - 165th Intake]The 165th Intake stood proudly before their loved ones in a Passing Out Parade (POP) held earlier today to mark the completion of their Basic Rescue Training (BRT) at the Civil Defence Academy. Equipped with essential lifesaving skills, these 332 recruits will now be streamed into various vocations in SCDF.Gracing the event was Mr Murali Pillai, GPC chairperson for Home Affairs and Law, and MP for Bukit Batok SMC. In his opening address, Mr Murali mentioned that National Service is a rite of passage for all sons of Singapore and is an avenue for bonds to be forged regardless of race, language or religion. He thanked the recruits for their commitment and effort in completing the first phase of their National Service (NS) journey and wished them all the best as they embark in the next chapter of their NS journey. Congratulations to the recruits of 165th Intake! You have officially become members of the Life Saving Force! We look forward to your service and contributions to the nation.Check out the pictures below for snippets on their Passing Out Parade and their training in the past few months. SCDFCelebratesNS55ANationofLifesavers
