Committing their personal time after office hours and over many weekends to attend the training sessions, 12 Civil Defence Auxiliary Unit (CDAU) volunteer firefighters took on the challenge and underwent 13 weeks of training at the Civil Defence Academy (CDA).Last evening, these 12 CDAU volunteer firefighters proudly graduated from the 8th Volunteer Firefighter Course (VFFC) in the presence of their family and friends. They will be posted to the various fire stations to work alongside SCDF regular officers, NSFs and ORNSmen.Congratulations to these 12 volunteers for completing the course! Welcome onboard the Life Saving Force and we look forward to your contributions as we work together in carrying out our mission of protecting and saving lives and property.Check out some highlights from the 8th VFFCs training sessions and graduation ceremony below.

It's a dog! It's a robot! It's a... robodog!? Featured for this month is SGT3 Amir Afiq Bin Mohd Kamal from Yishun Fire Station. In the foreground is a four-legged robot called the Rover-X. Equipped with sensors and cameras, this non-furry buddy can navigate various terrains autonomously and send vital information to a remote command-and-control station. This is especially useful for incidents such as those involving hazardous materials, as it allows our SCDF officers to make informed decisions on how best to manage the incident from a safe distance. We are 2 months away till the end of 2022! Stay tuned for the last post of our 2022 calendar series coming up next month :)Rover-X was developed by (Home Team Science and Technology Agency) in collaboration with industry partners.

[Final Update: Fire @ 9, Tuas View Lane]At about 4:35 p.m. today (1 Nov), SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon SCDFs arrival, black smoke was billowing from a warehouse storing petroleum and flammable materials. The area affected by the fire measured about 3 meters by 3 meters.SCDF firefighters and the Company Emergency Response Team (CERT) of the affected premises deployed 2 water jets to contain the fire, and 3 foam jets to extinguish the fire. The fire was extinguished in about an hour. A CERT member was conveyed by SCDF to Singapore General Hospital for smoke inhalation. Damping down operations are ongoing. The cause of fire is under investigation.

[Rescue 995 Touching Lives in the Life Saving Force]COVID-19 has impacted the world in every aspect of life. This is especially true for our heroes at the frontline who have to deal with the higher risk of exposure to the virus, and face tremendous amount of pressure and mental stress from the increased workload due to the COVID-19 virus and its variants. In commemoration of the World Mental Health Day held annually on 10 October, Rescue 995 met up with two SCDF Paracounsellors to find out more on what inspired them to take up this meaningful role of rendering psychological care and emotional support to their fellow frontliners.Read their stories through the link in our bio. [A 7-minute Read]

[Rescue 995 Moulding a New Generation of Marine Specialists]Civil Defence Academys (CDA) enduring philosophy Train as we Operate is deeply entrenched in SCDF officers.This is especially so for SCDFs trainers at the Home Team Tactical Centre (HTTC) where there are various purpose-built training simulators, such as ORCA, a simulator specially designed to provide realistic marine firefighting and rescue simulations and scenarios for trainees. Rescue 995 met up with two HTTC trainers for the Marine Specialist Course, Captain (CPT) Foo Changliang, Aloysius and Warrant Officer (WO2) Siti Mariam Binte Othman to learn more about the course and their experiences on being a trainer. Read more on the story through the link in our bio! [A 5-minute read]

Following the conclusion of a 24-hour assessment by a team of International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) assessors, we are pleased to announce that the SCDF Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) framework for our ORNS Rescue and Medical Units (RU/MU) has been successfully accredited! SCDF is honoured to be the first organisation in the Asia-Pacific region to undergo this accreditation exercise and have its USAR framework for ORNS units recognised by the INSARAG. About 300 ORNS personnel from the SCDF 21 RU/MU were involved in this accreditation exercise held at the Home Team Tactical Centre over the weekend, where their USAR capabilities were tested in both day and night operations involving complex height rescue, cutting, rigging and lifting operations. LTC (NS) Jahan De Silva Din Abdullah, Commander, 21 RU, was proud of his unit's effort and contributions in attaining this achievement for SCDF - Our training and hard work over the past three years, and overcoming the challenges posed by the pandemic, have come to fruition.Mr Mohd Halimi Taib, Team Lead of the Technical Recognition Group from INSARAG, complimented the ORNS Unit for having shown "a high level of competency and skills proficiency. This enabled the unit to have good command, control and coordination of the multiple and concurrent rescue and medical scenarios that the unit was tested over the 24-hour assessment". Our deep appreciation goes out to our ORNSmen without whom this achievement would not be possible. Thank you for your strong commitment in serving the nation! TheLifeSavingForce SCDFcelebratesNS55

[INSARAG-Recognised National Accreditation Process involving SCDF's ORNS 21 RU/MU] Today, the SCDF's Operationally Ready National Servicemen (ORNS) 21 Rescue Unit and 21 Medical Unit (21 RU/MU) that operate under the 2nd SCDF Division have officially commenced their Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) capabilities assessment by the International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) assessors at the Home Team Tactical Centre. This assessment is part of the INSARAG-Recognised National Accreditation Process (IRNAP) that will empower SCDF to be the first organisation in an Asia-Pacific country to conduct self-certification of our ORNS units' USAR capability under the INSARAG framework.Over the past 3 years, despite challenges presented by the ongoing pandemic, our ORNSmen from the 21 RU/MU have put in lots of time, effort and hard work to train and prepare for this assessment.We will provide more pictures at the end of the assessment. Let's wish them all the best!

[Mass Fire Evacuation Drill @ KTPH]The Mass Fire Evacuation Drill (MFED) launching ceremony took place at Khoo Teck Puat Hospital (KTPH) earlier today. Organised by the National Fire And Emergency Preparedness Council - NFEC with participation from Yishun Health and SCDF, this much anticipated campaign resumed after a two-year hiatus due to COVID-19. The launching ceremony kicked off with a simulated fire in one of the wards. Upon activation, the hospital's Company Emergency Response Team (CERT) sprung into action to provide immediate firefighting response and casualty evacuation. Upon SCDFs arrival, the CERT continue to work together with the SCDF firefighters to extinguish the fire and ensure safe evacuation of all patients.About 310 premises and more than 58,000 participants will be conducting MFEDs in their respective premises during this month-long campaign. Such MFEDs are essential in validating the response plans and evacuation procedures of the premises, to ensure that everyone is prepared to take the necessary action in the event of an emergency. ANationofLifesavers

[Ferry Rescue Exercise (FEREX) 2022]SCDF participated in the Ferry Rescue Exercise (FEREX) earlier today. This exercise is conducted annually by the (MPA) and held in conjunction with the International Safety Week. Mr S Iswaran, Minister for Transport, was present to observe the exercise.In today's exercise scenario, the hull of a ferry carrying several passengers was damaged in an accident. As part of the joint agency response, SCDF Marine Division's Heavy Rescue Vessel (HRV) went alongside the stricken ferry to simulate the rescue and evacuation of passengers. Meanwhile, SCDF's Emergency Medical Services (EMS), together with the Disaster Site Medical Command (DSMC), were also deployed at the Harbourfront Ferry Terminal where the first aid point and medical triage facilities were set up to provide treatment to the casualties.This exercise tested the operational readiness and response of the various supporting agencies as well as ferry operators in the event of a ferry mishap.Check out some of the highlights from this exercise below!

[Neighbours help others to safely evacuate during a fire at Blk 866 Yishun St 81]On the evening of 23 July 2022, two Good Samaritans worked together to safely evacuate their fellow neighbours at the above-mentioned location.Mr Malik Maksudi had just reached home when he heard cries for help. He proceeded down the block and saw smoke and flames coming out of a unit on the 4th floor. Mr John Wu, Vice-Chairman of the National Fire And Emergency Preparedness Council, who is also a resident of the block, sprung into action alongside Mr Malik.Upon arriving at the affected unit, the duo successfully evacuated a person who was still inside and other occupants from neighbouring units. The probable cause of the fire was determined to be due to electrical origin in a bedroom of the affected unit. Such fires can be avoided: Do not continue to use electrical appliances that are faulty or have signs of damage to the wires. Do not overload an electrical socket.Yesterday, Mr Malik was presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. The award was co-presented by COL Lim Beng Hui, Commander 3rd SCDF Division and Mr John Wu. Kudos to Mr Malik for his neighbourly spirit and his exemplary action! You too can learn basic firefighting, first aid and CPR-AED in the physical session of the SCDF's CEPP or attend its e-modules session online at CommunityFirstResponders CommunityLifesaversANationofLifesavers OurCFRsOurHeroesOurResponseMattersWeMakeSGSecure From L to R COL Lim Beng Hui, Commander, 3rd SCDF Division, Mr Malik Maksudi, Mr John Wu, Vice-Chairman, National Fire and Emergency Preparedness Council

[Final Update: Fire @ Blk 222 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh]At about 8.20pm today (12 Aug), SCDF was alerted to a fire at the above-mentioned location. Upon SCDFs arrival, the fire was raging and thick black smoke was emitting from a unit on the 3rd floor. At the height of the firefighting operation, two water jets were deployed to fight the fire. As a result of the fire, the entire unit was affected by heat and smoke damage.One person was conveyed to Singapore General Hospital for smoke inhalation. Another person was assessed by an SCDF paramedic for smoke inhalation and subsequently refused conveyance to the hospital.About 50 occupants from the affected block were evacuated by the Police and SCDF as a precautionary measure. We understand some occupants of the affected block had self-evacuated proactively.The cause of the fire is under investigation.

[Behind the scenes with the NDP 2022 SCDF contingent]SCDFs contingent has been training hard for the National Day 2022 (NDP 2022) Parade and Ceremony!CPL (NSF) Soh Kian Ho from Clementi Fire Station is part of the SCDF contingent this year. His family had also participated in previous NDPs: his mom marched in 1987, his dad marched in 2015 and his sister assisted with video production in 2021. The sense of pride in all of us marching together fills me at every rehearsal. The past 12 weeks of training has strengthened our bonds and from it weve forged strong friendships. [Basic Rescue Training Passing Out Parade - 164th Intake]A total of 336recruits from the 164th Intake stood proudly before their loved ones in a Passing Out Parade (POP) held earlier today to mark the completion of their Basic Rescue Training (BRT) at the Civil Defence Academy. Equipped with essential lifesaving skills, these recruits will now be streamed into various vocations in SCDF.Gracing the event was Mr Christopher de Souza, GPC member for Home Affairs and Law, and MP for Holland-Bukit Timah GRC. As we celebrate 55 years of National Service in Singapore, Mr Christopher mentioned that National Service is not only a source of pride and strength for our nation, but it has become a cornerstone of our nations shared identity, and a key thread of our social fabric. He thanked the recruits for their commitment and effort in completing the first phase of their National Service journey.Congratulations to the recruits of 164th Intake! You have officially become Rescuers of the Life Saving Force! We look forward to your service and contributions to the nation.SCDFCelebratesNS55ANationofLifesavers

[Fire @ Blk 92B Telok Blangah Street 31]At about 11.40am today (3 Aug), SCDF was alerted to a fire at the above-mentioned location. Upon SCDFs arrival, the fire was raging and thick black smoke was emitting from a unit on the 11th floor. Firefighters from Alexandra Fire Station conducted forcible entry into the unit and extinguished the fire using two water jets. As a result of the fire, the entire unit was affected by heat and smoke damage. Damping down operations are ongoing.A person was assessed by an SCDF paramedic for smoke inhalation and subsequently refused conveyance to the hospital. About 50 occupants from the affected block were evacuated by the Police and SCDF as a precautionary measure. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

[SCDF e-Calendar 2022]For the month of August, we have Warrant Officer 1 (WO1) Muhammad Syahmi bin Sariff, a Rescue Section Commander with the Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) As a member of SCDF's DART, WO1 Syahmi is trained to handle complex operations such as urban search and rescue, prolonged fire fighting operations, height and confined space rescue operations, road traffic and industrial accidents, and water rescue. Behind him is the ORCA, a Marine Firefighting and Rescue Training Facility at the Home Team Tactical Centre (HTTC). Modelled after an actual sea vessel, the ORCA allows for various training scenarios with access via different doors and hatches, as well as compartments that can be flooded to simulate a real emergency on board a vessel.Stay tuned for more of our e-calendar where we'll feature an SCDF officer in each successive month!TheLifeSavingForceANationofLifesavers

[SCDF Celebrates NS55] .Meet LTA Wang Mingkang, a Rescue Engineer for the 41 Rescue Unit, whose role is to develop mitigation plans, monitor and assess a buildings structural support. As a rescue engineer, LTA Mingkang is well-versed in the knowledge of buildings and structures, including typical collapse patterns and their structural behaviours under adverse loading. Using these knowledge, he provides hazard reduction alternatives through the stabilisation of these buildings and structures. Besides carrying out the role of a Rescue Engineer in SCDF, LTA Mingkang also works as a Research Engineer who conducts research relating to structural collapse through the use of experiments and numerical simulations.Above and beyond his duty to serve, LTA Mingkang is a firm believer in lifelong learning and this can be seen in his Civil Engineering PhD candidature where he provides support in a research collaboration project which involves the design and assessment of precast concrete framed structures.Like LTA Mingkang, most of us wear multiple hats in our lives: National Serviceman, Employee, Student. And each day, we strive to be the best that we can be in every aspect of our lives. As we celebrate NS55 this year, let us reflect on the collective resolve and dedication of our fellow National Servicemen in building a stronger Singapore for generations to come.

[Canberra Community Resilience Day]On Sunday, 24 July 2022, about 500 participants attended the Canberra Community Resilience (CR) Day, organised by 3rd SCDF Division in partnership with the People's Association (PA) and the Canberra Community Emergency and Engagement (C2E) Committee. At the Canberra CR Day, cadets from the National Civil Defence Cadet Corps (), members of the CD Lionhearter Club and volunteers from the Home Team Volunteer Network () proudly contributed their time and effort to impart and equip members of the public with Emergency Preparedness (EP) skills. Such EP skills included Improvised First Aid Skills (IFAS), Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), usage of an Automated External Defibrillator (AED), how to use a fire extinguisher and as well as household fire safety tips.As part of the CR Day, participants also learnt how to respond when the Public Warning System is activated and where to find the nearest Civil Defence Public Shelters.Once equipped with these life-saving skills, the public is encouraged to step forward and register as Community First Responders (CFRs) via the MyResponder app to assist those in need of assistance during emergencies. CFRs are vital in enabling our community stay strong and resilient by assisting in grassroots emergency response efforts with the respective C2Es.SCDF, PA and C2E Committees plan to conduct a series of CR Day programmes annually across the four SCDF land divisions. In the meantime, you can also join us towards building ANationofLifesavers by learning lifesaving skills through the Community Emergency and Preparedness Programme (CEPP) at

[Exercise @ The Float @ Marina Bay 2022] National Day is coming up next month! In preparation for the celebration at The Float @ Marina Bay, SCDF conducted an operational exercise which simulated a chemical agent release scenario at the said location early this morning. About 280 SCDF officers and 26 emergency vehicles were involved in the exercise. Such exercises not only help in familiarising our emergency responders with the area of operations, but are crucial in ensuring that we remain ready to respond to emergencies, anytime. The exercise was supported by the Ministry of Defence, Singapore (MINDEF), Ministry of Health, Singapore and Singapore Police Force. Check out the pics below to see the highlights of the exercise!

[Exercise Rambo 2022]A total of 259 Operationally Ready National Servicemen (ORNS) from 42 Rescue Unit (RU) and 42 Medical Unit (MU), took part in a gruelling, 12-hour long exercise earlier today at the Home Team Tactical Centre (HTTC).In the Rescue Unit/Medical Unit Proficiency Assessment (codenamed Exercise Rambo), our ORNS will undergo a series of simulated scenarios specifically designed to rigorously test and evaluate their competencies in handling large-scale and prolonged urban search and rescue (USAR) operations. Such exercises are crucial in ensuring the operational readiness of our ORNS in responding to major emergencies.The ORNS are tasked in various individual roles, such as rescuers, medical support and service support personnel. As a unit, they are required to conduct USAR operations in collapsed structures based on the United Nation's International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) requirements. The ORNS were tested on their ability to perform cutting, breaking, and lifting operations, and render medical assistance to casualties at the incident site.This exercise capped-off the 42 RU's 5th year of In-Camp Training (ICT). The ORNS had sacrificed their personal time to ensure the success of the exercise. We thank them for responding to the call of duty, and being ready to protect and save lives and property for a safe Singapore. TheLifeSavingForceSCDFcelebratesNS55

[Exercise Rambo 2022]A total of 259 Operationally Ready National Servicemen (ORNS) from 42 Rescue Unit (RU) and 42 Medical Unit (MU), took part in a gruelling, 12-hour long exercise earlier today at the Home Team Tactical Centre (HTTC).In the Rescue Unit/Medical Unit Proficiency Assessment (codenamed Exercise Rambo), our ORNS will undergo a series of simulated scenarios specifically designed to rigorously test and evaluate their competencies in handling large-scale and prolonged urban search and rescue (USAR) operations. Such exercises are crucial in ensuring the operational readiness of our ORNS in responding to major emergencies.The ORNS are tasked in various individual roles, such as rescuers, medical support and service support personnel. As a unit, they are required to conduct USAR operations in collapsed structures based on the United Nation's International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) requirements. The ORNS were tested on their ability to perform cutting, breaking, and lifting operations, and render medical assistance to casualties at the incident site.This exercise capped-off the 42 RU's 5th year of In-Camp Training (ICT). The ORNS had sacrificed their personal time to ensure the success of the exercise. We thank them for responding to the call of duty, and being ready to protect and save lives and property for a safe Singapore. TheLifeSavingForceSCDFcelebratesNS55

[NS55 Get-Together for NS Personnel]Earlier this evening, the NS55 Get-Together event was held at Khatib Clubhouse. About 350 SCDF Operationally Ready National Servicemen (ORNS) were in attendance to commemorate 55 years of NS in Singapore and to recognise the contributions of past and present NSmen.Gracing the event was Ms Sun Xueling, Minister of State, Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of Social and Family Development. In her opening address, she recognised the integral role that NSmen serve in the Life Saving Force and acknowledged the efforts that SCDF has put in place to create a more meaningful NS experience.Tokens of appreciation were also presented to approximately 50 national servicemen who made significant contributions to SCDF by serving 10 years or more as a key appointment/responsibility appointment holders.To all our NSmen, past and present: Thank you for your commitment, dedication and contributions towards the Life Saving Force!SCDFcelebratesNS55

[Final Update: Fire @ No. 50, Choa Chu Kang Track 14]At about 7.35pm today (20 July), SCDF was alerted to a fire at the above-mentioned location. The fire, which involved rows of potted plants in a nursery, was confined to an area of about 20 meters by 20 meters.At the height of the firefighting operation, a total of five water jets were used to contain and prevent the fire from spreading.The fire was extinguished within one and a half hours.Several caged birds were found dead near the scene of the fire. There were no other reported injuries.The cause of the fire is under investigation.

[17th NCDCC Affirmation Day 2022]This afternoon, close to 675 Secondary 1 students were sworn in as National Civil Defence Cadet Corps (NCDCC) cadets at the NCDCC Affirmation Day 2022.The event was graced by Ms Loh Wee Cheng, Divisional Director, Student Development Curriculum Division 1, MOE.These young cadets have taken that first important step towards joining the lifesaving fraternity. As an NCDCC cadet, they will be equipped with important life saving skills such as first aid, basic fire-fighting and CPR-AED procedure.Theyll even get the opportunity to specialise in areas such as fire safety, medical response, and urban search and rescue.Through their time in NCDCC, the cadets will be nurtured into resilient, concerned and active citizens who are ready to serve the community as Community First Responders in times of need. Congratulations and welcome onboard to all newly affirmed cadets! We eagerly look forward to having you serve the community with pride and compassion ANationOfLifesavers

[Increase in 995 EMS Calls] 995 Emergency Medical Services (EMS) calls to SCDF have increased to about 760 calls a day on average in the first week of July, with the highest being 810.The average daily number of EMS calls pre-COVID-19 was about 550. If EMS calls continue to climb, the public may experience delays in ambulance response, particularly for less critical medical incidents.We are monitoring the situation closely. We have put in place measures to manage the increase in EMS Calls. Some of these measures are: Optimise and adjust deployments of ambulances to areas with a high rate of medical emergency calls Continue prioritising our response to critical life-threatening medical emergencies Patients assessed by SCDF paramedics to have non-emergency medical conditions will not be conveyed to hospitalOur 995 call takers, paramedics and frontliners are doing their best to provide swift conveyance to hospital for people with life-threatening and emergency medical conditions. Here's what YOU can do to help. Refrain from calling 995 if you are not suffering any life-threatening or emergency medical conditions.By doing so, SCDF can continue to provide swift conveyance to those who require our emergency medical services. See pictures for more details.

[Community Lifesavers on Wheels]This afternoon, the SCDF-Ninja Van AED-on-Wheels programme was officially launched by Ms Sun Xueling, Minister of State for Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of Social and Family Development.50 delivery vehicles from have been equipped with Automated External Defibrillators (AEDs), sponsored by COSEM Safety and Security Services Pte Ltd. Ninja Van Singapore has also equipped these 50 vehicles with a fire extinguisher and a first aid kit. To prepare them for their role as Community Lifesavers, 50 Ninja Van drivers have been trained by SCDF to administer Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), applying AED, conduct basic firefighting and administer first aid.The AED-on-Wheels programme equips vehicles on the move with an AED, in support of SCDFs Save-A-Life initiative. The other companies who are onboard this programme are: Strides Taxi (formerly SMRT Taxi), Grab and ComfortDelGro.Drivers are alerted to cardiac arrest emergencies and also minor fires within a 1.5 kilometre radius of their vehicle's location through SCDF's myResponder app.During the launch, an active AED-on-Wheels taxi driver from was also awarded the SCDF Community First Responder Award. Mr Elson Sim Kong Thong had responded and assisted in two minor fires and two cardiac arrest incidents last year.SCDF warmly welcomes Ninja Van and its drivers to the Lifesaver family. ANationofLifesavers

[Geylang Serai Community Resilience Day]On Saturday, 2 July 2022, about 500 participants attended the Geylang Serai Community Resilience (CR) Day, organised by 2nd SCDF Division in partnership with the People's Association (PA) and the Geylang Serai Community Emergency and Engagement (C2E) Committee. The CR Day aims to impart and equip members of the public with Emergency Preparedness (EP) skills and knowledge such as Improvised First Aid Skills (IFAS), conducting Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), usage of an Automated External Defibrillator (AED), and how to use a fire extinguisher, as well as household fire safety tips.As part of the CR Day, participants will also learn how to respond when the Public Warning System is activated and where to find the nearest Civil Defence Public Shelters.Upon being equipped with these life-saving skills, the public is encouraged to step forward and register as Community First Responders (CFRs) to assist those in need of help during emergencies. CFRs are vital in enabling our community to stay strong and resilient by assisting in grassroots emergency response efforts with the respective C2Es.SCDF, PA and C2E Committees plan to conduct a series of CR Day programmes annually across the four SCDF land Divisions. In the meantime, you can also join us in paving the way towards building ANationofLifesavers by learning lifesaving skills through the Community Emergency and Preparedness Programme (CEPP). You can find out more through the link in our bio!

[SCDF DART - UK ISAR Exercise 2022]Earlier this week, we welcomed our friends from the UK International Search and Rescue (ISAR) team for a joint urban search and rescue exercise. Held at the Home Team Tactical Centre (HTTC) at Mandai from 28 - 30 June, the exercise was conducted together with rescuers from SCDF's elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART). The exercise saw the participants conducting a number of challenging exercise scenarios such as search and rescue of a collapsed building, chemical plant incident and a complex height rescue exercise. The UK ISAR team was led by Commander Russ Gauden. He shared that "The facility (at HTTC) gave a huge test of endurance, skill and attributes for UK ISAR. SCDF are a world leading team and the opportunity to train and exercise alongside them gave UK ISAR colleagues and myself a huge sense of pride." Singapore's hot and humid weather was also an element of challenge for the British rescuers as the climate here is unlike their home country, but we salute them for their perseverance and stamina throughout the exercise! On top of the hands-on exercise to test their response capabilities, a sharing session was also held where the experts from UK discussed topics relating to search and rescue, such as disaster victim identification.The joint exercise was an enriching opportunity for both parties to work alongside and learn from each other, in our common mission of protecting and saving lives. To many more years of partnership! thelifesavingforce: MX Aidil and LCP Syukri, SCDF Corporate Communications Department

SCDF are a world leading team and the opportunity to train and exercise alongside them gave UK ISAR colleagues and myself a huge sense of pride." Singapore's hot and humid weather was also an element of challenge for the British rescuers as the climate here is unlike their home country, but we salute them for their perseverance and stamina throughout the exercise! On top of the hands-on exercise to test their response capabilities, a sharing session was also held where the experts from UK discussed topics relating to search and rescue, such as disaster victim identification.The joint exercise was an enriching opportunity for both parties to work alongside and learn from each other, in our common mission of protecting and saving lives. To many more years of partnership! thelifesavingforce: MX Aidil and LCP Syukri, SCDF Corporate Communications Department

The 6th generation (6G) of the Light Fire Attack Vehicle (LFAV) aka Red Rhino, recently launched at the SCDF Workplan Seminar on 10 June, marks the transition from a 4 to a 3-crew configuration. This transition is to optimise the tighter constraints on available resources and at the same time, maintain our operational edge through leveraging technology.This 6G Red Rhino comes equipped with various new and enhanced equipping features, such as two 25kg Compressed Air Foam (CAF) trolleys, a vehicle fire suppression blanket, and a portable, battery operated rescue tool, which can be operated by a single firefighter. What's more, it also comes with a charming plus one - the 2nd generation of Red Rhino Robot (3R 2.0). This red beauty has people turning heads and safely shifting lanes for it, especially when it croons and flashes red/blue. What a stunner! TheLifeSavingForce

[Fire @ Block 682 Hougang Avenue 4]At approximately 9.50pm yesterday (1 July), SCDF responded to a fire at the above-mentioned location. Upon SCDF's arrival, the fire was raging and thick black smoke was emitting from a 3rd floor unit. The fire involved contents of a bedroom. Firefighters from Sengkang Fire Station donned breathing apparatus sets and extinguished the fire with a water jet. As a result of the fire, the entire unit was affected by heat and smoke damage.One occupant from the affected unit had evacuated prior to SCDFs arrival. He was assessed by an SCDF paramedic and conveyed to Singapore General Hospital for smoke inhalation.About 25 people from the affected block were evacuated by the Police and SCDF as a precautionary measure.The cause of the fire is under investigation.

[Three Good Samaritans and two police officers saved two toddlers during a fire at Block 218 Marsiling Crescent] On the night of 22 June 2022, three Good Samaritans and two police officers saved two toddlers during a fire at the above-mentioned location. Mr Muhammad Firdaus Bin Aziz was resting at home when he was alerted by a neighbour to the fire. Springing into action, he broke down the door of the affected unit and conducted a preliminary search. Mr Sebastian Ng was also alerted to the fire. After evacuating his family, he proceeded to the affected unit to do another search. Meanwhile, Sergeant Nur Fadilah Binte Arshad and Special Constable Franco Kam Chuan Kun from the were activated to the incident. When they arrived at the scene, the two police officers met Mr Sebastian and other neighbours. When told that there could be persons trapped in the affected unit, the two police officers immediately entered the unit, found two toddlers and swiftly rescued them. Mdm Annaboorani Kanapathy assisted to console the two toddlers as SCDF officers rendered medical assistance. Yesterday, the three Good Samaritans and two police officers were each awarded the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. The award was presented by COL Goh Boon Han, Commander 4th SCDF Division. Kudos to these individuals for their prompt and exemplary actions! [NDP 2022 Total Defence Display]NDP 2022 is coming next month and the Total Defence Display (TDD) will be back! SCDF is proud to participate in TDD which is put together by the Singapore Armed Forces and the Home Team. TDD will showcase SCDFs firefighting robots such as the Unmanned Firefighting Machine (UFM) that packs a punch in prolonged operations. .Meet SGT1 Jagadeeshvaran S/O Rananathan, a Navigational Specialist from Brani Marine Fire Station who performs a critical role in ensuring the safe navigation of the firefighting vessel whenever it is being deployed.While serving his National Service, SGT1 Jagadeeshvaran learnt many hard and soft skills as well as valuable life lessons. Having been in Brani Marine Fire Station for the past 8 months, he acquired specific skills ranging from rope tying to height and water rescue.His most memorable experience was responding to a fire on top of a hill on Kusu island. This incident was memorable to him as he was the first arriving Section Commander who with his team, promptly set up the initial water jet to fight the fire.Even when off duty, SGT1 Jagadeeshvaran remains tightly knitted with his rota. From time to time, he enjoys putting his own hairdressing skills to the test by helping his rota mates trim their hair at his fathers barber shop.Everyone has a unique experience and a different story to tell. As we continue to celebrate NS55 in SCDF, we pay tribute to the contributions and sacrifices made by each National Serviceman which enable Singaporeans to enjoy a safe and secure home.{Stay tuned for the coverage of more NS vocations in our subsequent series!}SCDFcelebratesNS55

[25th Rota Commander Course (RCC) Commissioning Ceremony]After undergoing seven months of rigorous training, 36 officer cadets from the 25th RCC were commissioned as SCDF Senior Officers at the Civil Defence Academy this morning.The RCC commissioning ceremony is a significant milestone that marks the transition of these 36 individuals, including 25 Full-time National Servicemen, into SCDF Senior Officers. As Senior Officers, their tasks include leading a team to respond to a wide range of incidents such as firefighting, rescue and Hazardous Materials. This RCC also included international trainees for the first time in two years due to the pandemic. Hailing from the BFRD - Brunei Fire Rescue Department, the three participants now join the ranks of other BFRD Senior Officers who have graduated from SCDFs training programmes.In a speech delivered by Mr Zhulkarnain Bin Abdul Rahim, the Deputy Chairperson of the Government Parliamentary Committee (Home Affairs and Law), he acknowledged the strong support of family members and friends of the cadets in helping them to reach this significant milestone. He also spoke about the great responsibilities to be shouldered by the newly minted Senior Officers, and urged them to always prioritise the well-being and safety of the people they lead.On the very same training grounds where months of learning and intense training took place, the cadets stood proudly and were officially commissioned as SCDF Senior Officers. Congratulations to the 25th RCC! We wish them all the best as they venture forth in their journey with the Life Saving Force. ANationOfLifesavers

[Fire @ Block 218 Marsiling Crescent]At approximately 10.40pm yesterday (22 June), SCDF responded to a fire at the above-mentioned location.The fire involved contents of a bedroom in a 2nd floor unit. Upon SCDF's arrival, the fire was raging and thick black smoke was emitting from the unit. Firefighters from Woodlands Fire Station donned breathing apparatus sets and extinguished the fire with a water jet. As a result of the fire, the entire unit was affected by heat and smoke damage.About 60 people from neighbouring units were evacuated by the Police as a precautionary measure. Two police officers also rescued two toddlers who were found conscious in the living room of the affected unit prior to SCDFs arrival. The two toddlers were conveyed to KK Women's and Children's Hospital by two SCDF ambulances.We understand that after the fire started, a member of the public had attempted to force open the door of the affected unit to rescue the two toddlers. SCDF will be reaching out to the person to commend him for his quick-thinking and prompt action in attempting to rescue the toddlers.The cause of fire is under investigation.

On the evening of 4 May 2022, personnel from 605 Squadron came across a road traffic accident at the junction of KJE (BKE) exit towards Brickland Road. Without hesitation, they stopped their vehicle and together with a few other Good Samaritans (including a Civil Defence Auxiliary Unit officer), successfully freed three casualties who were trapped in their damaged vehicle. The RSAF team provided first aid to the casualties, diverted traffic away from the accident, and comforted the casualties until the arrival of SCDFs emergency responders.And on the evening of 22 May 2022, three staff from Bukit Gombak MRT Station, saved a man who fell unconscious after suffering a cardiac arrest. Mr Mohamed Wahed Bin Sawpi, Mr Muhammad Rizwan Bin Hamzah and Mdm Nur Farah Shafiqah Binte Mohamed Madi put their CPR and AED skills to use that day. Their collective effort is a testament of the importance of learning Emergency Preparedness Skills (e.g. CPR and AED).Yesterday, the Good Samaritans were awarded the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. The award was presented by COL Goh Boon Han, Commander, 4th SCDF Division.You too can learn first aid skills such as CPR-AED and basic firefighting in the physical session of the SCDFs CEPP or attend its e-modules session online via the link in our bio.CommunityFirstRespondersCommunityLifesaversANationofLifesaversOurCFRsOurHeros

[Fire @ 53, Compassvale Bow]At approximately 5.55pm today (6 June), SCDF responded to a fire at the above-mentioned location. Upon SCDFs arrival, black smoke could be seen emitting from a 15th floor unit. Firefighters from Sengkang Fire Station donned breathing apparatus sets and conducted forcible entry to gain access into the unit. No one was in the unit.The fire, which involved the contents of kitchen, was extinguished using a water jet. A dog was found in the living room of the unit and was rescued by SCDF. The dog was handed back to the owner. About 10 people from the affected block were evacuated by SCDF. There were no reported injuries. The fire was largely confined to the kitchen and the cause of the fire is under investigation.

[Marymount Community Resilience Day]Earlier today (5 June), the Marymount Community Resilience (CR) Day, held at Bishan North Shopping Mall was launched by Ms Gan Siow Huang, Advisor to Marymount SMC grassroots organisations. Marymount CR Day marks the first time a fully physical CR Day was held since the easing of Covid-19 safe management measures.The CR Day programme, organised in partnership with Peoples Association (PA), National Fire and Emergency Preparedness Council (NFEC), and Community Emergency and Engagement (C2E) Committees, aims to impart skills such as Improvised First Aid, Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), Automated External Defibrillator (AED), using a fire extinguisher, as well as raising awareness on various fire safety tips. Participants can also learn about the Public Warning System and Civil Defence Shelters.Once equipped with these life-saving skills, the public are encouraged to step forward and register as Community First Responders (CFRs) to assist those in distress in times of an emergency.During Marymount CR Day, 8 persons were presented with the SCDF Community First Responder Award (CFRA) and 3 persons were presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award (CLA). The CFRA is presented to members of the public who stepped forward to render assistance to others in distress and/or save property. The CLA is presented to members of the public whose actions involved an element of self-risk and/or contributed to saving lives.You too can learn EP skills in the physical session of the SCDFs Community Emergency Preparedness Programme or attend its e-modules session online at

Pictured here for the month of June is LTC Muhammad Shahdele bin Isman, Commander of Ang Mo Kio Fire Station. Beyond his tall stature, LTC Shahdele is an approachable figure with 120 station personnel under his care. He is in charge of emergency situations that unfold within his station boundaries such as in Ang Mo Kio, Bishan, Serangoon and Serangoon North areas. Behind him is the Forward Command Vehicle (FCV) which functions as a mobile headquarters command and control centre. It may look like a big, ordinary bus, but the FCV is deployed to major incidents to facilitate mission planning, decision making and incident monitoring, led by commanders like LTC Shahdele himself. Within the FCV, essential computer and communications equipment, as well as a extendable mast equipped with weather monitoring, spotlight and cameras for situational awareness, can be set up to provide enhanced operational and tactical capability at the incident site. Stay tuned for more of our e-calendar where well feature an SCDF officer in each successive month! TheLifeSavingForce ANationofLifesavers

[Opening of Lifesavers' Connect Hub at Kallang Fire Station]Did you know that besides learning Emergency Preparedness skills, SCDF volunteer leaders also receive training on leadership and public speaking skills?Yesterday (31 May), the Lifesavers' Connect Hub (LCH) at Kallang Fire Station (KFS) was officially opened by Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State, Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development. The LCH will serve as a dedicated space for SCDF volunteer leaders to receive training beyond lifesaving skills. With these skills, they will be able to carry out their roles meaningfully as well-rounded volunteers. These volunteer leaders include members of the Civil Defence Auxiliary Unit, as well as student members of the National Civil Defence Cadet Corps and CD Lionhearter Club. The LCH at KFS will host the training for our volunteer leaders while the permanent LCH will be built at Hill Street. Visit the Home Team Volunteer Network through the link in our bio to find out more on how you can be a SCDF volunteer!ANationOfLifesavers

[SCDF Celebrates NS55]Meet LTA(Dr) Justin Ng Choon Hwee, a Medical Officer (MO) currently serving his full-time National Service with SCDF.As a MO, LTA(Dr) Justin's job scope includes conducting medical board reviews where he assesses SCDF officers' suitability to take on different frontline roles based on their fitness level. MOs are also part of the SCDF Operation Lionheart Contingent when it is activated for overseas humanitarian missions.In his seven months with the Force, LTA(Dr) Justin has seen through various projects, one of which was an initiative to improve Paramedic education and training. Through the development of a digital application to replace traditional pen and paper tests, data values and insights are obtained to provide real-time, customised feedback for Paramedics, thereby improving their learning experience. Here in SCDF, we are thankful for the diversity of our National Servicemen, together with their specialised skillsets and knowledge, for they help to propel innovation and performance in our everyday life.{Stay tuned for the coverage of more NS vocations in our subsequent series!}SCDFcelebratesNS55

[Rescue @ 18, Defu Avenue 2] At about 1.05pm today (27 May), SCDF was activated for a rescue incident Involving a man that was trapped under a large metal cylindrical pipe between a trailer and a lorry. Arriving first at the scene, SCDF firefighters and Emergency Medical Services from Paya Lebar Fire Station immediately conducted an assessment on the trapped man and promptly rendered medical assistance to stabilise him. Rescuers from the elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) were also activated, and working together with the fire station crew, they used two air lifting bags to lift the pipe. An air lifting bag is a thin and lightweight piece of rescue equipment that can be used in confined spaces, where bulkier rescue equipment would not be able to be deployed. When compressed air is filled into the air lifting bag, it expands and enables rescuers to lift, spread or create space between two objects, thereby facilitating the rescue operation. Once the injured man was freed, an SCDF ambulance conveyed him to Tan Tock Seng Hospital.

The SCDF Emergency Medical Services (EMS) community gathered together earlier this week for the inaugural launch of the SCDF EMS Week. The 3-day event was held both virtually and physically, and saw the participation of EMS personnel across the 4 SCDF Divisions. During the event, the EMS community conducted chats, focussed group discussions, and organised a retreat to bond and share their experiences.A key highlight of the event was the EMS Battleground, Simulation Wars competition. Participating teams were put through realistic simulations that challenged their on-scene response in identifying scene hazards, providing patient care under a variety of conditions, and tested their teamwork and communication skills. The competition also required participants to demonstrate clinical skills, command and control and situational awareness, a key requirement for our EMS crews to operate effectively in today's dynamic and complex operating environment.Comr Eric Yap, Commissioner SCDF, graced the commemorative event yesterday and witnessed the finals of the competition, where the team from 4th SCDF Division emerged as the champion. Congratulations to the winning team! To the SCDF EMS family, thank you for your hard work, dedication and commitment to duty. Thank you for the many contributions in helping to build and develop the prehospital emergency care landscape. Heres wishing the best for many more successful EMS events ahead!EMSturns25TheLifeSavingForce

The competition also required participants to demonstrate clinical skills, command and control and situational awareness, a key requirement for our EMS crews to operate effectively in today's dynamic and complex operating environment.Comr Eric Yap, Commissioner SCDF, graced the commemorative event yesterday and witnessed the finals of the competition, where the team from 4th SCDF Division emerged as the champion. Congratulations to the winning team! To the SCDF EMS family, thank you for your hard work, dedication and commitment to duty. Thank you for the many contributions in helping to build and develop the prehospital emergency care landscape. Heres wishing the best for many more successful EMS events ahead!EMSturns25TheLifeSavingForce

[Fire @ 4007 Depot Lane]At about 10.15am today (10 May), SCDF responded to a fire at the above-mentioned location. Upon arrival, SCDF emergency responders found the fire raging in an industrial unit. SCDF initially deployed two water jets as protective curtains to prevent the fire from spreading to the adjacent units. The fire was subsequently extinguished using two foam jets and one water jet. About 20 people from the affected premises self-evacuated before SCDF's arrival. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

[SCDF e-Calendar 2022]This month, we have CPT Shavithiya Shanmugam from the Training and Professional Development Department! As a member of the Hazmat Emergency Assessment and Response Team (HEART), CPT Shavithiya and her team are on standby 24/7 daily and during various nation-wide large scale events to respond to any suspected chemical agent incidents.Behind her is the HazMat Control Vehicle (HCV) with its launch pad extended and the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) situated on it. In the event of a chemical incident, the UAV can be attached with chemical detectors before being deployed from the vehicle. It is able to measure not only the geographical spread of contamination, but also the height of the spread.May the month of May be great for you! Stay tuned for more of our e-calendar where we'll feature an SCDF officer in each successive month.TheLifeSavingForceANationofLifeSavers

[SCDF Celebrates NS55]Here in SCDF, serving National Service (NS) goes beyond being in a frontline unit. There are many vocations that allow both our Operationally Ready National Servicemen (ORNS) and full-time National Servicemen (NSF) to contribute to the best that they could. Meet CPL(NS) Burhan Jumadi, an ORNSman who used to serve his 2-year full-time NS as a Multimedia Specialist in the Media Production Unit (MPU) of SCDF's Corporate Communications Department from 2019 to 2020. During his NSF days with MPU, CPL(NS) Burhan was actively involved in MPU's camera and lighting team to produce SCDF in-house media content for educational and branding purposes. His most memorable involvement was during the 2019 Singapore-Global Firefighters & Paramedics Challenge (SGFPC). CPL(NS) Burhan, together with his team, put their heads together for the intensive planning on the camera angle for the live streaming of SGFPC online. And it was a smashing success winning the hearts and accolades of netizens!With CPL(NS) Burhan's past experience in the Audio Visual (AV) Industry prior to his NS enlistment, being in MPU gave him the golden opportunity to put his skills and experience into good use. It also allowed him to stay abreast of latest developments, including building up his social network in the media industry.Today, CPL(NS) Burhan still keeps in touch with his former NSF batchmates and he is confident that their friendship will persist for many years to come. "In MPU, it doesn't matter whether you are junior or senior individuals. What matters is the rich and fruitful journey you'll embark together in your 2 years as NSFs with the team".This year, as we celebrate 55 years of NS in Singapore, we in SCDF pay tribute to the effort and dedication of Singaporeans who are serving as well as those who had served NS across vocations. THANK YOU for your service to our nation! {Stay tune for the coverage of more NS vocations in our subsequent series.}

[Basic Rescue Training Passing Out Parade - 163rd Intake]On Thursday, 28th April, 304 recruits from the 163rd Intake stood proudly in a Passing Out Parade (POP) to mark the completion of their Basic Rescue Training (BRT) at the Civil Defence Academy (CDA). Equipped with essential lifesaving skills, these recruits will now be streamed into various vocations in SCDF. For the first time since the COVID-19 outbreak, the families and loved ones of the recruits were invited to the National Service Training Centre (NSTC) at CDA to witness this significant moment, instead of viewing it through livestream. In his address to the recruits, Mr Vikram Nair, GPC member for Home Affairs and Law, and MP for Sembawang GRC congratulated all recruits and reaffirmed the values of SCDF in ensuring the safety of our nation, especially as we celebrate 55 years of National Service in Singapore this year.Congratulations to the recruits of 163rd Intake! You have officially become Rescuers of the Life Saving Force. We look forward to your service and contributions to the nation.SCDFCelebratesNS55ANationofLifesavers

[SCDF rescues 14 cats from fire]On 21 April 2022 at about 8.30am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at Block 422 Fajar Road. The fire involved the contents of a service yard in a unit on the second floor of the block. Firefighters from Bukit Batok Fire Station conducted forcible entry into the unit and extinguished the fire using three compressed air foam backpacks. SCDF rescued 14 cats that were found unconscious within the unit. The firefighters, some of them cross-trained as emergency medical technicians, provided oxygen and conducted CardioPulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) on the cats. 13 of the cats eventually regained consciousness, while one had passed away.About 20 people were evacuated from neighbouring units as a precautionary measure. The cause of the fire is under investigation.Picture: / TikTok

[Fire @ Kusu Island]At approximately 6.30pm yesterday on 17 April in the midst of a heavy downpour, SCDFs marine and land-based firefighting forces responded to a fire at Kusu island, one of the offshore islands on the southern coast of Singapore. SCDF despatched a Marine Rescue Vessel (MRV) and a Rapid Response Fire Vessel (RFV) from Brani Marine Fire Station and West Coast Marine Fire Station. An additional firefighting crew from Marina Bay Fire Station was also despatched and responded aboard the RFV. Upon SCDF's arrival at the island, the fire was raging at a cluster of shrines located on top of a hill. Using the MRV as a water pump, the firefighters laid a vast number of hoses from the jetty to the top of the hill, covering a distance of about 520 meters. The fire was extinguished with two water jets within an hour of SCDF's arrival on the island.There were no reported injuries. Damping down* operations are ongoing. The cause of the fire is under investigation. *Damping down refers to the application of water to burnt surfaces immediately after a fire is put out. It is to prevent any potential rekindling of fire from hot burnt surfaces.

From today, you may notice that some of our SCDF frontliners and enforcement officers are equipped with body-worn cameras (BWCs). The recorded footages from BWCs will be used for coaching and training purposes to further improve SCDF officers' performances. It will also help to ensure greater accountability and transparency in our officers' interactions with members of the public, including deterring potential abuse against the officers. In the long run, BWCs will livestream footages to SCDF's Operations Centre so as to enhance SCDF's commanders real-time situational awareness during an ongoing situation. Since its pilot implementation in 2015, the collection, storage and usage of recorded data from BWCs have been and will be strictly controlled and safeguarded.

You would have seen or heard about SCDFs latest Mandarin drama serial, In Safe Hands (with English subtitles), which was aired daily on Mediacorp channel 8 from 7 March to 18 March this year. The making of In Safe Hands was a challenging but truly enriching experience for the Mediacorp production team, artistes and several SCDF officers. Rescue 995 goes behind the scenes of 'In Safe Hands' and this time in an exclusive interview (Part 2) with Loh Woon Woon, Mediacorp Executive Producer; Oh Wei Ting and Lau Ching Poon, Mediacorp script writers; two SCDF production advisers namely Lieutenant Colonel (LTC) Khaisarah Mansor and Major (MAJ) Shafi Rafie, as well as the SCDF casts: LTC Ryan Hoo Wei Kun, Staff Sergeant (SSG) Gregory Ryan and SSG Kamarul Arifin. Read more on their experiences in this second and final interview series of In Safe Hands. Link in our bio! (10-minute read)

For todays International Siblings Day, meet brothers SSG Muhammad Kamarul Arifin Bin Kamarruddin and SGT2 Muhammad Kamarul Hanafi Bin Kamarruddin, two of many siblings in SCDF! SSG Kamarul is currently a Fire and Rescue Specialist and like many older siblings, he is a role model to his younger bro. In fact, his passion to serve in the Force has inspired his younger brother to be an SCDF Paramedic !While they have different responsibilities and commitments as adults, both brothers still make it a point to go out regularly with their parents.As a testament to how close they have been and still are, the brothers have recreated some of their childhood pictures Heres a shoutout from The Life Saving Force to all siblings - Happy International Siblings Day! (Psst: SSG Kamarul plays Deputy Rota Commander WO Malik in the recent Mediacorp channel 8 drama, In Safe Hands, that was aired last month!)

[163rd BRT Intake]We warmly welcome our newly enlisted recruits to The Life Saving Force.Generations before them had served National Service (NS), now it is time for these young men to go through the rite of passage in contributing to a safe and secure Singapore.Recruits from the 163rd Basic Rescue Training (BRT) Intake were enlisted into NS at the National Service Training Centre (NSTC) of the Civil Defence Academy yesterday, meeting strangers who will soon be their buddies and brothers-in-training.Their parents and loved ones also had a chance to send them off physically at the academy and get a glimpse of the training that the recruits will be undergoing, a practice that was put on hiatus for the past two years due to COVID-19. Remember to follow here on our Facebook page to get first-hand glimpse into their training and lives as SCDF recruits. Lets show them our support by leaving words of encouragement in the comment section below!Check out more photos of the enlistment day here: go.gov.sg/163brtSCDFCelebratesNS55ANationOfLifeSavers

[Four Sport Singapore staff successfully resuscitate a cardiac arrest patient] On the afternoon of 15 Feb 2022, staff Mr Guo Ze, Mr Luo Shiwei, Mr Kow Heng Bee and Ms Lee Pei Shan were alerted to a collapsed man at Kallang Basin Swimming Complex.Upon assessing that the man was not breathing and had no pulse, the team immediately conducted Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and used an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) before SCDF's arrival. The patient's pulse returned and he eventually regained consciousness. On Monday (28 Mar 2022), the four lifesavers were each awarded the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. The awards were presented by COL Shaiful Herman Bin Shali, Commander, 1st SCDF Division. Thank you Mr Guo, Mr Luo, Mr Kow and Ms Lee for saving a life! You too can learn basic firefighting, first aid and CPR-AED in the physical session of the SCDF's CEPP or attend its e-modules session online at CommunityFirstResponders CommunityLifesaversANationofLifesavers OurCFRsOurHeroesFrom L to R:COL Shaiful Herman Bin Shali, Commander, 1st SCDF Division, Mr Sng Hock Lin, Chief, ActiveSG, Mr Luo Shiwei, Mr Guo Ze, Mr Kow Heng Nee, Ms. Lee Pei Shan and Mr Jeremy Sho, Senior Centre Manager, ActiveSG.

[SCDF e-Calendar 2022]Ushering in the month of April is SGT2 Muhammad Elaf Tan Wei, a Section Commander at Woodlands Fire Station who signed on with SCDF immediately after his full-time National Service (NS). With his burning passion and infectious energy, SGT Elaf is your friendly neighbourhood firefighter whom you can count on to protect and save lives and properties Beside SGT Elaf is the Pumper Firefighting Machine (PFM), a versatile firefighting robot capable of traversing up and down staircases. It is utilised to mitigate fires at factories and shophouses, and is robust enough to withstand up to 250C of heat in close proximity for 10 continuous minutes without any loss of functionality. Stay tuned for more of our e-calendar where we'll feature an SCDF officer in each successive month! TheLifeSavingForceANationofLifeSavers

On 1 April 2022 at about 6.35am, SCDF was alerted to a road traffic accident near the junction of Lok Yang Way and First Lok Yang Road. Upon SCDF's arrival at the incident scene, a passenger bus was found overturned on its side. Another passenger bus had rammed into a fence by the roadside and a man was pinned in the driver's seat. Firefighters from Jurong Fire Station used hydraulic rescue equipment to free the man. The man was subsequently pronounced dead at the scene by an SCDF paramedic. As there were multiple casualties involved in this accident, the first-arriving SCDF paramedic established a triaging system to prioritise the casualties according to the severity of their injuries. Casualties with severe injuries were treated and conveyed to the hospitals as priority. Additional ambulances and medical resources were also dispatched to support the ongoing operation. A Mass Decontamination Vehicle (MDV) from SCDF's Special Rescue Unit (SRU) was also activated to the incident. Responders from the SRU, comprising Full-time National Servicemen, configured their MDV into a casualty conveyance vehicle. The MDV subsequently conveyed 14 casualties to Ng Teng Fong General Hospital.A total of 37 casualties were conveyed by SCDF to Ng Teng Fong General Hospital and National University Hospital.

[Commemorating a Decade of Marine Transformation]On this day a decade ago, SCDFs Marine Division (MD) was officially established. Fast forward 10 years and here we are today Bigger. Faster. Stronger. A commemorative event was held earlier this morning to mark this significant milestone. Gracing the event as the Guest-of-Honour was Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS) for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development.SCDFs MD would not be where we are today without the hard work of our committed marine officers, including NSFs and ORNSmen. To honour the efforts of our pioneer officers who took on the challenge of building up this Division since 2012, a specially designed Marine Medallion was presented by Assoc Prof Faishal to ten long serving officers.In attendance at the ceremony were representatives from related agencies such as Police Coast Guard, , , Maritime Security Task Force and . Each of these agencies have supported the MD over the past decade.As we journey ahead, MD will, among other things, be pursuing the use of more advanced and unmanned technologies in fire and rescue operations. We also look forward to expand our fleet of next generation marine vessels with enhanced capabilities, as well as establishing a new Division HQ and a third Marine Fire Post at Punggol by 2025. Psst. If you want to find out more about MD's transformation in the past decade, please visit the Civil Defence Heritage Gallery located at Central Fire Station at 62 Hill Street.SCDFMarineTurns10ADecadeOfTransformation

[Commemorating a Decade of Marine Transformation]On this day a decade ago, SCDFs Marine Division (MD) was officially established. Fast forward 10 years and here we are today Bigger. Faster. Stronger. A commemorative event was held earlier this morning to mark this significant milestone. Gracing the event as the Guest-of-Honour was Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS) for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development.SCDFs MD would not be where we are today without the hard work of our committed marine officers, including NSFs and ORNSmen. To honour the efforts of our pioneer officers who took on the challenge of building up this Division since 2012, a specially designed Marine Medallion was presented by Assoc Prof Faishal to ten long serving officers.In attendance at the ceremony were representatives from related agencies such as Police Coast Guard, , , Maritime Security Task Force and . Each of these agencies have supported the MD over the past decade.As we journey ahead, MD will, among other things, be pursuing the use of more advanced and unmanned technologies in fire and rescue operations. We also look forward to expand our fleet of next generation marine vessels with enhanced capabilities, as well as establishing a new Division HQ and a third Marine Fire Post at Punggol by 2025. Psst. If you want to find out more about MD's transformation in the past decade, please visit the Civil Defence Heritage Gallery located at Central Fire Station at 62 Hill Street.SCDFMarineTurns10ADecadeOfTransformation

SCDFs latest Mandarin drama serial, In Safe Hands (with English subtitles), was aired daily on Mediacorp Channel 8 from 7 March to 18 March this year. [Fire @ Block 121 Bukit Merah View]At approximately 11.45am today (30 Mar), SCDF responded to a fire at the above-mentioned location. Upon the arrival of SCDF emergency responders, the fire was already raging in the living room-cum-bedroom of a one-room residential unit on the 2nd floor.Firefighters from Alexandra Fire Station and Central Fire Station donned breathing apparatus sets and carefully manoeuvred their way into the heavily smoky unit. The fire was extinguished using a water jet. The rest of the unit was affected by heat and smoke damage.Two persons from the affected unit had self-evacuated prior to the arrival of SCDF forces. In addition, about 35 people from the affected block were subsequently evacuated by Police and SCDF. A person sustained burn injuries while another four persons suffered from smoke inhalation. SCDF conveyed them to Singapore General Hospital.The cause of the fire is under investigation.

Did you know that SCDFs Marine Division has grown from a mere two fireboats to a fleet of six vessels with robust response capabilities? These vessels are equipped to handle maritime emergencies such as fires and rescue cases as well as incidents involving chemical, biological and radiological elements. These are truly critical functions to safeguard Singapore as one of the worlds biggest ports. From L to R: Heavy Rescue Vessel (HRV), Heavy Fire Vessel (HFV), Marine Rescue Vessel (MRV). Foreground: Rapid Response Fire Vessels (RFV).

[Three Good Samaritans assisted during a fire at Block 29 Chai Chee Avenue] On the morning of 8 Mar 2022, three Good Samaritans assisted during a fire at the above-mentioned location. Mr Kam Chee Wai was tending to his stall when he was alerted to smoke and fire from a neighbouring stall. Springing into action, he grabbed a nearby fire extinguisher and attempted to put out the fire. Mr Raymond Liew Choon Pang was also tending to his stall nearby and told his fellow stall holders to turn off their kitchen exhaust system to prevent the fire from spreading. Mr Raymond subsequently used additional fire extinguishers to fight the fire with Mr Kam. Ms Toh Mary, a staff member from the nearby supermarket, noticed the smoke coming from the direction of the stall. She immediately grabbed additional fire extinguishers from the supermarket and brought them over to continue with the firefighting efforts. On Saturday (26 Mar 2022), the three Good Samaritans were each awarded with the SCDF Community First Responder Award. The award was presented by Mr Tan Chuan-Jin, Speaker of Parliament, Advisor for Marine Parade GRC Grassroots Organisations. Kudos to these brave individuals for their prompt and exemplary actions! You too can learn basic firefighting, first aid and CPR-AED in the physical session of the SCDF's CEPP or attend its e-modules session online at CommunityFirstResponders CommunityLifesaversANationofLifesavers OurCFRsOurHeroes

The enhanced AED-on-Wheels Programme was launched on 25 February 2022 to equip drivers with Automated External Defibrillators (AED) in their privately-owned vehicles.For a start, in phase one of the programme, there are 50 trained participating drivers. They have been trained to conduct Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and operate an AED, and will be alerted to cardiac arrest cases via the SCDFs myResponder app within a 1.5 kilometres radius of their location.Rescue 995 engaged two of the volunteers in this programme as they share their enthusiastic support for the programme.Read more on their stories through the link in our bio. [Good Samaritans saved lives at Labrador Jetty and Kusu Island] On 1 Feb 2022, Mr Hadnan Bin Yaacob and Mr Mohammed Fazly Bin Ahmad Roslisham were at their family get-together at Labrador Park when a man fell into the sea from Labrador Jetty. Mr Hadnan and Mr Fazly immediately jumped into the water to rescue the unconscious man. Once on shore, Mr Hadnan commenced Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) on the man who subsequently regained consciousness. On 12 Feb 2022, Mr Joaquin Sanchez and Mr Inigo Nicolas Ortiz were at Kusu Island when they heard shouts for help. Rushing towards the direction of the cries, they saw a floating figure in the sea. Without hesitation, Mr Joaquin and Mr Ortiz jumped into the sea and brought the unresponsive man back to shore. They commenced CPR on the man who subsequently regained his breathing. For their prompt life saving actions, the four Good Samaritans were each awarded with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award on 3 Mar 2022. The award was presented by COL Shaiful Herman Bin Shali, Commander, 1st SCDF Division. Kudos to these brave individuals who stepped forward to help others during an emergency situation! You too can learn basic firefighting, first aid and CPR-AED in the physical session of the SCDFs CEPP or attend its e-modules session online at

We're glad many of you enjoyed our recent video on Exercise Carina where we responded to a simulated chemical agent release incident! You may have noticed that some of our responders were wearing different types of protective suits during the exercise. Learn more about each of these suits - their unique design and function by scrolling through the pics!: PTE Muhammad Syukri Bin Mohd Salim from the Media Production Unit of SCDF Corporate Communications DepartmentPic 2: The yellow and black attire with reflective strips are the most commonly seen gear worn by SCDF frontliners during firefighting operations.Pic 3: These grey attire, known as the Nuclear, Biological and Chemical (NBC) protective suits are worn by SCDF emergency responders to a HazMat incident. These suits protect them against direct contact with/ being contaminated by radioactive, biological or chemical substances.Pic 4: The red suits are the High Performance Suits (HPS), and are worn by our HazMat specialists. It protects responders from hazardous chemicals in solid, liquid, gas and/or vapour form and has been tested against known chemical warfare agents. Pic 5: These are the Light Decontamination Suit (LDS), which are usually donned by rescuers from the Special Rescue Unit (SRU) as they decontaminate casualties under a water shower. It can provide responders with up to 24 hours of protection in liquid and vapour-hazard areas.

Learn more about each of these suits - their unique design and function by scrolling through the pics!: PTE Muhammad Syukri Bin Mohd Salim from the Media Production Unit of SCDF Corporate Communications DepartmentPic 2: The yellow and black attire with reflective strips are the most commonly seen gear worn by SCDF frontliners during firefighting operations.Pic 3: These grey attire, known as the Nuclear, Biological and Chemical (NBC) protective suits are worn by SCDF emergency responders to a HazMat incident. These suits protect them against direct contact with/ being contaminated by radioactive, biological or chemical substances.Pic 4: The red suits are the High Performance Suits (HPS), and are worn by our HazMat specialists. It protects responders from hazardous chemicals in solid, liquid, gas and/or vapour form and has been tested against known chemical warfare agents. Pic 5: These are the Light Decontamination Suit (LDS), which are usually donned by rescuers from the Special Rescue Unit (SRU) as they decontaminate casualties under a water shower. It can provide responders with up to 24 hours of protection in liquid and vapour-hazard areas.

[Exercise Bluewhale Mar 2022] Earlier this week, SCDF conducted a marine emergency response exercise in the southern part of Singapore. The exercise was supported by and The exercise scenario involved the release of a chemical agent (CA) onboard a ferry carrying 60 passengers. Many passengers who were exposed to the toxic CA vapour started convulsing and vomiting, and one passenger fell overboard in a bid to escape the fumes. Such a challenging scenario is important as it allows SCDF to test and fine-tune its ops coordination between its Marine Division and Land Divisions , including validating and updating its operational plans and procedures with related agencies. During the exercise, about 20 emergency and supporting vehicles, including marine vessels from SCDF and related agencies, were deployed. Check out the pictures on SCDFs operational response to such an incident! By the way, did you know that it has been almost a decade since SCDF set up its marine firefighting and rescue capability? Over the years, SCDFs marine firefighters and vessels have responded to numerous fire and rescue incidents as well as exercises like the one above. Keep a lookout for an upcoming 4-part series as we celebrate SCDF's Marine Division's 10th year anniversary!ANationofLifesavers

[Fire @ Block 29 Chai Chee Avenue]At approximately 6.45am today (8 Mar), SCDF responded to a fire at the above-mentioned location. The fire involved contents of three stalls and a kitchen exhaust ducting (KED) in a coffeeshop. Prior to SCDF's arrival, some members of the public had assisted to mitigate the fire using fire extinguishers. The fire was extinguished by firefighters with two water jets.About 15 people had self-evacuated upon the occurrence of the fire and there were no reported injuries. Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire had originated from overheated cooking from one of the fire-affected stalls.SCDF would like to remind the public, especially stall holders, on the prevention of KED fires with the following fire safety tips as depicted on the infographic.

International Womens Day recognises the accomplishments of women around the world.Like the rest of the world, we are proud to celebrate the experiences and achievements of the women in SCDF.Featured here are three of our lady officers , CPT Pek Hong Kun, LTA Gangadevi D/O Rountan and WO1 Dan Qiong, and their thoughts on being in the Life Saving Force.Besides being our frontline leaders, these ladies, like many out there, are someones mother, daughter, sister, aunt, niece, cousin, friend, neighbour On this very special day, lets give a SHOUT OUT to all the women in our lives, and show them our love and appreciation Happy International Womens Day!2nd picture credits: Ministry of Home AffairsIWD2022

< In Safe Hands >We are just 3 days away from the premiere of the Mediacorp-SCDF drama In Safe Hands!To prepare for their roles, Mediacorp artistes went through a series of training sessions with our SCDF frontline officers in August 2021 to ensure realistic portrayal of their roles in the drama. This included a series of hands-on sessions on emergency medical protocols, firefighting techniques, the handling of SCDF's latest technological gadgets and even taking rides on SCDF emergency appliances. Check out on some of the highlights here! Stay tuned for the premiere of In Safe Hands, an exclusive drama (with English subtitles) on The Life Saving Force on 7 March at 7.30pm. Do look out for some of our very own multi-racial SCDF personnel starring alongside the cast! InSafeHands #mediacorpInSafeHandsANationOfLifesaversTheLifeSavingForce

The tragic fire at Robinsons departmental store in November 1972 served as a lesson that we should never take fire safety for granted. Since then, stringent measures were taken to prevent and protect residential and commercial premises from fire. That includes ensuring that all fire hydrants are in good working condition every year!More recently, SCDF and Public Utilities Board introduced the Smart Hydrant a newly designed, intelligent fire hydrant that is not only easier and faster to operate but also a game changer for SCDFs frontline operations.Read more on our fire hydrants their past, present and future through the link in our bio.

Today marks the official opening of SCDF's 23rd fire station, (PFS)! It was officially opened by SM Teo Chee Hean, Senior Minister and Co-ordinating Minister for National Security earlier this morning.Co-located with at 151 Punggol Central, PFS aims to provide faster emergency response to the existing Punggol town and upcoming developments like the Punggol Digital District. Sharing the compound and various facilities with a fellow Home Team Department offers greater ease of information and resources sharing, and fosters enhanced rapport within the Home Team. It also provides greater opportunity for joint community engagements to serve Punggol residents better Psst! Did you know that PFS is SCDFs first Smart Fire Station equipped with cutting-edge technologies, unique training infrastructure, and a dedicated community engagement facility? Scroll through the pics to check out some features that make PFS a smart station!

[Two Good Samaritans assisted in evacuating neighbours during a fire]On 7 February 2022, two residents assisted in evacuating neighbours during a unit fire on the 14th floor at Blk 688F Woodlands Drive 75.Mr Deevak S/O Premdas was in the neighbourhood when a family member called him to inform that there was a fire at his block. Mr Marcus Lim Chin Keat had just returned home from work when he was also alerted to the fire. Working as a team, the duo alerted and assisted neighbours, including two persons with disabilities, to evacuate. Yesterday, on 20 February 2022, Mr Deevak and Mr Marcus were awarded the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. The award was presented by Mr Vikram Nair, Member of Parliament for Sembawang GRC. Kudos to these brave individuals for their prompt and exemplary actions during the emergency.You too can learn basic firefighting, first aid and CPR-AED in the physical session of the SCDF's CEPP or attend its e-modules session online at CommunityFirstResponders CommunityLifesaversANationofLifesavers OurCFRsOurHeroesFrom L to RFront row: Mr Deevak S/O Premdas, Mr Marcus Lim Chin Keat. Back row: COL Lim Beng Hui, Commander, 3rd SCDF Division, Mr Vikram Nair, MP for Sembawang GRC, COL Bob Tan, Deputy Director, Volunteer and Community Partnership Department.

The SCDF annual statistics for Emergency Medical Services (EMS), Fire Incidents and Fire Safety Enforcement for Year 2021 were released today.In a nutshell:1 While the total number of ambulance calls increased by 11.9% compared to 2020, there was a decrease of 8.1% in the number of false alarm calls.2 The number of fire calls fell by 1.8% from 2020. The leading cause of fires that occurred in residential premises are unattended cooking, electrical sources and household content. 3 The number of fires involving Personal Mobility Devices (PMDs) and Power Assisted Bicycles (PABs) saw a significant decrease of 19.1% from 2020.Scroll through to find out more about the statistics.

Like all museums, the Civil Defence Heritage Gallery (CDHG) offer visitors a glimpse into the past. However, a visit to the CDHG is not all about an eye-opening experience of the Civil Defence development in Singapore from the late 1800s. It is also a journey on the SCDF today and even a peep into the near future. Since its opening in 2001, the gallery has hosted more than 800,000 local and international visitors! In December last year, the CDHG commemorated its twentieth anniversary.Rescue 995 took an exclusive tour of the gallery with Mr Subandi Bin Somo, the resourceful Manager of CDHG.Read more on the gallery through the link in our bio!
