[Seven Good Samaritans To The Rescue In Vehicular Fires]On 13 Jan 2022 at about 7.30am, a car traveling along Bartley Road near Maris Stella High School caught fire. Upon seeing heavy smoke emitting from the car, Mr Raymond Seah Yong Huat, Operations Manager of Maris Stella High School, took a total of three fire extinguishers to extinguish the fire. Meanwhile, the security officer of the school, Mr Suani Bin Surani, assisted the passengers to evacuate from the burning car.In another incident on 27 Dec 2021 at about 3.00pm, a car caught fire while traveling along Farrer Road. Seeing the fire from across the road, Mr Kadhirvel Murugavadivel and Mr Veeraiyan Somaskandan rushed to assist the occupants of the car to evacuate before successfully extinguishing the fire by means of fire extinguishers and a water hose. In the last incident on 23 Dec 2021 at about 6.20pm, a car caught fire while traveling along Victoria Street. Mr Alamin Md, Mr Uddin Rokan and Mr Nasir, who were working at a nearby construction site, sprung into action and used a few fire extinguishers to mitigate the fire. After extinguishing the fire, the trio established a cordon around the smoky car to deter others from being too close to it.Yesterday on 26 Jan 2022, these seven Good Samaritans were each awarded with the SCDF Community First Responder Award. The awards were presented by COL Shaiful Herman Bin Shali, Commander 1st SCDF Division. Kudos to these civic-minded individuals for their prompt and exemplary actions! Be a Community First Responder and help others during emergency situations. CommunityFirstResponders CommunityLifesaversANationofLifesavers OurCFRsOurHeroes

[Fire @ No. 20 Jalan Samulun]At about 12.25am this morning (25 Jan), SCDF responded to a fire at the above-mentioned location. Upon arrival, firefighters from Tuas Fire Station immediately deployed resources to surround and contain the fire which involved a large pile of construction waste measuring about 20 metres by 20 metres and 6 metres in height. Firefighters had to don breathing apparatus sets to navigate through the smoke-logged environment to conduct the firefighting operation. The fire was brought under control within 30 minutes.A total of 40 firefighters were deployed and at the height of the operation, four water jets and an Unmanned Firefighting Machine (UFM) were used to contain the fire. Foam was also used to cover the surface of the waste, a more effective firefighting strategy for fires which are deep-seated. On 22 Nov 2021 at about 7.50am, Mr Jway Boon Seng suffered a cardiac arrest while traveling on an MRT train. Alerted by a call for help via the train's emergency communication button, Station Manager Mr Xam Tan Ying Hao sprang into action. He brought Mr Jway out of the train and onto Canberra MRT Station with the help of a few other passengers. Thereafter, together with Dr Lee Wei Sheng and Mr Kelvin Tan Jiong Hao, the trio performed Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and used an Automated External Defibrillator (AED). Mr Jway survived the cardiac arrest and he is deeply grateful for the prompt intervention by the Community Lifesavers. Mr Kelvin has since been enlisted as a full-time national serviceman with the SCDF. In another incident on 20 Dec 2021, taxi driver, Mr Sin York Tan was driving his taxi when he noticed an injured motorcyclist at the junction of Upper Serangoon Road and Hougang Street 21. Mr Sin is a Community First Responder (CFR) under the SCDF-ComfortDelGro AED-on-Wheels programme and trained in basic life saving skills through the SCDF's Community Emergency Prepardness Programme (CEPP). He immediately stopped his taxi safely, grabbed a first aid kit from the taxi and attended to the injured casualty. Yesterday on 14 Jan 2022, these four Good Samaritans were each awarded the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award and Community First Responder Award by the SCDF. The awards were presented by COL Lim Beng Hui, Commander 3rd SCDF Division. For Mr Sin, this is the second time in which he had received such an award. He had previously rendered assistance in another road traffic accident on 22 Nov 2021. Kudos to these brave individuals who stepped forward to help others during emergency situations! You too can learn basic firefighting, first aid and CPR-AED in the physical session of the SCDF's CEPP or attend its e-modules session online at CommunityFirstResponders CommunityLifesaversANationofLifesavers OurCFRsOurHeroes

[Fire @ Blk 366 Bukit Batok Street 31] At about 2.40pm this afternoon (14 Jan), SCDF was alerted to a fire at the above-mentioned location. The fire involved the contents of a bedroom on the 4th floor. The occupants of the unit had evacuated before SCDF's arrival. Firefighters from Bukit Batok Fire Station conducted forcible entry into the unit and extinguished the fire using a water jet. As a result of the fire, the bedroom was affected by heat and smoke damage. There were no reported injuries. The cause of the fire is under investigation. We understand that a member of the public had mitigated the fire using a water hose before SCDFs arrival. SCDF will be reaching out to commend the person for his quick-thinking and prompt action in managing the emergency situation.

On the afternoon of 4 Jan 2022, five members of public and a Bus Captain were recognised with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award (CLA) for stepping forward during two separate fire incidents. On 8 Oct 2021, Bus Captain Mr Mohd Azim Bin M Rosley was plying bus service 99 when he encountered a motorcycle on fire along Jalan Boon Lay. He stopped his bus safely at a bus stop nearby and took a fire extinguisher from his bus to fight the fire. Within minutes, he had swiftly extinguished the flames and resumed his bus route. In another incident on 20 Oct 2021, a fire broke out in a 7th floor unit of Blk 470 Choa Chu Kang Avenue 3. Siblings, Mr Muhammad Rusyaidi Bin Abdul Rashid and Ms Intan Sabrina Binte Abdul Rashid were alerted to the fire and assisted to evacuate children from the affected unit before alerting all other residents on the same floor to evacuate. Ms Linda Lim Lay Kuan, Ms Cynthia Loh Bee Kheng and Mr Vincent Lau Chee Wah were alerted to the smoke from the affected unit and assisted with evacuation efforts of the affected block, as well as calling 995. The award presentation was graced by Mr Murali Pillai, Member of Parliament for Bukit Batok SMC. The awards were presented by COL Goh Boon Han, Commander 4th SCDF Division.Kudos to these brave individuals who stepped forward to help!You too can learn basic firefighting, first aid and CPR-AED in the physical session of the SCDF's Community Emergency Preparedness Programme (CEPP) or attend its e-modules session online at CommunityLifesaversANationofLifesavers OurCFRsOurHeroes

[24th Rota Commander Course (RCC) Commissioning Ceremony]After undergoing seven months of rigorous training, 48 officer cadets from the 24th Rota Commander Course (RCC) were commissioned as SCDF Senior Officers at the Civil Defence Academy earlier this morning.The RCC commissioning ceremony is a significant milestone that marks the transition of these 48 individuals, including 28 full-time national servicemen, into SCDF Senior Officers. As Senior Officers, their tasks include leading a team each to respond to a wide multitude of incidents such as firefighting and rescue operations. Unlike previous batches, the 24th RCC is also the first batch with four in-service Paramedics among the cadets who have embarked on their journey to become Paramedic Senior Officers. This is part of the new Paramedic Senior Officer Scheme which aims to further drive SCDF's Emergency Medical Services development.In a virtual speech delivered by Associate Professor Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, he acknowledged the strong support of family members and friends of the cadets in helping them to reach this significant milestone. He also observed that despite the challenges posed by the pandemic, SCDF's core functions of firefighting, rescue and emergency medical services remained steadfast and unwaivered.On the very same training grounds where months of learning and intense training took place, the cadets stood proudly and were officially commissioned as SCDF Senior Officers. Congratulations to the 24th RCC! We wish them all the best as they venture forth in their journey with the Life Saving Force. [Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, Safe Management Measures (SMM) were observed at the event for all attendees.]ANationofLifesavers

On 29 Nov 2021 at about 6.15pm, six Good Samaritans and an SCDF Operationally Ready National Serviceman (ORNS) saved the life of a man who had a cardiac arrest and had fallen along the staircase entrance at Marymount MRT Station.Corporal (NS) Vincent Yong De Hao was on his way home after completing his operational standby at Bishan Fire Station as part of his In-Camp Training, when he noticed the cardiac arrest victim and sprung into action to assess him. Eldercare facility colleagues Ms Jacqueline Teo Mei Ling and Ms Kam Siew Yuen who were passing by, joined Corporal (NS) Vincent to render assistance.SMRT Senior Station Manager (SSM) Mr Gary Tan Kian Kok & Assistant Station Manager (ASM) Mr Shakirin Bin Sarip, who were on duty at the Marymount MRT Station, were alerted of the incident. Upon assessing the situation, SSM Gary immediately grabbed an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) from the passenger service counter, while ASM Shakirin called 995.Working as a team, the five lifesavers took turns to perform CPR-AED.Shortly after SCDFs arrival, off-duty nurses Ms Hannah Thang Hui Li & Ms Carmelita B. Lumayag joined the other Good Samaritans in conducting CPR-AED and assisting SCDFs Emergency Medical Services.Yesterday morning, these community first responders were presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award by COL Shaiful Herman Bin Shali, Commander, 1st SCDF Division. Corporal (NS) Vincent will be commended with the SCDF Service Excellence Award.You too can learn basic firefighting, first aid and CPR-AED in the physical session of the SCDFs Community Emergency Preparedness Programme (CEPP) or attend its e-modules session online at From L to R: COL Shaiful Herman Bin Shali, Commander, 1st SCDF Division, Ms Kam Siew Yuen, Ms Hannah Thang Hui Li, SSM Gary Tan Kian Kok, Ms Jacqueline Teo Mei Ling, ASM Shakirin Bin Sarip, COL Bob Tan, Deputy Director, Volunteer and Community Partnership Department. Not in picture: Ms Carmelita B. Lumayag, Corporal (NS) Vincent Yong De Hao.

Yesterday (13 Dec 2021), five members of the public were awarded the Community Lifesaver Award (CLA), in recognition of their public-spiritedness and gallant efforts in two separate incidents. The two incidents involved 1 a residential unit on fire and 2 a cardiac arrest victim.1 In the first incident, Mr Goh Boon Hong was alerted to his neighbours cries for help when a fire broke out in her kitchen. With the help of 2 other Community First Responders (CFRs), Mr Goh extinguished the fire using a fire extinguisher from his home before SCDFs arrival. I bought an extinguisher because I dont know when Ill need it, said Mr Goh.2 In the second incident, Mr Darryl Lee responded to an alert on his myResponder app notifying him of a cardiac arrest case. Upon his arrival at the incident site, he saw a group of CFRs performing CPR on the victim. He proceeded to assist by administering oxygen to the victim.I was very nervous, but I did what I could, said Mr Darryl when recounting the incident. I would give (Mr Darryl) full marks for his assistance that day. We couldnt have done it without him, said Dr Bernard Cheong, one of the other award recipients who resuscitated the cardiac arrest victim before SCDFs arrival. The award was presented by COL Goh Boon Han, Commander 4th SCDF Division, during an award presentation ceremony at HQ 4th SCDF Division. Kudos to the 5 Good Samaritans who stepped forward! Head to our SCDF Facebook page for more details of their collective CFR efforts!To learn more on what to do in such emergencies, join the online module of the SCDF's Community Emergency Prepardness Programme via the link in our bio or contact one of the four SCDF Division HQs to register for a practical class. [SCDFxSGEA Inaugural Esports Festival 2021: Brave the Heat!]Held on 5 December 2021 at Marina Bay Sands, the inaugural SCDF x Singapore Esports Association (SGEA) Esports Festival 2021: Brave the Heat, saw the top four teams coming together for the Mobile Legends Grand FinalsLaunched by SCDF in collaboration with , this inaugural esports festival attracts students from Institute of Higher Learning (IHL) and Full-time National Servicemen to test their communication and leadership skills as they battle against their opponents.After several rounds of gripping and nail-biting matches, Team EVOS Junior eventually emerged as the champion and the other three winning teams are Spirits (1stRunner Up), Bandits (2ndRunner Up) and Monarch (3rdRunner Up)! A huge thank you to our guests of honours, SCDFs Deputy Commissioner (DC) Teong How Hwa, Deputy Commissioner (Strategy & Corporate Services) and Mr Ng Chong Geng, President of SGEA, for gracing the event and presenting the awards to our SCDF X SGEA Esports Festival winners!Esteemed guests and members of public also got to witness an exciting exhibition match between professional Mobile Legends team, Team Kingsmen and Team 995, our very own SCDF Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MLBB) Esports Team!Congratulations once again to all the winning teams!Stay Pumped and Feel the Heat as we await our next eSports Festival.Catch the grand finals and the exciting match between Kingsmen and Team 995 here:

Were glad to see that young Bray is having fun at our virtual Fire Station Open House! Are you searching for a fun-filled activity for your child this December holiday?Join us at our virtual Fire Station Open House! Held over Zoom every Saturday, your child and yourself can expect to learn more about the various emergency vehicles, station routine, and useful tips on staying fire safe, all in the comfort of your own home!Of course, these open houses are not limited to just children and parents anyone can join us. As each Zoom session can only accommodate 300 persons, do sign up soon and we look forward to seeing you at the virtual open house! Register here: go.gov.sg/vfsoh

Besides SCDFs microsite and FB, our SCDF e-magazine, Rescue 995, is now on Instagram too! Keep your eyes peeled for our fortnightly articles that sheds more insights on the adrenaline pumping actions, rich activities and of course, the people behind the Life Saving Force.Now on this issue of Rescue 995 -Home Team Volunteer Network (HTVN) celebrated its decennial anniversary on 28 October 2021. Four outstanding volunteers were recognised for their leadership, strong commitment and active participation in volunteering for the Home Team (HT). Sixteen other HT volunteers received the Commendation Award for their exemplary service. Mr Yunnos Bin Shariff is one of the four HT volunteers who was awarded the HTVN Outstanding Volunteer Award. SCDFs MAJ (V) Tan Teow Chye, Officer Cadet Trainee (OCT) Adam Idris Lim Wei and Captain (NCDCC) Nur Fadliyana Binte Komarudin were among the sixteen volunteers who were awarded the HTVN Commendation Award for exemplary services. SCDF and Rescue 995 hereby salute our volunteers, our invaluable partners, in commemoration of the International Volunteer Day on 5th December. Read the full story through the link in our bio!

!On this special day, we applaud, commend and shout out to all our active SCDF volunteers our fellow lifesavers. They hail from numerous volunteer schemes namely, the Civil Defence Auxiliary Unit (CDAU), the National Civil Defence Corps (NCDCC) and the Civil Defence (CD) Lionhearters. The CD Lionhearters comprise youths in most of the local tertiary institutions as well as junior ones from primary schools yes, in SCDF, our volunteer lifesavers start young, some as young as 10 years of age!And of course, not forgetting the 102,418 (and counting) members of the public who have registered with the SCDFs myResponder app to be activated as the nations Community First Responders (CFRs) in the event of cardiac arrest or minor fire cases. Our volunteers and CFRs continue to serve their calling by not only stepping forward as fellow lifesavers to help those in distress but also as advocates to help us spread the word that there is a role for everyone in Emergency Preparedness. As the late Mr Kofi Annan, former United Nations Secretary-General, once said, , .THANK YOU to each and every one of you, across all ages, for your sacrifices and commitments to the noble cause and for bringing Singapore closer to being a !For those who are keen on volunteering with SCDF (or other Home Team departments), you may explore the opportunities via the link in our bio.ANationofLifesaversOurVolunteersOurHeroesOurCFRsOurLifesavers

As the late Mr Kofi Annan, former United Nations Secretary-General, once said, , .THANK YOU to each and every one of you, across all ages, for your sacrifices and commitments to the noble cause and for bringing Singapore closer to being a !For those who are keen on volunteering with SCDF (or other Home Team departments), you may explore the opportunities via the link in our bio.ANationofLifesaversOurVolunteersOurHeroesOurCFRsOurLifesavers

On the morning of 3 Dec 2021, 19 people were recognised with the SCDF Community First Responder Award (CFRA) and Community Lifesaver Award (CLA) for their life saving actions during two separate cardiac arrest incidents. On 27 Sep 2021, staff Mr Muhammad Adlan Bin Hasan Basri, Mr Steven Ismail Bin Muhammad, Mr Henry Tan Kim Heng and Mr Abdul Naqeeb Bin Abdul Latiff were alerted when an instructor had collapsed from cardiac arrest at Heartbeat. The team conducted Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and used an Automated External Defibrillator to successfully resuscitate the instructor before SCDF's arrival. In another incident on 7 Oct 2021, a worker had suffered from cardiac arrest at Pasir Ris Sport Centre. 15 people came together and conducted Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and used an Automated External Defibrillator until SCDF's arrival. The 15 people are staff Mr Steven Ong How Tiong, Mr Terence Yong Chen Ngiap, Mr Patrick Chan Lee Chong, Ms Norsidah Sheila Hassan, Mr Muhammad Shahir Bin Hamzah, Mr Chan Kok Hong, Mr Fred Leong Chong Wah, Mr Danny Yau Lay Swee, Mr Abdul Rahman Bin Salim, Mr Vincent Fong Peng Yuen, Ms Cecilia Sau Fong Chan, Mr John Lee Say Kheng, and members of public Mr Darren Tan Chun Yong, Mr Marcus Chia Ying Han and Mr Marvel Chua Tze-An. The awards were presented by COL Chew Keng Tok, Commander, 2nd SCDF Division. Kudos to the 19 Good Samaritans who stepped forward! You too can learn basic firefighting, first aid and CPR-AED in the physical session of the SCDF's Community Emergency Prepardness Programme (CEPP) or attend its e-modules session online at CommunityFirstResponders CommunityLifesaversANationofLifesavers OurCFRsOurHeroes

[ Community Lifesavers on the Road] On 22 Nov 2021 at about 11am, cabby, Mr Sin York Tan, was plying along Chin Swee Road in his taxi when he saw a person sitting by the roadside. He soon realised that a road traffic accident had occured between a car and a Power Assisted Bicycle (PAB). Mr Sin is a Community First Responder (CFR) under the SCDF-ComfortDelGro AED-on-Wheels programme. He had been trained in basic life saving skills by the SCDF in the Community Emergency Prepardness Programme. As an active and trained CFR, Mr Sin immediately stopped his taxi safely, grabbed a first aid kit from his taxi and attended to the casualty by the side of the road. Although the casualty had only sustained minor injuries but as a precautionary measure, Mr Sin stayed with him until the arrival of an SCDF ambulance. Mr Sin is no stranger to helping others in distress for he had rendered medical assistance to others and even extinguished a vehicle on fire.For proactively stepping forth to help others, Mr Sin was today presented with the SCDF Community First Responder Award by COL Shaiful Herman, Commander 1st SCDF Division. You too can learn basic firefighting, first aid and CPR-AED in the physical session of the SCDF's Community Emergency Prepardness Programme (CEPP) or attend its e-modules session online! Find out more through the link in our bio CommunityLifesaversANationofLifesavers OurCFRsOurHeroes

You may have heard of the road traffic accident that occured at the junction of North Bridge Road and Parliament Place on 14 Nov 2021 where members of the public stepped forward to render assistance. At a ceremony today, COL Shaiful Herman, Commander 1st SCDF Division, presented the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award to five Auxiliary Police Officers from Cisco who sprung into action, with instinct borne from years of service on the job.SSGT Mohammad Bin Jamaludin rescued a person inside an overturned car and attended to the person's injuries, while SGT Toh Jia Hong Jackson freed a person pinned under the overturned car, with the combined efforts of other members of public. SGT Kaliyaperumal Paramasivam, CPL Hanis Bin Harun and CPL Low Zhi Hao conducted checks to ensure there were no further casualties, managed the gathering crowd of onlookers and kept vehicular traffic clear to ensure SCDF's prompt arrival. Thank you officers for your lifesaving actions. There were also numerous members of the public who had rendered assistance. We would like to thank and recognize them for their community spiritedness in responding to this emergency, and we would appreciate if they could contact SCDF at 64717429 (during office hours). On 10 Nov 2021 at about 8.05pm, a family of three prevented a fire involving a Power Assisted Bicycle (PAB) from spreading along the 9th floor common corridor of Blk 94 Pipit Road. Mr Abdullah Bin Mohammad Taha, an SCDF ORNSman, sprung into action by calling 995 and commenced firefighting efforts using a fire extinguisher and buckets of water with his father, Mr Mohammad Taha Bin Abdullah. Meanwhile Mr Abdullah's stepmother, Mdm Nuraisha Binte Abdullah evacuated a wheelchair-bound neighbour to safety. Yesterday, 19 Nov 2021, the trio were presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award by Ms Tin Pei Ling, Member of Parliament for MacPherson SMC, for their crucial efforts in preventing the spread of the fire.Thank you Mr Abdullah, Mr Taha and Mdm Nuraisha for your timely intervention! CommunityLifesaverANationofLifesavers OurCFRsOurHeroesAMemberOfTheHomeTeamFrom L to R:Front Row - Mr Taha, Mdm Nuraisha, Mr AbdullahBack Row - COL Bob Tan, Deputy Director, Volunteer and Community Partnership Department, COL Chew Keng Tok, Commander, 2nd SCDF Division, Ms Tin Pei Ling, MP for MacPherson SMC, Mr Lim Cheng Huat, Chairman, MacPherson C2E.

You might have seen videos circulating online a few weeks ago of smoke billowing dramatically out from the SLE underpass. What you didn't see was the teamwork of a dynamic duo to save the day...On 2 November 2021, during the early evening rush hour traffic at about 5.00pm, two gentlemen rescued a driver from a car that was on fire at the exit 1 slip road of the underpass along SLE (towards BKE).One of these gentlemen, Mr Johnson Chia Yong Lee, was driving along SLE when he saw a car careen across the road and hit the left wall of the underpass. He saw black smoke emitting from the damaged car and immediately stopped his car. Driven by a sense of duty, he got out of his car and rushed over to help.When he reached the affected car, a fire was developing within it. The driver was still in the burning car and in a daze! Mr Johnson opened the driver's door and swiftly brought the dazed driver out of the car. Another gentleman, Mr Azlee Bin Abd Shukor, was driving a van when he spotted black smoke and flames in the SLE underpass. Then, he saw Mr Johnson waving frantically for assistance. Realizing the precarious situation, he stopped his van alongside Mr Johnson.Working as a team, the duo brought the dazed driver into Mr Azlee's van. They then drove further down the road towards safety, away from the intense heat and smoke of the burning car.For their gallant rescue and timely intervention, Mr Johnson and Mr Azlee were each presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award by COL Lim Beng Hui, Commander 3rd SCDF Division, today.Kudos to Mr Johnson and Mr Azlee, our brave heroes! CommunityLifesaver ANationofLifesavers OurCFRsOurHeroes

Earlier this week, SCDF participated in Exercise High Crest (XHC), an annual multiagency exercise led by the Singapore Maritime Crisis Centre (SMCC)and involving resources from maritime related agencies including SCDFsMarine Division.Through this exercise, XHC21 aims to validate the Whole-of Government's response against potential attacks or threats on Singapores Key Coastal installations.It alsovalidatesthe national agencies'activation protocols, processes andoperationalresponses to neutralise such threats, including themanagement of the situation after the threat has been neutralised.Two SCDF vessels from our Marine Division, namely the Rapid Response Fire Vessel (RFV) and Heavy Rescue Vessel (HRV) were involved in the exercise.Both vessels responded to a simulated firefighting scenario out at sea.Check out some of the highlights from yesterday's exercise!

[Community Resilience Day @ 1st Div] On 30 October 2021, 1st SCDF Division held the first ever Community Resilience (CR) Day in collaboration with and QueenstownC2E Committee. The CR Day saw approximately 150 participants tuning in through zoom while about 40 participants were physically present (in accordance to prevailing SMMs) to learn essential life-saving skills on what to do during an emergency situation. Participants were trained in first aid, CPR & AED, and fire safety at home through a fun and engaging session led by the SCDF hosts. Parliamentary Secretary, Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth & Ministry of Social and Family Development, and Queenstown Grassroots Advisor Mr Eric Chua graced the event. In his address, he highlighted the importance of Community First Responders and the crucial role they play in lending a helping hand to others in times of emergency.This is vital in enabling our community to stay strong.Amidst the ongoing COVID-19 situation, SCDF will be imparting Emergency Preparedness skills in a series of hybrid Community Resilience Days to be rolled out by the four SCDF Divisions, in accordance to prevailing SMMs.In the meantime, do join these Queenstown residents in paving the way towards building ANationofLifesavers and learning lifesaving skills through the Community Emergency Preparedness Programme (CEPP). The CEPP is also available online.

Today, 10th October, is World Mental Health Day. Mental health struggles are not always outwardly visible. People struggling with mental health may often feel that they are stumbling through the dark with poor visibility and have no end in sight. To those who are grappling with mental health issues, remember that help is always available. There will always be light at the end of the tunnel Here at SCDF, we care.WorldMentalHealthDay TheLifeSavingForce: CPT Daven Tan

You would have heard of SCDF's Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) being proficient in height rescue operations, but did you know that they are also trained in scuba diving? This picture, taken by DART member , shows them during one of their training sessions at the Home Team Tactical Centre (HTTC). Hovering above them is the underwater Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) which aids in locating victims underwater. Through the use of sonar technology and an in-build camera, the ROV facilitates DART members to pinpoint the exact location of victims, hence boosting the efficiency of underwater search and rescue operations.

[Fire @ No. 86 Geylang Bahru]Earlier today at about 2.35am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the aforementioned location. Upon SCDF's arrival, the fire was well-alight in two ground floor units of a double storey industrial premises. Firefighters immediately deployed water jets around the exterior of the premises to contain the fire and prevent it from spreading. Simultaneously, forcible entry was conducted to create quick access into the burning units.Once the fire was under control, firefighters wearing breathing apparatus sets proceeded deep into the smoke-logged unit to locate the seat of fire. Firefighters had to exercise extreme caution as the second floor mezzanine level had already collapsed.The fire involving contents of a plumbing services workshop across two units was extinguished by SCDF in about two hours. The adjacent units sustained heat and smoke damages.SCDF deployed 17 emergency vehicles and about 60 firefighters to the incident. At the height of the firefighting operation, four water jets and an Unmanned Firefighting Machine (UFM) were deployed. A Combined Platform Ladder (CPL) was also utilised for aerial monitoring of the incident.A firefighter, a Full-Time National Serviceman (NSF), experienced slight smoke inhalation. He was conveyed to Singapore General Hospital and has since been discharged. There were no other reported injuries. SCDF is currently performing damping down* operations.*Damping down refers to the application of water to wet burnt surfaces immediately after a fire is put out. It is to prevent any potential rekindle of fire from the hot burnt surfaces.

[Fire @ No. 20 Tuas Ave 20] On 23 September 2021 at about 3.15pm, SCDF responded to a fire at No. 20 Tuas Ave 20. Upon SCDF's arrival, an electrical switchroom on the first floor was smoke-logged. SCDF firefighters wearing breathing apparatus sets entered the premises cautiously to locate the fire. The fire involved a chimney fan switch in the electrical switchroom. SCDF extinguished a few pockets of fire with two dry powder fire extinguishers. SCDF conveyed two persons to the Singapore General Hospital for burn injuries*. A person was pronounced dead at the scene by an SCDF paramedic.About 80 people self-evacuated from the premises. SCDF is investigating the cause of the fire. *Patients who suffered smoke inhalation or serious burn injuries but are in stable condition, will be conveyed to Singapore General Hospital's specialised Burn Centre instead of the nearest hospital.

On the night of 29 May 2021, a man was cycling at Jurong Lake Gardens when he suffered from a cardiac arrest and collapsed. Mr Tang Jie and Mr Leong Wai Kit, on-duty lifeguards, were at the nearby Jurong Lake Gardens Swimming Complex when they were alerted to the emergency by a passerby. The two lifeguards grabbed an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) from the swimming complex and ran over to Jurong Lake Gardens. Together with an unknown Good Samaritan, they performed Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) on the victim. The lifesaving trio continued conducting CPR-AED until the arrival of an SCDF ambulance. The victim was successfully revived at scene.On 13 September 2021, Mr Tang and Mr Leong received the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award from COL Anthony Toh, Commander 4th SCDF Division, in an award presentation ceremony. It was also attended by Mr Sng Hock Lin, Chief ActiveSG. Thank you Mr Tang, Mr Leong and the Good Samaritan for saving a life! SCDF would appreciate if the unknown Good Samaritan could reach out to us so that we can duly recognise his good deed. To know more on what to do in such emergencies, join the online module of the SCDF's Community Emergency Prepardness Programme at or contact one of the four SCDF Division HQs to register for a practical class. ANationOfLifesavers OurCFRsOurHeroes

The key mid-year statistics for SCDF Emergency Medical Services (EMS) and Fire Incidents for the first half 2021 were released earlier this week.In summary:1 While the total number of ambulance calls increased by 1.4% compared to the first half of 2020, there was a significant decrease of 15.4% and 16.4% in the number of non-emergency calls and false alarm calls respectively. 2 The number of fire calls fell by 0.6% from the first half of 2020. Fires that occurred in residential premises decreased by 2.7%. Fires involving cooking activities was the leading cause of fires in residential premises.3 The number of fires involving Personal Mobility Devices (PMDs) and Power Assisted Bicycles (PABs) saw a significant decrease of 32.6% from the first half of 2020. On Saturday, 17 July 2021, Mr Samuel Tan was at Palawan Beach, for a casual outing when he was alerted to cries for help. Springing into action from his instinct as a Volunteer Special Constabulary (VSC) police officer, Mr Samuel alerted a nearby lifeguard station and ran swiftly towards the distress call. He found an unconscious child on the beach. Recalling his CPR-AED skills acquired during his days with , Mr Samuel, with the help from the Sentosa lifeguards, conducted CPR-AED on the child. The child was successfully revived before the arrival of the SCDF ambulance. For his valiant and exemplary lifesaving deed, Mr Samuel was presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award on 8 September 2021 by COL Shaiful Herman Bin Shali, Commander 1st SCDF Division. Thank you Mr Samuel and the Sentosa lifeguards for saving a precious life. To know more on what to do during emergencies, join the online module of the SCDF's Community Emergency Prepardness Programme at or contact one of the four SCDF Division HQs to register for a practical class. [SCDF Celebrates Teachers' Day]To teach is to touch a life forever.Meet SWO1 Irianto Bin Marino and CPT Jadyn Toh Pei Xuan who are trainers at the Civil Defence Academy (CDA). With 7 and 2 years of experience as trainers respectively, this duo are familiar faces to multiple batches of SCDF trainees who have passed through the doors of CDA.What's interesting is that CPT Jadyn used to be a trainee under SWO1 Irianto! Recalling her days as a cadet during her Rota Commander's Course (RCC), CPT Jadyn describes SWO1 Irianto as a "firm" yet "fatherly" figure.Today, their work as fellow trainers at CDA allow them to cross path often, working together and exchanging ideas on the best approach to conduct classes for trainees.As we celebrate Teachers' Day today, we would like to recognise the hard work and dedication of all teachers and trainers. Trainers in SCDF play an important role of imparting valuable knowledge and skills to trainees, nurturing the next generation of life savers.Happy Teachers' Day!

[ Community Lifesavers on the Road] Earlier today, the SCDF-ComfortDelGro AED-on-Wheels programme was officially launched by Associate Professor Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State for Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development. The AED-on-Wheels programme equips vehicles on the move with an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) each to facilitate the quick delivery of an AED that can be used to restore the heartbeat of a cardiac arrest victim. 50 taxis and 10 MedCare minibuses from ComfortDelGro have been equipped with AEDs, sponsored by the . ComfortDelGro Corporation Limited has also equipped each of these vehicles with a fire extinguisher and a first aid kit. 60 ComfortDelGro drivers have been trained by SCDF in life saving skills on Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), basic firefighting and basic first aid as well as on the use of AED. These drivers will be alerted to cardiac arrest emergencies that occur within a 1.5 km radius of their vehicles location through the SCDF's myResponder app. Every second counts in a cardiac arrest emergency and SCDF warmly welcomes ComfortDelGro to the family of Community Lifesavers. ANationofLifesavers

Yesterday, SCDF participated in the Ferry Rescue Exercise (FEREX), an annual exercise conducted by . Two SCDF vessels from our Marine Division, namely the Rapid Response Fire Vessel (RFV) and Heavy Rescue Vessel (HRV) were involved in the exercise which aims to test the operational readiness of agencies and ferry operators. In this exercise scenario, the hull of a ferry carrying several passengers was damaged in an accident, causing the ferry to sink rapidly. As part of joint agency support, our RFV went alongside the stricken ferry to simulate casualty transfer and evacuation of passengers. Meanwhile, on the HRV's heli-winch pad, SCDF's Marine specialists and the Republic of Singapore Air Force (RSAF) Super Puma helicopter worked together to airlift a 'critically injured' passenger. This afternoon at , Mr Masagos Zulkifli, Minister for Social and Family Development, Second Minister for Health, and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs, Member of Parliament for Tampines GRC, presented the SCDF Community First Responder Award (CFRA) to three members of the public who had assisted in the initial firefighting efforts during a coffeeshop fire at Block 823A Tampines Street 81 on 7 August 2021. Mr Molla Sowkat, worker, was in the vicinity when he saw a lot of smoke and instinctively ran towards it. He pulled out a nearby fire hosereel to douse the fire. A few minutes later, Mr Muhammad Raiz Bin Abdul Razak, motion graphics designer and Mr Mohamed Fariq Bin Abbas, a SCDF Operationally Ready National Serviceman, joined Mr Sowkat. In the face of intense heat and billowing smoke, the brave and determined trio took turns in using the hosereel to fight the fire. Thank you Mr Sowkat, Mr Raiz and Mr Fariq for being exemplary Community First Responders! You too can learn what do during a fire, including how to use a fire extinguisher and a hosereel, via our Community Emergency Prepardness Programme (CEPP) e-modules online at Alternatively, you could contact one of the four SCDF Division HQs to register for a hands-on CEPP class. [Decommissioning of SCDF's pioneer vessels]When SCDF took over the marine firefighting and rescue functions from Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) on 1 April 2012, we also took over the operation of two Marine Fire Vessels (MFVs). These two vessels were refurbished and renamed as Firefighter 1 and Firefighter 2, and have been through thick and thin with our marine personnel right from the start. Deployed in numerous firefighting and rescue incidents, standby as well as exercises, these MFVs played an instrumental role in the formative years of SCDF Marine Division.Right before sunset on 3rd August 2021, Firefighter 1 and Firefighter 2 were officially decommissioned in a ceremony. This is the first time that SCDF has held a decommissioning ceremony for our vessels and it was attended by a contingent from Marine Division and fire stations. Against the setting sun, the blue ensign flags from the two MFVs were lowered to symbolise the halt to their operation. It was a formal and solemn ceremony, befitting the retirement of our pioneer vessels.The decommissioning ceremony was followed by a send-off on 4th August 2021. The send-off included a water salute for the MFVs as they passed through the channel, with marine personnel waving their final goodbyes. The decommissioning and send-off of these MFVs mark a bittersweet moment for us. While we are sad to bid goodbye to our pioneer vessels, we are glad to know that their legacy have led to a new generation of state-of-the-art firefighting and rescue vessels, which stand ready to continue to keep Singapore waters in safe hands.

The Lunar Seventh Month or Hungry Ghost Festival is coming up in a few days. Do exercise caution when conducting religious activities like the burning of joss sticks and incense papers. Here are some fire safety tips to minimise any potential hazards during this period. Remember, fire safety is our collective responsibility!

[Fire @ 70 West Coast Ferry Road] At about 4.40pm today, SCDF responded to a fire at the aforementioned address. The fire involved a berthed tugboat. Eight persons on the tugboat had evacuated before SCDF's arrival. Upon SCDFs arrival, smoke was seen coming from the tugboat. SCDF firefighters from Clementi Fire Station and West Coast Marine Fire Station donned breathing apparatus sets and boarded the tugboat. They located the seat of the fire in the engine room. A water jet was quickly set up to conduct firefighting operations and a key consideration was not to apply too much water that could affect the stability of the tugboat. The fire was extinguished within 20 minutes of SCDF's arrival. SCDF ambulances conveyed eight persons to Singapore General Hospital for smoke inhalation and burn injuries.

[Fire @ Block 295C Compassvale Crescent] At about 2.50pm today, SCDF responded to a fire at the aforementioned address. The fire involved the contents of a living room of a unit on the sixth floor. Two occupants from the affected unit had evacuated prior to SCDF's arrival. Upon SCDF's arrival, dense black smoke was seen coming out of the affected unit. Firefighters wearing breathing apparatus sets extinguished the fire with a water jet.The entire unit was damaged by heat and smoke. About 30 residents of the affected block were evacuated by the Police as a precautionary measure. SCDF assessed the two occupants from the affected unit and one of them was conveyed by an SCDF ambulance to Singapore General Hospital for smoke inhalation. Preliminary investigation into the cause of the fire indicates that it was of electrical origin, from a portable vehicle jumpstarter that was being charged at the time of the fire.

Yesterday, seven Good Samaritans were each presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award for their life saving actions in three separate incidents.On 30 May 2021, Mr Vincent Lim was exercising at Choa Chu Kang Stadium when he suffered a cardiac arrest. Mr Loy Kwong Choy witnessed the incident and rushed over to help. Sport Singapore Sports Champions, Mr Mohamad Noriman Bin Bahtiar, Mr Mohammad Azhar Bin Abdullah Sani and Mr Del Moro Dennis Ranido were alerted to the incident and responded as well. The team quickly alerted SCDF and performed CPR-AED. Mr Vincent was successfully revived before being conveyed to hospital by SCDF ambulance. Mr Vincent and his wife attended the award presentation ceremony yesterday and thanked the life savers. In the second incident on 26 March 2021, a man suffered from a cardiac arrest near Woodlands MRT Station. Mr Andrew Chua, the SMRT on-duty station manager witnessed the incident and rushed to help. Alerted through the SCDF myResponder app, Mr Sheh Yusof Bin Mohamed Shaus also responded. The duo performed CPR-AED on the victim and he subsequently regained his pulse and breathing before being conveyed to hospital by SCDF ambulance. The third incident occurred on 10 June 2021 at Block 283 Bukit Batok East Avenue 3. Mr Muhammad Nasiruddin Md Khalid noticed that his neighbours unit was on fire. Mr Nasiruddin, with a wet cloth covering his mouth, braved smoke and fire and charged into the burning unit to rescue an unconscious man out of the house. You too can learn CPR-AED skill in the SCDF's Community Emergency Prepardness (CEPP) e-modules online at Download the myResponder app and be a CommunityLifesaver today! ANationOfLifesavers

It's not everyday that you see one of our DART Rescue Vehicle (DRV) on the road.The DRV is a specialised vehicle of our elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART). Spanning almost 10m in length and weighing 9.5 tonnes, it is designed and equipped to respond to more complex missions involving either height, collapsed structure or underwater rescue operations. If you spot one of our iconic emergency vehicles along the road, do share your picture with us with the hashtag myscdf!:

[Fire @ Blk 395 Tampines Ave 7]At about 9.40am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the aforementioned address. Upon arrival, SCDF firefighters wearing breathing apparatus sets conducted forced entry into the smoke-logged unit on the 10th floor. SCDF rescued an occupant from the window of the affected unit. The fire, which involved a bedroom of the unit was extinguished with one water jet.About 40 residents from levels 9 to 12 of the affected block were evacuated by the Police as a precautionary measure. A resident from the 11th floor fell during evacuation and was conveyed to Sengkang General Hospital. The unit occupant who was rescued by SCDF firefighters was assessed by a paramedic and subsequently refused conveyance to the hospital. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

In times of emergency, would you know how to react? If your answer is no, why not consider joining our Community Emergency Preparedness Programme (CEPP). CEPP focuses on equiping participants with knowledge on core lifesaving skills and essential emergency procedures, so that you can help others during emergencies. The CEPP syllabus consists of 3 tiers: 'I am Safe' (Tier 1), 'Response Ready' (Tier 2) and 'Lifesaver' (Tier 3). Tier 1 and 2 are available online as e-modules, so you can learn them at your own convenience. Upon successful completion of the online module in Tier 2, you can then sign up for the practical lessons in Tier 2 and 3, which are held in person. Do make sure to complete the Tier 2 e-module before booking a Tier 2 practical lesson at the Division HQ closest to you!Find out more about CEPP at: TogetherANationOfLifesaversTheLifeSavingForceCommunityFirstResponder

[SCDF conducts workshop on Urban Search and Rescue for international participants]Recently, SCDF, with support from the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (UNOCHA), conducted a workshop on the International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) Guidelines 2020 for the Asia Pacific (AP) region.The virtual event was attended by about 120 international participants from the INSARAG Network, including government officials and national civil defence organisations. The opening remarks were delivered by SCDFs Deputy Commissioner (Ops and Resilience), DC Anwar Abdullah, and the INSARAG AP Regional Chair 2021 from BASARNAS Indonesia, Mr Barokna Haulah. During the three-hour session, SCDF speakers introduced participants to the INSARAG community, its systems, and fundamentals of the latest Guidelines - a set of internationally accepted documents that outline the methodology for countries to develop their national urban search and rescue (USAR) response capability. The Guidelines also outline the requirements and standards for international USAR teams to respond to affected countries.The speakers also provided advice on developing a countrys national emergency management framework, which would allow them to better respond to disasters. The workshop concluded with a robust exchange of views during a Q&A session, where participants gleaned a deeper understanding on the practical applications of the Guidelines.We look forward to our continued partnership with the INSARAG network and stand ever ready to contribute to the international Search and Rescue community.

[23rd Rota Commander Course (RCC) Commissioning Ceremony]This morning, 41 officer cadets from the 23rd Rota Commander Course (RCC) were commissioned as SCDF Senior Officers in a ceremony held at the Civil Defence Academy. At the closed-door ceremony due to the ongoing COVID-19 situation, family members and invited guests were able to tune into a live video broadcast of the ceremony to bear witness to this proud moment of their loved ones.The RCC commissioning ceremony is a significant milestone that marks the transition of officer cadets into Senior Officers after 28 weeks of rigorous training. As Senior Officers, these 15 career officers and 26 full-time national servicemen will be leading a team to respond to a wide multitude of firefighting and rescue incidents.In a virtual speech delivered by Mr. Desmond Tan, Minister of State (MOS) for Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment, he reiterated that while the COVID-19 pandemic has changed the way we go about our lives, SCDFs core function of firefighting, rescue and emergency medical services remain unchanged. He acknowledged that SCDF has employed new technologies in transforming its operations and emphasized the need to continue to do so, in order to remain effective and efficient.Congratulations to our newly commissioned SCDF Senior Officers! We wish them all the best as they go forth in their journey with the Life Saving Force. [Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, Safe Management Measures (SMM) were observed at the event to ensure the safety of all attendees.]ANationofLifesavers

At the closed-door ceremony due to the ongoing COVID-19 situation, family members and invited guests were able to tune into a live video broadcast of the ceremony to bear witness to this proud moment of their loved ones.The RCC commissioning ceremony is a significant milestone that marks the transition of officer cadets into Senior Officers after 28 weeks of rigorous training. As Senior Officers, these 15 career officers and 26 full-time national servicemen will be leading a team to respond to a wide multitude of firefighting and rescue incidents.In a virtual speech delivered by Mr. Desmond Tan, Minister of State (MOS) for Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment, he reiterated that while the COVID-19 pandemic has changed the way we go about our lives, SCDFs core function of firefighting, rescue and emergency medical services remain unchanged. He acknowledged that SCDF has employed new technologies in transforming its operations and emphasized the need to continue to do so, in order to remain effective and efficient.Congratulations to our newly commissioned SCDF Senior Officers! We wish them all the best as they go forth in their journey with the Life Saving Force. [Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, Safe Management Measures (SMM) were observed at the event to ensure the safety of all attendees.]ANationofLifesavers

[SCDF X IBM Lifesavers' Innovation Challenge: Call for Code 2021 - Grand Finals] Yesterday, the Grand Finals of the SCDF X IBM Lifesavers' Innovation Challenge: Call for Code 2021, in partnership with Accenture, took place at the Marina Bay Sands Convention Centre. This annual event encourages members of the public to innovate solutions to tackle various issues relating to emergency response and civil defence in Singapore. This year, close to 225 students from local tertiary institutions formed teams to participate in the challenge. Before yesterdays event, teams were tasked to submit a 1-minute video pitch along with a code sequence to address one of the problem statements on a Post-Pandemic society, Sustainable Development, and Climate Change. Six teams eventually made it to todays Grand Finals. The six teams had to pitch their ideas to a panel of judges comprising SCDFs Deputy Commissioner (DC) Teong How Hwa, DC, Future Technology & Public Safety; Tan Jee Toon, Director of IBM Partner Ecosystem Leader (ASEAN); and Cade Tan, Applied Innovation & Ventures Lead (Accenture Southeast Asia). Congratulations to team 'Seviours' for emerging as this years champion! They have been awarded a cash prize of S$10,000 for their winning idea of a system that leverages Internet-of-Things (IoT) sensors, Artifical Intelligence (AI), and automation to enable early and efficient response to high-voltage charging fires. Four other teams were awarded a total cash prize of S$11,000. Each of the top five teams was also awarded up to US$120,000 in IBM cloud credits to develop their projects with IBM. A big thank you to all participants! As we head towards a decade of new frontiers, our civil defence, community resilience and emergency response will need to keep up with the times. Now more than ever, we need innovative solutions so that as ANationOfLifesavers, we are always ready to respond.[In light of the COVID-19 pandemic, Safe Management Measures (SMM) were observed at the event to ensure the safety of all attendees.]

[Fire @ Blk 123 Ang Mo Kio Avenue 6]Earlier today at about 9.40am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the aforementioned address. Upon arrival, SCDF firefighters wearing breathing apparatus sets proceeded to a unit on the 7th floor where the fire was raging. An occupant from the burning unit was seen at the 7th floor staircase landing and was safely evacuated by SCDF firefighters. The fire which involved the contents of the unit was extinguished with a water jet and two Compressed Air Foam (CAF) backpacks.About 130 residents from levels 5 to 9 of the affected block, were evacuated by the Police and SCDF as a precautionary measure. Staff and residents from the AWWA Nursing Home, located from levels 2 to 4, had self-evacuated prior to SCDFs arrival.A total of seven residents were conveyed to Singapore General Hospital, Khoo Teck Puat Hospital and National University Hospital for smoke inhalation and giddiness.The cause of the fire is under investigation.

[Road Traffic Accident after the junction of Toh Guan Road/Toh Guan Road East]At 10.15am, SCDF received a call for assistance for a road traffic accident involving a lorry and a van after the junction of Toh Guan Road and Toh Guan Road East. Emergency responders from Jurong and Clementi Fire Stations were dispatched to the scene. As a result of the accident, the lorrys cabin was crushed inwards, pinning the driver in the seat, with both his legs severely trapped at the floor area near the accelerator and brake pedals.The driver of the van had self-evacuated and was assessed by a paramedic before being conveyed to Ng Teng Fong General Hospital.Due to the intricacy of the rescue operation, rescuers from SCDF's elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) were also dispatched to the scene.Within the confined space in the lorry, DART rescuers manoeuvred delicately, using a slew of hydraulic rescue equipment to cut through the crushed cabin to access the trapped driver. A paramedic was also actively monitoring the drivers vital signs throughout the rescue operation. The entire rescue operation took almost an hour. The lorry driver was conscious throughout the operation and was conveyed to National University Hospital.

[Memorandum of Understanding between SCDF, SAF and NYP] Earlier today, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF), Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) and Nanyang Polytechnic (NYP) was signed. The signing ceremony was held virtually over Zoom and witnessed by COMR Eric Yap, Commissioner SCDF, Major-General Goh Si Hou, Chief of Army and Ms Jeanne Liew, Principal & Chief Executive Officer of NYP.The MoU provides the framework for the enhancement of the professional standards of paramedics, including SCDF paramedics and SAF Military Medical Experts, through a new 12-month Diploma (Conversion) in Paramedic Science and 1200 hours On-The-Job Training Programme (OTP). The diploma provides graduates with strong theoretical foundations and real-world experience essential for frontline paramedics in dealing with increasingly complex pre-hospital health emergencies that require diagnosis and prioritisation of treatment for patients. The OTP will be led by SCDF's National Emergency Medical Services Training Centre for graduates to gain essential hands-on opportunities in real-time emergency ambulance operations under the supervision of senior SCDF paramedics. The MoU was signed by Assistant Commissioner (AC) Yong Meng Wah, Director Emergency Medical Services Department, Chief Army Medical Officer Colonel (COL) (Dr) Lee Wei Ting and Director of NYP's School of Health and Social Sciences Dr Bryan Chua. On the training of a new generation of paramedics, AC Yong said, "This collaboration has allowed us to bring our national pre-hospital emergency care to a level that meets or even surpasses most international standards for quality patient care. I am glad we are levelling up the foundational knowledge and proficiency of the new generation of paramedics and further raising the overall standards of SCDF paramedics."Top (Witnesses): Chief of Army Major-General Goh Si Hou from the SAF, Commissioner Eric Yap from the SCDF and Principal & Chief Executive Officer Ms Jeanne Liew from NYP.Bottom (Signatories): COL (Dr) Lee Wei Ting from the SAF, AC Yong Meng Wah from the SCDF and Dr Bryan Chua from NYP.

"We're really glad that we were able to save him." Ms Sunitha, SCDF Community Lifesaver Award recipient. Yesterday, a husband and wife were commended by SCDF for saving the life of a cardiac arrest patient. On 18 March 2021 at about 6.00pm, Ms Sunitha Palanidurai, an off-duty senior respiratory therapist from Alexandra Hospital, was out for a walk with her husband, Mr Balaji Thangavelu, when they noticed an elderly man being supported by his friend at a nearby multi-purpose hall. The couple approached and realised that the elderly man was in cardiac arrest with no pulse or breathing. They immediately placed him on the floor, conducted Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and asked passersby to retrieve an Automated External Defibrillator (AED). The elderly man regained his pulse and breathing before the arrival of the SCDFs emergency medical services. For their timely actions, Ms Sunitha and Mr Balaji were awarded the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award, presented by COL Anthony Toh, Commander 4th SCDF Division. Ms Sunitha had learnt the CPR-AED skill in her medical training while Mr Balaji had learnt it as part of his training in the maritime industry. You too can learn CPR-AED skill in SCDF's Community Emergency Prepardness (CEPP) e-modules online at Together ANationOfLifesavers

They immediately placed him on the floor, conducted Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and asked passersby to retrieve an Automated External Defibrillator (AED). The elderly man regained his pulse and breathing before the arrival of the SCDFs emergency medical services. For their timely actions, Ms Sunitha and Mr Balaji were awarded the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award, presented by COL Anthony Toh, Commander 4th SCDF Division. Ms Sunitha had learnt the CPR-AED skill in her medical training while Mr Balaji had learnt it as part of his training in the maritime industry. You too can learn CPR-AED skill in SCDF's Community Emergency Prepardness (CEPP) e-modules online at Together ANationOfLifesavers

Our Fire Stations are manned 24/7 round-the-clock.Can you guess which Fire Station is this? 3 hints below!1 The slide was first implemented at this station. Replacing the historic sliding pole, the slide provides our frontline officers improved safety as they proceed to the emergency vehicles to respond to incidents.2 This station moved to its current location in November 2017.3 It is also known as Station 41. (BONUS: Do you know what '41' stands for?): .jpg

Do you know that Central Fire Station is the oldest existing fire station? Formerly known as Hill Street Fire Station, construction of the red-and-white brick building was completed in 1909. This distinctive architectural style was popular during the Edwardian era (1901-1910). Another key feature of the fire station is its lookout tower, which was the tallest tower in Singapore until the 1930s. Standing at approximately 34 metres, a fireman was always stationed in the lookout tower to spot fires. Upon spotting a fire, the fireman would relay the location to his colleagues on the ground through a long iron pipe which ran from the top of the watchtower to the base. Central Fire Station was gazetted as a national monument by the Preservation of Monuments Board on 18 December 1998. Today, it remains as an active fire station where SCDF emergency responders are on standby round-the-clock, ready to respond to emergencies..:

[ ]Today, 312 SCDF Operationally Ready National Servicemen (ORNS) from 41B Rescue Battalion (RBn)/4th SCDF Division, took part in Exercise Rambo at the Home Team Tactical Centre (HTTC).Ex Rambo is a series of simulated scenarios designed to rigorously test and evaluate a RBns competencies in handling large-scale and prolonged urban search and rescue (USAR) operations. The 8-hour exercise involved ORNSmen comprising rescuers, medical and service support personnel. The battalion is required to conduct USAR operations in collapsed structures based on the requirements of the United Nation's International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG). They were tested on their ability to perform cutting, breaking, and lifting operations, and being able to medically treat victims at the incident site.Even amid the COVID-19 pandemic, such exercises are crucial in ensuring the operational readiness of our ORNSmen to respond to major emergencies. To ensure the safety of the personnel throughout the exercise, several safe management measures (SMM) were implemented. This exercise capped off a week of preparation during their annual In-Camp Training (ICT). Each ORNSman sacrificed his personal time to ensure the success of the exercise and we thank them for standing ever ready to protect and save lives and property as part of the Life Saving Force.

[Lifesavers on the move]On 28 Jan, the SCDF-Grab AED-on-Wheels programme was officially launched by Associate Professor Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development.50 Grab private hire vehicles are now equipped with AEDs for cardiac arrest cases. They are also equipped with first aid kits and fire extinguishers for other emergencies.To prepare Grab driver-partners for their new lifesaving role, SCDF trained 64 of them on how to perform CPR, apply first aid, and use a fire extinguisher.The AED-on-Wheels programme increases the availability of roving AEDs to facilitate its quick delivery to a cardiac arrest victim, thereby increasing the victims chances of survival. Drivers are alerted to such cases within a 1.5km radius of the vehicles location via SCDFs myResponder app.Grab is the third company to join the programme which was started in 2015. As of end-September 2020, drivers under the programme have arrived on scene for 158 cardiac arrest cases.We warmly welcome Grab and its driver-partners into our lifesaving family!ANationOfLifesavers

[EX YELLOWSTORM]Earlier this morning, SCDF conducted an exerciseat Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1. The exercise involved two simultaneous scenarios: a fire incident involving a vehicle transporting Hazardous Material (HazMat) and a HazMat incident involving a leak from a chlorine cylinder.Upon notification of the incident, members of the Company Emergency Response Team (CERT) commenced snatch rescue of casualties, initiated firefighting operation and called SCDF for assistance.Upon arrival, SCDF firefighters from Tampines Fire Station and other supporting stations worked together with the CERT members to prevent the fire from escalating, and concurrently carried out rescue and evacuation operations. SCDF's HazMat specialists were also involved in mitigating the leak of harmful chemicals.About 120 SCDF personnel comprising career officers and full-time National Servicemen from the fire stations, HazMat unit and Special Rescue unit were involved in the exercise.Through such exercises, SCDF responders are able to take part in realistic scenario-based training to sharpen their operational knowledge and skills. These exercises also enhance our familiarity with the operating terrain and its challenges as well as in validating the emergency plans of the industrial premises.ANationofLifesavers

Earlier today, six officers from SCDFs elite Disaster Assistance & Rescue Team (DART) were awarded the Public Spiritedness Award by . Their bold and decisive actions assisted the Police in the arrest of a man for a case of Outrage of Modesty.On 31 March 2020 at about 6.20am, six SCDF DART officers were having their routine training run along Mountbatten Road when they noticed a commotion at a bus stop and a man running away.Upon investigation, the DART officers were notified by a bus captain that it was a case of Outrage of Modesty.Five of the DART officers immediately chased after the man while one SCDF officer remained behind to provide assurance to the victim. The pursuit lasted about 600m and the officers detained the man until Police's arrival.Ive caught up to the suspect after 300m. However, I conducted an appreciation of the situation and decided to trip him at a grass patch ahead so as to prevent any serious injuries to him. SGT 3 Muhd Khalid Abdulah Sani.For their actions, WO1 Ngui Hook Siong, SGT3 Muhd KhalidAbdulah Sani, SGT3 Muhammad ShafiiRahmat, WO2 Sulaiman Ahmad, SSG Sharulizam Oshman and SSG Zamri Amran were awarded the Public Spiritedness Award by AC Julius Lim, Commander Bedok Division during a ceremony conducted at Bedok Police Division Headquarters.

[Workers commended for rescuing boy from ledge]You may have seen a recent viral video of a worker operating a boom lift to rescue a boy from a kitchen ledge. Today, SCDF awarded him and his colleague for their heroic act.On Sunday morning (3 Jan), Mr Das Dipto, a landscape maintenance worker, was cleaning a boom lift which he had used for pruning trees when an anxious woman approached him and his colleague, Mr Biswas Jibom. The woman pleaded for them to help a boy who was stranded on a third-floor kitchen ledge at a nearby HDB block 243, Hougang Street 22. With Mr Jibom directing him and ensuring the path ahead was clear, Mr Dipto carefully steered the machinery with the boom lift down a narrow pathtowards the block. He saw the frightful boy precariously standing on the ledge, crying and grabbing onto a laundry pole. Mr Dipto raised the boom lifts platform towards the boy while calmly assuring the boy that he was there to rescue him. Within minutes, Mr Dipto reached out with both his arms, lifted the boy onto the platform and lowered him to safety, much to the relief and rousing cheers from a crowd of onlookers.When SCDF resources arrived, the boy had already been rescued. He was assessed by an SCDF paramedic and he did not require any medical assistance.Today, for their quick-thinking and selfless act, Mr Dipto and Mr Jibom received SCDF's Community Lifesaver Award from COL Lim Han Chee, 3rd SCDF Division Commander.Thank you Mr Dipto and Mr Jibom! Your commendable act brings us closer to building ANationOfLifesavers.

[Workers commended for rescuing boy from ledge]You may have seen a recent viral video of a worker operating a boom lift to rescue a boy from a kitchen ledge. Today, SCDF awarded him and his colleague for their heroic act.On Sunday morning (3 Jan), Mr Das Dipto, a landscape maintenance worker, was cleaning a boom lift which he had used for pruning trees when an anxious woman approached him and his colleague, Mr Biswas Jibom. The woman pleaded for them to help a boy who was stranded on a third-floor kitchen ledge at a nearby HDB block 243, Hougang Street 22. With Mr Jibom directing him and ensuring the path ahead was clear, Mr Dipto carefully steered the machinery with the boom lift down a narrow pathtowards the block. He saw the frightful boy precariously standing on the ledge, crying and grabbing onto a laundry pole. Mr Dipto raised the boom lifts platform towards the boy while calmly assuring the boy that he was there to rescue him. Within minutes, Mr Dipto reached out with both his arms, lifted the boy onto the platform and lowered him to safety, much to the relief and rousing cheers from a crowd of onlookers.When SCDF resources arrived, the boy had already been rescued. He was assessed by an SCDF paramedic and he did not require any medical assistance.Today, for their quick-thinking and selfless act, Mr Dipto and Mr Jibom received SCDF's Community Lifesaver Award from COL Lim Han Chee, 3rd SCDF Division Commander.Thank you Mr Dipto and Mr Jibom! Your commendable act brings us closer to building ANationOfLifesavers.

On 27 September, a man was found unconscious near Boon Lay MRT station. Suspecting that the man had suffered a cardiac arrest, four Community First Responders (CFRs) responded swiftly and worked together to save the man. Off-duty nurse from National University Hospital (NUH), Ms. Franchesca Santos Rubio, was alerted of the incident via the myResponder app and rushed to the location from her home. She immediately performed one cycle of CPR on the man. Two SMRT staff, Mr. Muhammad Azhari bin Abdullah and Mdm. Hilmiah Binte Ahmad also assisted by bringing an AED and placing the pads on the man. Mdm. Hilmiah subsequently administered three AED shocks.SMRTs Mr. Baharudin Bin Johan presence was also timely in helping to manage the crowd. This allowed the CFRs to have the working space needed to safely administer CPR and use the AED. All four CFRs remained by the mans side until the arrival of SCDFs emergency medical services.On Monday, for their gallant efforts in helping to save a life, Ms. Franchesca and Mdm. Hilmiah were awarded with the Community Lifesaver Award while Mr. Muhammad Azhari and Mr. Baharudin were awarded with the Community First Responder Award.Download the myResponder app and be a CommunityFirstResponder today!ANationOfLifesavers

Happy International Volunteer Day! On this special day, we honour those from our various volunteer schemes the National Civil Defence Cadet Corps (NCDCC), the Civil Defence Auxiliary Unit (CDAU), and the Civil Defence (CD) Lionhearters Clubs. And of course, the members of the public who have stepped forward as Community First Responders (CFRs) in times of need.Pandemic or not, our volunteers continue to serve their calling and come forth as CFRs to render assistance to those in distress, bringing Singapore closer to being a Nation of Lifesavers.Thank you all for your selflessness and dedication!

[ ]Since SCDF took over marine firefighting operations in April 2012, SCDFs Marine Division has been growing steadily both in terms of capacity building and infrastructural development. In a short span of eight years, SCDFs Marine Division has grown from two firefighting vessels and a single marine fire station @ West Coast, to establishing a Marine Division Headquarters and a marine fire station @ Brani, a marine fire post @ Loyang and @ Gul. The Marine Division also acquired new, multi-purposed vessels, which can carry out prolonged and complex firefighting and rescue operations, including responding to a Chemical, Biological and Radiological incident at sea.To date, SCDFs Marine Fire Stations have responded to a number of fire and rescue operations, such as the Jalan Samulun fire in 2013 that resulted from an explosion on-board a tugboat where SCDF rescued four casualties; and in July 2018, SCDF marine firefighting resources battled a fire in the upper decks of the superstructure of a container ship in a 5-hour long firefighting operation. More recently on 13th November 2020, SCDFs Heavy Rescue Vessel and Rapid Response Fire Vessel were dispatched to rescue a man who had fallen down a hatch onboard a container vessel and had sustained a serious leg injury.The establishment and growth of the Marine Division was made possible, thanks to the dedicated officers of the Marine Division, led by Marine Commander, Assistant Commissioner (AC) Derek Tan. Today, the helm of SCDFs marine capabilities was handed over to Colonel (COL) Ryan Ong, the newly appointed Marine Commander, who was previously the Deputy Commander of the Marine Division.AC Derek Tan will assume his new appointment as Director Fire Safety Department.With Singapore as one of the worlds busiest ports, SCDF will keep innovating and enhancing our marine capabilities and continuously upgrade the skillsets of our marine officers to ensure prompt and effective emergency response to incidents within Singapores territorial waters.

Fair warning, this post may induce cuteness overload but please 995ForEmergenciesOnlyHave you seen our adorable furry friends interacting with firefighting hoses at theSingapore Zoo,Jurong Bird Parkor River safari?As part of the Lifesaving Forces efforts to contribute to environmental sustainability, we recently donated more than 90 firefighting hoses to WRS. This is the second time that we had donated old hoses to WRS in support of the global effort to go green. Sharp-eyed visitors may have seensome of the animals trying to solve puzzle feedersor snoozing with familiar-looking hoses.The hoses are made of materials that are durable and safe for the animals.It can withstand the strong teeth of hyenas and the sharp talons of eagles.The hoses will be re-purposed with tender loving care by the WRSanimalcareteams for housing enhancements and enrichment devices to keep the animals physically and mentally stimulated.Swipe to see just how much the animals love their new toys! Photos 1 to 6 courtesy of WRS.

[Marine Rescue Operation @ Southeast of Singapore]At 12.30pm yesterday, SCDF received a call for medical assistance from an anchored container vessel in the southeast of Singapore. A man had fallen down a hatch onboard the container vessel and sustained a serious leg injury. Two SCDF marine vessels were deployed to the incident. Arriving alongside the container vessel, two SCDF marine specialists who are cross-trained as Emergency Medical Technicians quickly boarded the vessel with their rescue and medical equipment to assess the situation. A man was found conscious but immobile at the container vessels medical bay. As this was a case of fall, the SCDF marine specialists proceeded with great caution in handling the casualty and carefully secured him onto a stretcher. Concurrently, officers from SCDFs Heavy Rescue Vessel (HRV) boarded the container vessel to set up a lowering system of ropes and pulleys between the two vessels. This is an intricate rescue cum evacuation operation in view of the waves and windy condition out at sea. The casualty was safely lowered to the HRV's deck.He was then swiftly ferried to Marina South Pier where an SCDF emergency ambulance had been on standby to receive him. After a further medical assessment by the ambulance crew, he was conveyed to the Singapore General Hospital.

The casualty was safely lowered to the HRV's deck.He was then swiftly ferried to Marina South Pier where an SCDF emergency ambulance had been on standby to receive him. After a further medical assessment by the ambulance crew, he was conveyed to the Singapore General Hospital.

Fire Safety Tips for Use of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) cylindersat HomeAs we stay home during this period, some of us may be cooking our own meals. However, do be careful as aflash fire could occur while cooking and this could damage property, cause injuries and even fatalities..In March and April this year, there were 7 cases of flash fires involving LPG cylindersin residential homes. As a result of these fires, 7 persons suffered injuries..If you fail to ignite the gas stove after several attempts:.1) do not continue to ignite the stove; .2) switch off the gas valve; .3) ventilate the kitchen by opening all doors and windows before attempting to re-ignite the stove..See the infographics below for more fire safety tips on the proper storage and usage of LPG cylinders at home.

What began as a usual bus ride home for a student ended with her saving a womans life.Diniy Qurratuaini, a National Civil Defence Cadet Corps (NCDCC) cadet from Temasek Secondary School, was on her way home when the bus she was on collided into a pedestrian, knocking her unconscious. Without hesitation, Diniy instructed a fellow passenger to call 995 before she rushed down to attend to the collapsed woman.After assessing that the woman was not breathing and had no pulse, Diniy immediately performed CPR on her. After a few cycles of CPR, the woman regained consciousness. Diniy stayed by her side until SCDF emergency responders arrived to render further medical assistance.Diniys quick-thinking and selfless act showed that age is no barrier to saving lives. I continued my journey home and told my parents about the incident. Only then did I realise the magnitude of the situation. Im glad I was there to render help and I am thankful to NCDCC for teaching me skills I can use in such life-threatening emergencies - Diniy Qurratuaini

SCDF participated in the Ferry Rescue Exercise (FEREX), an annual exercise organised by the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore.Over 350 personnel from 10 agencies and companies participated in the exercise, designed to test and validate a multi-agency response to a ferry mishap incident within Singapore waters.This years FEREX saw two of our newly commissioned vessels in action. On the Heavy Rescue Vessels heli-winch pad, SCDF marine firefighters and a helicopter crew from the Republic of Singapore Air Force worked together to airlift a severely injured casualty. The Marine Rescue Vessel was deployed to evacuate passengers from the stricken ferry.Check out some of the highlights from the exercise!

The SCDF Marine Command welcomed the latest addition to its fleet - a Heavy Rescue Vessel (HRV), the 'Red Manta'. The launching ceremony was officiated by Comr Eric Yap, Commissioner SCDF.This formidable vessel is able to evacuate up to 300 casualties, and is equipped with 12 shower cubicles that allow for the mass decontamination of casualties affected by hazardous materials.It is also the first Catamaran (twin-hulled) vessel in Marine Command which offers higher stability during vessel-to-vessel transfer operations. An innovative lift system allows casualties from the main deck to be brought to the heli-winch pad above, where critically injured persons can be airlifted to hospitals.With Singapore as the top maritime capital in the world for the past three years and with one of the world's busiest ports, the newly launched HRV further enhances SCDF's marine capabilities in ensuring prompt and effective emergency response to incidents within Singapore's territorial waters.

The SCDF Marine Command witnessed the launch of its third Rapid Response Fire Vessel (RFV2.0), the 'White Swordfish'. The launching ceremony was officiated by Commissioner Eric Yap, Commissioner SCDF.-The RFV is apurpose-built vessel designed entirely by the Marine Command.Equipped with water jet propulsion, the vessel can reach speeds of more than 40 knots and, powerful firefighting monitors enable the RFV to provide effective response to ship fires.-Compared to the fleet's first twoRFVs, the RFV2.0 'White Swordfish'has an enhanced rescue capability for shallow waters. Its innovative Launch and Recovery System (LARS)allows the crew to quickly deploy an inflatable rescue boat in beaches and reefs less than one meter in depth.-The vessel will be deployed to the upcoming Punggol marine outpost, where it will serve the northern waters of Singapore which is generally shallower.-The launch of the 'White Swordfish' signifies the constant evolution of SCDF's marine firefighting and rescue capabilities.
