On 21 April 2018, a fire broke out at Htein Bin landfill in Hlaing Thaya Township in Yangon, Myanmar. Fumes from the fire had spread to nearby township and poses a health risk to people living in these areas.This afternoon, LTC Firoz Ramjan and MAJ Kenneth Mak were deployed to Myanmar as part of an ASEAN Emergency Response and Assessment Team(ERAT), under the auspices of the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on disaster management (AHA Centre).Theprimary function of the ASEAN-ERAT is to provide rapid assessment and determine the critical resources required for the areas affected by the fire and fumes.

The Home Team Diploma and ITE Sponsorship Awards Ceremony was held on Saturday, 21 April, at the Ministry of Home Affairs Headquarters at New Phoenix Park. The ceremony was officiated by Mrs. Josephine Teo, Second Minister for Home Affairs. Eight students received the SCDF sponsorships at the Home Team Diploma and ITE Sponsorship Ceremony 2018. Of the eight recipients, two are no strangers to the SCDF. Their elder siblings, MAJ Zulkifli Abdullah and SSG Rasheedh Ibrahim, have been the source of inspiration for them to join the family of The Life Saving Force. We wish our recipients all the best in their studies and look forward to them joining us upon graduation!ANationofLifesavers

The SCDF Workplan Seminar 2018 was held today at Singapore University of Technology and Design. The venue was befitting as the event showcased several forward-looking projects that are poised to push the technological boundaries of SCDFs emergency response.Some of the highlights include the HazMat Control Vehicle, DART Rescue Vehicle, 6th Generation Red Rhino and the Red Rhino Robot or 3R.At the event, Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law announced that a Singapore Government Scholarship for paramedics will be rolled out later this year. This allows the scholarship recipients to read para-medicine or related disciplines such as emergency health in overseas universities, thus developing leaders with clinical expertise attuned to SCDFs operational needs.ANationofLifesavers

My sense of duty is not confined to whether I am in uniform or whether I am at work. When peoples lives are at risk, it is my responsibility to help. Im glad the fire managed to be extinguished before it could cause greater damage. And I wish a speedy recovery to the uncle who suffered smoke inhalation.-As reported yesterday, off-duty SCDF officer, SSG Yahafiz was first at scene to mitigate a fire in a unit at Block 103 Lor 1 Toa Payoh. He quickly extinguished the fire which involved a Personal Mobility Device (PMD) with a fire extinguisher, after kicking the front door open. You have done us proud!-ANationofLifesavers

After watching a series of Ultimate Fighting Championship matches on television, CPL (NS) Ahmad Syahyi Bin Mohd Amin picked up Brazilian Jiu Jitsu as a sport. The myResponder mobile app alerts CommunityFirstResponders to cardiac arrest cases taking place within their immediate vicinity. In such an emergency where every second counts, CommunityFirstResponders play a crucial role in providing prompt medical assistance prior to the arrival of SCDF paramedics.. CPT Lee En Hao, who had just been commissioned as an SCDF officer early last week, recalled his experience in responding to a myResponder case while he was still an officer cadet. . "When I heard my phone buzzing from the myResponder alert, I immediately rushed to the scene. By then an EMT-Firebiker had arrived, so I assisted him in performing CPR.. As a Community First Responder, there are many ways you can help such as getting an AED or performing CPR in a cardiac arrest case. Your noble efforts will make a difference in someone's life.". On 5 October 1981, 94 NSFs were enlisted into the Construction Brigade, the first NS Vocation of the Civil Defence Command (predecessor of SCDF). NSmen were trained in building construction and repair work before being posted to Housing Development Board for their on-the-job training. By the end of their training, these NSFs were awarded with the Advanced Builders Certificate which aided them in transitioning into the construction industry. In November 2002, the Construction Brigade was decommissioned as the skills were no longer required in the local construction industry. ANationofLifesavers OurHomeOurTeam NS50

Following the earthquake in Aceh on 7 December 2016, LTC Ng Geok Meng and MAJ Koh Kim Hwee, Stuart have been deployed to Indonesia as part of a five-man ASEAN Emergency Response and Assessment Team (ERAT), under the auspices of the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on disaster management (AHA Centre). The ERATs primary function is to provide rapid assessment and determine the critical resources (e.g. tents, medical kits) required for the areas affected by the earthquake. The two SCDF officers are expected to be there for a week.

SCDF units go head-to-head, putting their skills to the test in a series of challenges involving firefighting, rescue, medical and HazMat scenarios. The team with the highest overall points will win the trophy! Who are you gunning for? Come on down to Singapore Expo Hall 2 and lend your support!

In the Public Challenge, participants from various groups of the public take part in challenges related to their areas of speciality. Members of the Community Emergency Response Teams, schools, Company Emergency Response Teams and the medical fraternity compete in their respective categories to claim the honour of being crowned the best in their field!

In the School Challenge, students from various NCDCC units as well as the CD Lionhearters will compete in an obstacle course comprising casualty rescue, firefighting and CPR/AED procedures. Proceeding to the final from yesterdays heats are 3 teams from NCDCC HQ and 2 CD Lionhearter teams from Nanyang Polytechnic and Nanyang Technological University. Lets cheer them on in the final which will at Singapore Expo Hall 2!

SCDF's 21st fire station, Sentosa Fire Station commenced operations at 8am this morning. Located at 37 Artillery Avenue, it will provide emergency services within the popular resort island of Sentosa as well as its immediate vicinity such as the HarbourFront and Telok Blangah areas. 30 years ago at 11:25 am, the area surrounding Lian Yak Building trembled as the structure collapsed to the ground. 50 people were trapped in the building which comprised a bank, nightclub and Hotel New World. Senior Warrant Officers Isnin, Salleh and Jimmy (from left to right) were some of the many rescuers deployed to ground zero. "When we arrived at the scene, we didn't expect to see the building which we were familiar with, on the ground like a stack of cards. We regained our composure and went straight to work - digging through the rubble trying to find a way to the people who were trapped underneath." ANationofLifesavers

This morning, 8 off-duty firefighters from Bukit Batok Fire Station were having breakfast in a food court at Causeway Point after their 24-hour shift when they saw excessive smoke emitting from one of the stalls. They went to the kitchen to take a look and were alerted by the staff that a stove had caught fire. The Regular officer and 7 National Servicemen immediately sprang into action as their lifesaving instincts took over. 2 of them evacuated the staff from the kitchen while the rest evacuated other members of public to safety. They extinguished the fire with a hose reel and fire extinguisher. Due to their quick thinking, the damage was confined to the kitchen stove and no one was injured. Gentlemen, you have done us proud!ANationofLifesavers everydayheroes

We have deployed our 5,000-litre *heli-bucket and a 6-man Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) led by team leader WO1 Ahmad Faizal bin Abdul Hanan to Sumatra to assist the Indonesian authorities in conducting aerial fire-fighting operations. The team will operate the heli-bucket with the assistance of an RSAF Chinook helicopter. *The heli-bucket is a water dispenser slung underneath a helicopter. Water is usually collected from any open source, such as a reservoir or sea. The water in the bucket is discharged at the base of the bucket, when the release button is activated.Photo: Commissioner Eric Yap at Sembawang Air Base sending off the SCDF officers .TheLifeSavingForce mySCDF

76 year old Mr Goh Min Juan was watching TV when he heard explosion sounds coming from another residential unit located upstairs. As he was dashing up the stairs to find out what had happened, he was greeted by the smell of smoke and a sight of raging fire outside his neighbour's house.Immediately, he dashed down the same flight of stairs and told his wife to help him fill the buckets that they have at home with water. As he wife went on to do so, he started running up and down the stairs with the buckets of water to put out the fire. "I saw small fire balls shooting out from the fire! Thirty years go, I was trained in civil defence skills and today, I am glad that I am able to apply it to save a life and property. I knew that I had to do something about it before the fire spreads into the unit where my 15 year old neighbour was trapped in. It took me about seven trips up and down the flight of stairs before I could finally extinguish the fire! Of course, I handed over the 'operation' to the SCDF Emergency Responders upon their arrival," said Mr Goh. Mr Goh received the SCDF Public Spiritedness Awards for his acts of bravery from LTC Wesley Ho, Head Operations Branch of 2nd SCDF Division this morning.76YearOldHERO!ANationofLifesavers

SCDF was alerted to a fire at 6 Fan Yoong Road at 2.58am. 5 Fire Engines, 3 Red Rhinos, 9 Supporting Vehicles, 1 Ambulance and 1 Unmanned Fire Fighting Machine were dispatched.The raging fire that involved a warehouse dealing with plastic materials, was about the size of a football field. About 60 firefighters were deployed and at the height of the operation where The Life Saving Force encircled the area with 12 water jets, use of foam and the Unmanned Firefighting Machine to fight the fire. The fire was brought under control within an hour and extinguished at about 7am. SCDF is currently carrying out damping down operations. mySCDF

The Unmanned Firefighting Machine deployed at fire .23 Tuas Avenue 11 yesterday.PHOTO:TODAY

[LATEST] Fire at no.23 Tuas View 11SCDF was alerted to a case of fire at the above mentioned location at 3.38pm. 8 Fire Engines, 2 Red Rhinos, 4 Supporting Vehicles, 1 Ambulance and 1 Unmanned Firefighting Machine were dispatched to the scene.Upon SCDF arrival, the fire was well alight at a warehouse and involved waste products. The size of the fire affected area is approximately 50m x 50m.The fire was extinguished at 6.40pm using water jets, with the application of foam at selected areas. RESCUE INCIDENT at ALEXANDRA RDAt 2.49pm, SCDF was alerted to a rescue incident at 378, Alexandra Road. 2 Fire Engines, 1 Red Rhino, 2 Firebikes, 1 ambulance and 3 supporting vehickles were dispatched to the incident site.Upon SCDFs arrival, a single-storey building (approx. 20m by 10m) fitted with a zinc roof had collapsed after a tree, approximately 15m in height and 3m in diameter, fell ontoit. As a result two casualties were trapped under the rubble. SCDF firefighters together with DART rescuers immediately commenced rescue operations after stabilising the fallen tree and the building structure. The search and rescue operation had to be conducted cautiously by delicately creating space within the collapsed structure using hydraulic cutting and lifting equipment. The first casualty was rescued in about 40mins while the second casualty, who was pinned under the concrete debris was extricated about 45mins later. SCDF paramedic as well as a medical team from Alexandra Hospital were at the location to render medical assistance to both casualties.The casualties were sent to the Alexandra Hospital bySCDF ambulance. The whole search and rescue operation took about 90mins.myscdf TheLifeSavingForce

Welcome to the Hose Tower Instagram Challenge! Hose towers are a significant piece of of structure in a Fire Station. At a height of 5-9 stories, hose towers were used as a lookout post in the past and also to hang wet hoses (hoses were were made of woven cotton linen yarns in the past and stayed wet after use. Hanging the hoses in hose towers ensured that all standing water were removed) . Today, through better technology, the hose tower are no longer used to dry hoses or as a look out post. The hose tower however remains a symbolic structure in all the fire stations in Singapore.Can you identify which fire station this hose tower belongs to? myscdf TheLifeSavingForce
